Call upon the Lord, and speak to the king concerning us, to deliver us from death.”
Ekegusii: Modekai akamoteebia amang’ana onsi amonyorete; boigo akamoteebia omobaro bwe chitaabu Hamani arire eira kobeeka ase ekungo y’omorwoti, ng’a Abayahudi bonsi baitwe basirigwe kegima.

English: So Hathach went in and told her all these words.
Ekegusii: Boigo Modekai akaa Hataki riruube ririikire amang’ana ’ogochika koria kwaruetwe Susa igoro y’ogosirigwa kw’Abayahudi, erinde orokie Esiteri na amoteebie amang’ana onsi, boigo amoteebie ng’a agende ase omorwoti komosorora na komosaba amaabera ase abanto baye.

English: Esther said to Hathach, “Go to Mordecai, and say,
Ekegusii: Inyora ase kwaruete, ere akamoteebia ekero kware koragera korwa ase okoboko kwane. Ase engencho Hamani oyio ore oyokabere ase okogamba orobeirie goetera ase omogambi erio tobekwe ase ogokwa,

English: ‘All the nations of the empire know that any man or woman who goes in to the king into the inner court without being called, that person must die, unless the king stretches out his golden sceptre; then he shall live. I haven’t been called to go into the king for thirty days.’”
Ekegusii: Saba Omonene erio okwane n’omorwoti ase engencho yaito na ototorie korwa ase amakweri!

English: So Hathach reported to Mordecai all the words of Esther.
Ekegusii: Hataki akagenda, agateebia Esiteri amang’ana onsi Modekai atebeete.

English: Then Mordecai said to Hathach, “Go, and say to her, ‘Esther, don’t say to yourself that you alone will escape in the kingdom, more than all the other Jews.
Ekegusii: Esiteri agakwana na Hataki, akamoteebia airane ase Modekai, amoteebie,

English: For if you keep quiet on this occasion, help and protection will come to the Jews from another place; but you and your father’s house will perish. Who knows if you have been made queen for this occasion?’”
Ekegusii: “Omonto onde bwensi, abe omosacha gose omokungu, oragende ase omorwoti ase egoora ime atarangeiri, goika aitwe akwe. Okwo n’ogochika. Abasomba bonsi b’omorwoti na abanto bonsi be chingongo chi’oborwoti mbamanyete amang’ana ayio. Enchera n’eyemo yoka y’ogotooreka: eraarente omorwoti abe okomoragera n’enyimbo yaye y’oborwoti eroisirie korwa ase etaabu, ebe ekemanyererio ng’a rirorio natigwe abe moyo. Korende bono tindarangerigwa kogenda ase omorwoti ase engaki y’omotienyi oyomo.”

English: And Esther sent the messenger who came to her to Mordecai, saying,
Ekegusii: Ekero Modekai atebetigwe amang’ana y’Esiteri,

English: “Go and assemble the Jews that are in Susa, and all of you fast for me. Don’t eat or drink for three days, night and day. My maidens and I will also fast. Then I will go in to the king contrary to the law, even if I must die.”
Ekegusii: akamotomera abanto nokoiraneria oko: “Tokaga ng’a ekiagera ore ase enyomba y’omorwoti aye notooreke kobua Abayahudi bande.

English: So Mordecai went and did all that Esther commanded him.
Ekegusii: Naki onye aye kogokira‐kiri kegima ase engaki eye, ogokonywa na ogotooreka nigo korache ase Abayahudi korwa ensemo ende, korende aye na abanto b’enyomba ya iso mosirigwe. Ande, ning’o omanyete gose nase engencho y’engaki buna eye kwabeire enting’ana y’omorwoti?”

English: He prayed to the Lord, making mention of all the works of the Lord.
Ekegusii: Naende Esiteri agatoma okoiraneria oko gochia ase Modekai ogoteeba:

English: He said, “Lord God, you are king ruling over all, for all things are in your power, and there is no one who can oppose you in your purpose to save Israel;
Ekegusii: “Genda osangererie Abayahudi bonsi bare aa Susa, erio mweng’ate ase engencho yane. Timoria gose konywa ase amatuko atato, omobaso na obotuko. Inche amo nabasoomba baane abaiseke ntweng’ate boigo. Nyuma y’ayio ningende ase omorwoti mamincha y’amachiiko; onye ngochia gosirigwa, insirigwe.”

English: for you have made the sky and the earth and every wonderful thing under the sky.
Ekegusii: Erio Modakai akagenda agakora buna Esiteri amochigete.

English: You are Lord of all, and there is no one who can resist you, Lord.
Ekegusii: Erio Modekai akagenda na goikerania ogochika gw’Esiteri.

English: You know all things. You know, Lord, that it is not in insolence, nor arrogance, nor love of glory, that I have done this, to refuse to bow down to the arrogant Haman.
Ekegusii: Ase okweinyoria emeremo emenene omomene akorete ere akagenda, agakora onsi buna Esiteri amochiigete. Omenene, Omonene, Omonguru Omworoti

English: For I would gladly have kissed the soles of his feet for the safety of Israel.
Ekegusii: kera ring’ana nigo rire inse y’okobua kwao, naende onde taiyo oranyare gotenena ase obosio bwao ase okwerwa kwao ase ogotooria Israeli. Naye gwakorire igoro na ense

English: But I have done this that I might not set the glory of man above the glory of God. I will not worship anyone except you, my Lord, and I will not do these things in arrogance.
Ekegusii: na ebikone bionsi bire inse y’erioba naye omonene bw’ense, na onde tari orakoamererie, aye omonene nigo omanyete amang’ana onsi

English: And now, O Lord God, the King, the God of Abraham, spare your people, for our enemies are planning our destruction, and they have desired to destroy your ancient inheritance.
Ekegusii: nomanyete, aye omonyene nonya n’obwerori, ogwesika gose ogwetakooria, gokambetereria gokora onsi ayio nakorete nkanga korambereria inse ase ogosasiima ase obosio bw’omerori Hamani nabo narenge konyara konyunyunta ebisanyi biamagoro aye n’omogooko ekero narenge koba nobomaene ase oborendi bw’Abaisraeli. Korende keria inche nakorire, nagekorire

English: Do not overlook your people, whom you have redeemed for yourself out of the land of Egypt.
Ekegusii: kobua kobeka obonene bwa mwanyabaanto bosio bw’obonene bwa Nyasae Omobui; tingomotung’amera onde bwensi otatiga asore aye bweka omonene ase ogokora boigo, tinkonyara gokora obwerori. Ase igo, aye Nyasae Omonene, Omobui

English: Listen to my prayer. Have mercy on your inheritance and turn our mourning into gladness, that we may live and sing praise to your name, O Lord. Don’t utterly destroy the mouth of those who praise you, O Lord.”
Ekegusii: omorwoti, Omonene o Aburaamu abera abanto bao! Ogotagorwa gwaito ’nkoroberiigwa kore, yabekirwe emeroberio y’ogosaria oboererania bwa amang’ana ao y’echisokoro, tobaisa koombia omwana oo

English: All Israel cried with all their might, for death was before their eyes.
Ekegusii: oyio gwatooretie korwa Misiri erinde obe oyoo, igwa okogombereria kwane

English: And queen Esther took refuge in the Lord, being taken as it were in the agony of death.
Ekegusii: bwabere oboererania bwa amang’ana ao oonchore okweumia gwaito kobe omochengo, erio tomenye, Nyasae Omobui, toterere erieta riao tokiria ebikoba biaito, erio biria bia abakogotogia basire. Naende Abaisraeli bakarera n’ehinguru chiabo chionsi, ekiagera amakweri abatogoreretie amaiso.

English: Having taken off her glorious apparel, she put on garments of distress and mourning. Instead of grand perfumes she filled her head with ashes and dung. She greatly humbled her body, and she filled every place of her glad adorning with her tangled hair.
Ekegusii: Enting’ana Esiteri naende akebisa ase Omonene korwa ase obwoba bw’ogokwa okobe okwo kwamotang’aneire. Erio enting’ana Esiteri akeaboria emiambaro eria y’ogokumia, na kobeka emiambaro y’amagombo. Riika riokweyaka amanukato agotiokera igoro, agatuba omotwe oye n’eriibu n’esike y’eng’ombe. Akaonchora mobere oye ase ogwesusura, akaonchora ogwesoka kwaye kwa botaambe kw’omogooko n’ekieni bono gokaba n’eubi eyio yamorenterete ogwechanda gwasansorete etukia yaye. Enting’ana ekarera ase Omenene Nyasae bw’Abaisraeli ase amang’ana aya akobwatia:

English: She implored the Lord God of Israel, and said, “O my Lord, you alone are our king. Help me. I am destitute, and have no helper but you,
Ekegusii: Aye Nyasae Omonene one, omorwoti oito, aye omomoima

English: for my danger is near at hand.
Ekegusii: inchwo onkoonye, ekiagera inde inche bweka, naende inche tindi na mokonyi onde goetania aye, naende nigo inde ang’e gweita inche omonyene. Inche nigo norokereretigwe korwa obwana bwane,

English: I have heard from my birth in the tribe of my kindred that you, Lord, took Israel out of all the nations, and our fathers out of all their kindred for a perpetual inheritance, and have done for them all that you have said.
Ekegusii: ase egekuba kienyomba yaito eyio aye Nyasae Omobui gwachorete Israeli korwa ase ebisaku bionsi naboigo chisokoro chiaito korwa ase egati ya bonsi, babe omwando oo kare na kare naende kwabakoreire buna kwabarierete chiira. Korende intwe twakorire ebibe mamincha yao,

English: And now we have sinned before you, and you have delivered us into the hands of our enemies,
Ekegusii: naboigo gwatoereirie gochia ase ababisa baito erio korwa esiko gochia ase chinyasae chiabo, Nyasae Omobui, aye n’omoronge ore. Korende barabwo tibaisanegeti

English: because we honored their gods. You are righteous, O Lord.
Ekegusii: ase obororo bw’obosomba bwaito; batianire gochia ase emegwekano yaabo gosiria ogochika koria ebikoba biao aye omonyene biatorete batiinyie amorokererio ao bakirie emenwa ya baria bakogotogia barimie egesasiimero kiao n’obonene bw’enyomba yao ase ribaga riaye baigore emenwa y’abanto bense

English: But now they have not been content with the bitterness of our slavery, but have laid their hands on the hands of their idols
Ekegusii: baterere ogotogigwa ase emegwekano etaisaini gento naboigo batung’amere omorwoti obwate omobere bwechinyama. Omonene, tobaisa gotiga enyimbo yao

English: to abolish the decree of your mouth, and utterly to destroy your inheritance, and to stop the mouth of those who praise you, and to extinguish the glory of your house and your altar,
Ekegusii: ase amang’ana ataiyo Totiga ogosarigwa kobe ogosekerererwa Onchora emeroberio ebe mamincha ya baria bayeroberetie na bakore barabwo babe ekemanyererio ase omonto oria okoroberia amabe igoro yaito inyora, aye Nyasae Omobui, eorokie

English: and to open the mouth of the Gentiles to speak the praises of vanities, and that a mortal king should be admired forever.
Ekegusii: ase engaki y’emechando yaito. Korende inche, ong’e oboremu Omorwoti bw’echinyasae na Omonene bw’obobui bwonsi! Mbekere amang’ana y’okoebereria ime ase ebikoba biane

English: O Lord, don’t surrender your sceptre to those who don’t exist, and don’t let them laugh at our fall, but turn their counsel against themselves, and make an example of him who has begun to injure us.
Ekegusii: ekero nkorigererania n’endo; oonchore ekeririanda kiaye gochia ase omobisa oito erio aikere ogosirigwa kwaye naboigo bonsi banga ere! Korende ase tore intwe, ototoorie n’okoboko kwao

English: Remember us, O Lord! Manifest yourself in the time of our affliction. Encourage me, O King of gods, and ruler of all dominion!
Ekegusii: boigo onkoonye, ekiagera inde inche bweka naende tindi nonde otatiga aye bweka, Nyasae Omobui. Aye nore nobomanyi ase ebinto bionsi,

English: Put harmonious speech into my mouth before the lion, and turn his heart to hate him who fights against us, to the utter destruction of those who agree with him.
Ekegusii: boigo nomanyete inche nigo ngechete esiko korwa ase abanto bategeneti Nyasae, naende nigo ’nchaayete oborere bwa abanto bataarogeti, bw’omorwa isiko onde bwensi. Aye nomanyete ng’a nigo nde n’ebitango ebinge,

English: But deliver us by your hand, and help me who am alone and have no one but you, O Lord.
Ekegusii: naende nigo nchaayete ebimanyererio bi’obonene bwane, na tindi gokieboyia buna ebietubo bi’ebioge biane ekero nkoorokera omosangererekano, nigo ngechaayete buna richanchabe rigotioka, naende tindi koyieboyia ase amatuko ane y’ogotimoka. Omosomba oo tana koragera ase emesa eyemo na Hamani,

English: You know all things, and know that I hate the glory of transgressors, and that I abhor the bed of the uncircumcised and of every stranger.
Ekegusii: gose kogokera emeyega y’abanene gose konywa chidivai chiogotwera inse. Gose omosomba oo tana kwegokia

English: You know my necessity, for I abhor the symbol of my proud station, which is upon my head in the days of my splendor. I abhor it as a menstruous cloth, and I don’t wear it in the days of my tranquility.
Ekegusii: korwa rituko riria aetwe obonene goika rero, otatiga ase ore, aye Nyasae Omobui, Nyasae o Aburaamu. Aye Nyasae, oria obwate chinguru chibuete bonsi,

English: It came to pass on the third day, when she had ceased praying, that she took off her servant’s dress and put on her glorious apparel. Being splendidly dressed and having called upon God the Overseer and Preserver of all things, she took her two maids, and she leaned upon one, as a delicate female, and the other followed bearing her train. She was blooming in the perfection of her beauty. Her face was cheerful and looked lovely, but her heart was filled with fear. Having passed through all the doors, she stood before the king. He was sitting on his royal throne. He had put on all his glorious apparel, covered all over with gold and precious stones, and was very terrifying. And having raised his face resplendent with glory, he looked with intense anger. The queen fell, and changed her color as she fainted. She bowed herself upon the head of the maid who went before her. But God changed the spirit of the king to gentleness, and in intense feeling, he sprang from off his throne, and took her into his arms, until she recovered. He comforted her with peaceful words, and said to her, “What is the matter, Esther? I am your relative. Cheer up! You shall not die, for our command is openly declared to you: ‘Draw near.’”
Ekegusii: tegerera eriogi ria abatari na nguru, totoorie korwa ase amaboko y’abakori amabe, ’nsibore korwa ase obwoba bwane! Ase rituko ria gatato Esiteri gakoorire gosaba, akabeeka chianga chiaye chi’obokanyeku, erio akaboyia chianga chioboting’ana. Buna akomekameka igo akarorekana, akarangeria Nyansae, oyio orendete abanto baye na okobatooria. Akaira abaiseke abarendi baye bagachia koganya amo n’ere. Esiteri ore n’etukia enterere mono, akeegemera oyomo obo, n’oria onde akamobwatesia kobogoria engoba yaye.

English: And having raised the golden sceptre, he laid it upon her neck, and embraced her. He said, “Speak to me.” So she said to him, “I saw you, my lord, as an angel of God, and my heart was troubled for fear of your glory; for you, my lord, are to be wondered at, and your face is full of grace.” While she was speaking, she fainted and fell. Then the king was troubled, and all his servants comforted her.
Ekegusii: Oichire n’okomekameka n’obuya bw’ekieni kiaye, obosio bwaye bokamesia omogoko amo n’obwanchani. Korende enkoro yaye ekagongera n’obwoba.

English: The king said, “What do you desire, Esther? What is your request? Ask even to the half of my kingdom, and it shall be yours.”
Ekegusii: Ekero konya aetire korwa kera egesieri gochia ekende, akenyora oteneine bosio bw’Omorwoti. Omorwoti oyio nigo aikakansete bweboyetie n’echiaanga chiaye chi’obonene, okomekameka buna amagena ya amaabera amo n’amagana aande y’engencho - akarorekana ore oyobwogokumia keegima.

English: Esther said, “Today is a special day. So if it seems good to the king, let both him and Haman come to the feast which I will prepare this day.”
Ekegusii: Akarigereria igoro, agaichorwa n’echinguru chi’omorero, ore n’endamwamu egwoka. Enting’ana eria ekagwa k’egiregete inse, erangi y’ekieni keria egasira korwa obosio bwaye, n’omotwe oye okagwera omoiseke oria onde orenge ensemo oganyererete.

English: The king said, “Hurry and bring Haman here, that we may do as Esther said.” So they both came to the feast about which Esther had spoken.
Ekegusii: Korende Nyasae agaonchora enkoro y’omorwoti oria ekaba n’oboitongo gochia ase are. Erio omorwoti akaimoka korwa ase ekerogo kiaye kiobogambi ogoaka eriogi, erinde akamobogoria ase amaboko aye okona komweebereria n’amang’ana amororo igo goika akaba buya.

English: At the banquet, the king said to Esther, “What is your request, queen Esther? You shall have all that you require.”
Ekegusii: Akamoboria: “Esiteri ninki ekebe?” Inche n’oyomino, rema. Tori gokwa, ogochika gwaito nigo kore ase abanto baande abake - abbake niinchuo asende.

English: She said, “My request and my petition is:
Ekegusii: Akaimokia enyimbo yaye y’obogambi eyio yaroisirie n’amagena ya maabera agatorera Esiteri ase ebigoti biaye, akamoagata okomoteebia: kwana naiche, Esiteri akamoteebia “Inyiborie!” nigo okororekana buna oyomo bw’Abamalaika ba Nyasae. Enkoro yane nigo yaichorwa, n’omoichano bw’echinguru chiao. Nigo ore oyo bw’okororekana kw’ogokumia. Nyasae one Omobui, enkoro yao nigo eichire n’obuya.

English: if I have found favor in the king’s sight, let the king and Haman come again tomorrow to the feast which I shall prepare for them, and tomorrow I will do as I have done today.”
Ekegusii: Korende ekero Esiteri agendererete gokwana amang’ana aya, akagwa inse akagireka. Omorwoti akabwatwa n’amaabera nakogania komotooria. Ekero omorwoti aroche Esiteri enting’ana oteneine ase egoora, Esiteri akanyora ogwancherwa asare. Omorwoti akamworotera enyimbo yaye y’oborwoti eroisirie korwa ase etaabu, arenge nero koboko. Erio Esiteri akagenda gochia ang’e, agakuna mesia y’enyimbo eria.

English: So Haman went out from the king very glad and merry; but when Haman saw Mordecai the Jew in the court, he was greatly enraged.
Ekegusii: Na omorwoti akamobooria: “Eting’ana Esiteri, ninki origetie? Inteebia eki oganetie; aye n’okeegwe, nakeba nonya nekeng’ese ki’oborwoti bwane.”

English: Having gone into his own house, he called his friends, and his wife Zeresh.
Ekegusii: Esiteri akairaneria, “Koranche omorwoti, ochiche mwane reero, aye amo na Hamani, ase endagera nakoroiseirie aye omorwoti.”

English: He showed them his wealth and the glory with which the king had invested him, and how he had promoted him to be chief ruler in the kingdom.
Ekegusii: Omorwoti akarwa ogochika Hamani aretwe ase obwango, erinde banyare gokora aya Esiteri aganetie. Agwo omorwoti na Hamani bakagenda ase endagera eria Esiteri aroisetie.

English: Haman said, “The queen has called no one to the feast with the king but me, and I am invited tomorrow.
Ekegusii: Ekero baare konywa edivai, omorwoti akaboria Esiteri, “Ninki origetie? Ekio nokeegwe. Ninki oganetie? Nakeba nonya nekeng’ese ki’oborwoti bwane, nokeegwe.”

English: But these things don’t please me while I see Mordecai the Jew in the court.
Ekegusii: Esiteri akairaneria, “Ogosaba kwane na okogania kwane noko:

English: Then Zeresh his wife and his friends said to him, “Let a fifty cubit tall gallows be made for you. In the morning you speak to the king, and let Mordecai be hanged on the gallows; but you go in to the feast with the king, and be merry.” The saying pleased Haman, and the gallows was prepared.
Ekegusii: Onye nanyorire ogwancherwa ase obosio bwao, aye omorwoti, koranche aye amo na Hamani, ankio naende moche mobe abageni baane ase endagera ndache mbaroiserie. Ase ekero ekio nario ndache ngoteebie eki nganetie.”

English: The Lord removed sleep from the king that night; so he told his servant to bring in the books, the registers of daily events, to read to him.
Ekegusii: Ase obotuko boria omorwoti taraarete chitoro; agachiika arenterwe egetabu kerikire amang’ana y’ebiro ayio arenge gokoreka agwenerete koinyorwa, n’amang’ana ayio agasomwa asare.

English: And he found the records written concerning Mordecai, how he had told the king about the king’s two chamberlains, when they were keeping guard, and sought to lay hands on Ahasuerus.
Ekegusii: Amang’ana akarorekana ariikire ng’a Modekai natebeete igoro ya Bigitana na Teresi, abasoomba babere b’omorwoti, abwo barenge amateba na bare korenda egesieri ki’omorwoti, ng’a mbarigetie goita omorwoti Ahaswero.

English: The king said, “What honor or favor have we done for Mordecai?” The king’s servants said, “You haven’t done anything for him.”
Ekegusii: Omorwoti akaboria, “Inee! Ngosika ki, gose masikani ki Modekai akoreirwe ase engencho y’ayio?” Abanto b’omorwoti abarenge komokorera, bakamoiraneria, “Tana gokorerwa kende.”

English: And while the king was enquiring about the kindness of Mordecai, behold, Haman was in the court. The king said, “Who is in the court? Now Haman had come in to speak to the king about hanging Mordecai on the gallows which he had prepared.
Ekegusii: Omorwoti akaboria, “Ning’o oyio ore ase egoora?” Ekaba ng’a Hamani nere orenge gosoa ase egoora isiko y’enyomba y’omorwoti, akwane n’omorwoti, erinde achie gotonga Modekai ase orobambo roria amosimiseretie.

English: The king’s servants said, “Behold, Haman stands in the court.” And the king said, “Call him!”
Ekegusii: Ase ayio abasoomba bagateebia omorwoti, “Hamani oteneine ase egoora.” Omorwoti akabateebia, “Moteebie asoe.”

English: The king said to Haman, “What should I do for the man whom I wish to honor?” Haman said within himself, “Whom would the king honor but myself?”
Ekegusii: Ase igo Hamani agasoa ime, na omorwoti akamobooria, “Ninki agwenerete akorerwe omonto oria inche omorwoti nanchire gosika?” Hamani akarengereria ase omoyo oye ime, “Ning’o omorwoti anchete gosika kobua inche?”

English: He said to the king, “As for the man whom the king wishes to honor,
Ekegusii: Hamani akairaneria omorwoti, “Oria omorwoti anchete gosika

English: let the king’s servants bring the robe of fine linen which the king puts on, and the horse on which the king rides,
Ekegusii: goika arenterwe eanga y’oborwoti, eyio omorwoti abeekire, na ebarasi eyio omorwoti anarete koriina ebekeire egutwa y’oborwoti ase omotwe oye.

English: and let him give it to one of the king’s noble friends, and let him dress the man whom the king loves. Let him mount him on the horse, and proclaim through the streets of the city, saying, “This is what will be done for every man whom the king honors!”
Ekegusii: Omotang’ani oyomo omonene, na oyo bw’amasikani oyio ogokorera omorwoti, aegwe eanga eyio na ebarasi eyio. Erio abeekere omonto oyio omorwoti anchete gosika eanga eyio, na amoriinie ase ebarasi eyio, amoetananie ase ekerario ki’omochie, okoraria bosio bwaye amang’ana ayio: iga nabo Omonto oyio omorwoti anchire gosika agokorerwa.”

English: Then the king said to Haman, “You have spoken well. Do so for Mordecai the Jew, who waits in the palace, and let not a word of what you have spoken be neglected!”
Ekegusii: Erio omorwoti agateebia Hamani, “Genda bono bwango, oire chianga chiria na ebarasi eria, okorere Modekai, Omoyahudi oyio ore ase egeita kiane, inche omorwoti, buna gwateba. Tobaisa kweba nonya ne ring’ana erimo ase aria gwateeba.”

English: So Haman took the robe and the horse, dressed Mordecai, mounted him on the horse, and went through the streets of the city, proclaiming, “This is what will be done for every man whom the king wishes to honor.”
Ekegusii: Ase igo Hamani akaimokia eanga eria akayebekera Modekai, na akamoriinia ebarasi igoro, akamoetanania ase ekerario ki’omochie, akaba okoraria bosio bwaye, “iga nabo Omonto oyio omorwoti anchire gosika agokorerwa.”

English: Then Mordecai returned to the palace; but Haman went home mourning, with his head covered.
Ekegusii: Modekai akairana geita ki’omorwoti, korende Hamani akaayerera gochia bwoye, oichanete na korera, bwetubete omotwe oye.

English: Haman related the events that had happened to him to Zeresh his wife and to his friends. His friends and his wife said to him, “If Mordecai is of the race of the Jews, and you have begun to be humbled before him, you will assuredly fall; and you will not be able to withstand him, for the living God is with him.”
Ekegusii: Hamani agateebia Seresi mokaye, na abasani baye bonsi, kera egento eke kiamonyorete. Erio abanto baye abanyasemi, na Seresi mokaye, bakamoteebia, “Onye Modekai, oyio aye gwachakire koba inse yaye n’Omoyahudi are tokomonyara; amaene nere orakobue.”

English: While they were still speaking, the chamberlains arrived to rush Haman to the banquet which Esther had prepared.
Ekegusii: Ekero bagendererete gokwana nere, abakoreri b’enyomba y’omorwoti bagacha kwoyia Hamani bakamoira bwango ase endagera eria Esiteri aroisetie.

English: So the king and Haman went in to drink with the queen.
Ekegusii: Ase igo, omorwoti na Hamani bakagenda koria endagera amo n’Esiteri enting’ana.

English: The king said to Esther at the banquet on the second day, “What is it, queen Esther? What is your request? What is your petition? It shall be done for you, up to half of my kingdom.”
Ekegusii: Ekero barenge konywa edivai ase rituko erio ria kabere, omorwoti akaboria Esiteri naende, “Eting’ana Esiteri, ninki origetie? Ekio nokeegwe. Ninki oganetie? Gokerabe nonya nekeng’ese ki’oborwoti bwane, nokeegwe.”

English: She answered and said, “If I have found favor in the sight of the king, let my life be granted as my petition, and my people as my request.
Ekegusii: Eting’ana Esiteri akairaneria, akabora: “Aye omorwoti, onye nanyorire ogwancherwa ase obosio bwao, naende amang’ana aya karakogokie, ntige ngenderere koba moyo, na abanto baane boigo; oko nakwo okogania kwane.

English: For both I and my people are sold for destruction, pillage, and genocide. If both we and our children were sold for male and female slaves, I would not have bothered you, for this isn’t worthy of the king’s palace.”
Ekegusii: Inche na abanto baane twaoonigwe, tosirigwe kegima ase ogoitwa. Onye nigo twaoonigwa tochie koba abasoomba, abasacha na abakungu, nanga nigo nakira tinkwana, ekiagera amang’ana ayio tare goisana gochanda omorwoti.”

English: The king said, “Who has dared to do this thing?”
Ekegusii: Erio omorwoti Ahaswero akabooria enting’ana Esiteri, “Ning’o ore noboremu gokora ayare buna ayio? Ng’ai omonto buna oyio are?”

English: Esther said, “The enemy is Haman, this wicked man!” Then Haman was terrified in the presence of the king and the queen.
Ekegusii: Esiteri akairaneria, akamoteebia “Omochandi na omobisa oito omonene, nere oyo Hamani, omonto omobe kegima.” Erio Hamani agasogwa n’omoondoko ase obosio bw’omorwoti na obw’enting’ana.

English: The king rose up from the banquet to go into the garden. Haman began to beg the queen for mercy, for he saw that he was in serious trouble.
Ekegusii: Omorwoti akaimoka korwa ase omoyega oyio ore n’endamwamu, akagenda isiko ase egeticha kiare, agwo ase enyomba yaye. Hamani agatenena gosorora Esiteri enting’ana ng’a amotige abe moyo, ekiagera aroche ng’a omorwoti nigo arengereretie komosiria.

English: The king returned from the garden; and Haman had fallen upon the couch, begging the queen for mercy. The king said, “Will you even assault my wife in my house?” And when Haman heard it, he changed countenance.
Ekegusii: Ekero omorwoti airanete korwa ase egeticha aria isiko gochia ase enyomba eria ase barenge konywera edivai, Hamani nigo araire inse oumaime ase egeikaransero gi’Esiteri. Omorwoti akaboria, “Inee! Nigo aganetie gokorera enting’ana obonyaka ase obosio bwane aa nyomba mwane ime?” Na ekero ring’ana riasogete korwa ase omonwa bw’omorwoti, abasoomba bagatuba Hamani obosio.

English: And Bugathan, one of the chamberlains, said to the king, “Behold, Haman has also prepared a gallows for Mordecai, who spoke concerning the king, and a fifty cubit high gallows has been set up on Haman’s property.” The king said, “Let him be hanged on it!”
Ekegusii: Haribona, oyomo bw’abasoomba abaare gokorera omorwoti, akabora, “Rora orobambo rore rw’obotambe bw’amaboko emerongo etano, roria Hamani asimiseretie Modekai, oyo ogotooretie aye omorwoti, nao rore ang’e nenyomba ya Hamani.” Agwo omorwoti agachiika, “Gachie motonge Hamani ase orobambo roria igoro.”

English: So Haman was hanged on the gallows that had been prepared for Mordecai. Then the king’s wrath was abated.
Ekegusii: Ase igo Hamani agatongwa ase orobambo roria asimiseretie Modekai. Erio endamwamu y’omorwoti egakenda.

English: On that day, King Ahasuerus gave to Esther all that belonged to Haman the slanderer. The king called Mordecai, for Esther had told that he was related to her.
Ekegusii: Ase rituko riria omorwoti Ahaswero akaa Esiteri enting’ana enyomba ya Hamani, omochandi bw’Abayahudi. Modekai akanyora ribaga gosoa ase omorwoti, ekiagera Esiteri konya oteebirie omorwoti igoro y’oboiri bwaye na Modekai.

English: The king took the ring which he had taken away from Haman and gave it to Mordecai. Esther appointed Mordecai over all that had been Haman’s.
Ekegusii: Bono omorwoti akarusia ebonyi eria amoete Hamani, akayea Modekai, na Esiteri akabeeka Modekai atenenere enyomba eria yarenge ya Hamani.

English: She spoke yet again to the king, and fell at his feet, and implored him to undo Haman’s mischief and all that he had done against the Jews.
Ekegusii: Erio Esiteri agakwana naende n’omorwoti, agatung’ama inse ase amagoro aye, akamosorora mono ase ogoitera amariga ng’a asarie omoroberio bw’ogosiria Abayahudi, oria Hamani Omoagagi aruete.

English: Then the king extended the golden sceptre to Esther; and Esther arose to stand near the king.
Ekegusii: Omorwoti akaimokia enyimbo eria y’etaabu, akamosiema. Esiteri akaimoka, agatenena ase obosio bw’omorwoti akamorigereria.

English: Esther said, “If it seems good to you, and I have found favor in your sight, let an order be sent that the letters sent by Haman may be reversed—letters that were written for the destruction of the Jews who are in your kingdom.
Ekegusii: Erio ere akabora, “Aye omorwoti, onye kwarorire ng’a mbuya, na onye inche nanyorire ogwancherwa asore, ne ring’ana eri korirarorekane asore ng’a nerironge, naende erio ndinkogokie, aye omorwoti, koranche karwe ogochika gotanga amang’ana aria Hamani, mosinto bwa Hamedata Omoagagi, konya achiikire ng’a Abayahudi bonsi bare ase chingongo chionsi chi’obogambi bwao basirigwe.

English: For how could I see the affliction of my people, and how could I survive the destruction of my kindred?”
Ekegusii: Naki ndakore ndemererie ndore amabe ayio akobacheera abaminto? Gose naki ndakore ndemererie ndore abanto b’egesaku kiane bagosirigwa?”

English: Then the king said to Esther, “If I have given and freely granted you all that was Haman’s, and hanged him on a gallows because he laid his hands upon the Jews, what more do you seek?
Ekegusii: Omorwoti Ahaswero agateebia Esiteri enting’ana na Modekai Omoyahudi, “Rora, naeire Esiteri enyomba ya Hamani, na Hamani otongirwe igoro ase orobambo roria, ekiagera arigetie goita Abayahudi.

English: Write in my name whatever seems good to you, and seal it with my ring; for whatever is written at the command of the king, and sealed with my ring, cannot be countermanded.
Ekegusii: Gaki inwe riika riruube ase Abayahudi, moribeeke erieta riane, inche omorwoti, moriike buna morarore, moribeeke ekemanyererio ki’ebonyi yane, ekiagera riruube rinde rionsi ririikire na kobeekwa erieta ri’omorwoti amo nekemanyererio ki’ebonyi yaye, onde tari orarionchore.”

English: So the scribes were called in the first month, which is Nisan, on the twenty-third day of the same year; and orders were written to the Jews, whatever the king had commanded to the local governors and chiefs of the local governors, from India even to Ethiopia—one hundred twenty-seven local governors, according to the several provinces, in their own languages.
Ekegusii: Abariiki b’omorwoti bakarangerigwa agwo ase omotienyi o gatato, noro omotienyi o Siwani, rituko ri’emerongo ebere na gatato, na buna Modekai achiigete, amarube akarikwa gochia ase Abayahudi, na gochia ase abagaambi abanene b’oborwoti na abagabana, na abanene bonsi be chingongo chionsi korwa India goika Ethiopia, chingongo rigana erimo, na emerongo ebere, na isano na ibere (127). Amarube ayio akarikwa ase kera orogongo ase okoriikwa kw’engencho y’amariiko abo, na ase kera egesaku ase omonwa obo na ase Abayahudi ase enchera yabo y’okoriika ase omonwa obo.

English: They were written by order of the king, sealed with his ring, and the letters were sent by the couriers.
Ekegusii: Amang’ana ayio nigo arigetwe na kobekwa erieta ri’omorwoti Ahaswero, na akabekwa ekemanyererio ki’ebonyi yaye. Erio amarube ayio akairwa nabariini be chibarasi chi’omorwoti echio chiare kominyoka bwango.

English: In them, he charged them to use their own laws in every city, to help each other, and to treat their adversaries and those who attacked them as they pleased,
Ekegusii: Amarube ayio nigo arenge goteeba ng’a omorwoti orure ribaga ase Abayahudi ba kera omochie bache amo, erinde beegerere abanyene. Baegwe ribaga boigo goita abarwani bande bonsi ba kera egesaku baare gocha kobarwania, baite n’abana babo na abakungu babo; boigo basakore chinibo chiabo.

English: on one day in all the kingdom of Ahasuerus, on the thirteenth day of the twelfth month, which is Adar.
Ekegusii: Ayio akorete ase rituko erimo naro aya akobwatia:

English: The following is a copy of the letter containing orders: The great King Ahasuerus sends greetings to the rulers of provinces in one hundred twenty-seven local governance regions, from India to Ethiopia, even to those who are faithful to our interests. Many who have been frequently honored by the most abundant kindness of their benefactors have conceived ambitious designs, and not only endeavor to hurt our subjects, but moreover, not being able to bear prosperity, they also endeavor to plot against their own benefactors. They not only would utterly abolish gratitude from among men, but also, elated by the boastings of men who are strangers to all that is good, they supposed that they would escape the sin-hating vengeance of the ever-seeing God. And oftentimes evil exhortation has made partakers of the guilt of shedding innocent blood, and has involved in irremediable calamities many of those who had been appointed to offices of authority, who had been entrusted with the management of their friends’ affairs; while men, by the false sophistry of an evil disposition, have deceived the simple goodwill of the ruling powers. And it is possible to see this, not so much from more ancient traditional accounts, as it is immediately in your power to see it by examining what things have been wickedly perpetrated by the baseness of men unworthily holding power. It is right to take heed with regard to the future, that we may maintain the government in undisturbed peace for all men, adopting needful changes, and ever judging those cases which come under our notice with truly equitable decisions. For whereas Haman, a Macedonian, the son of Hammedatha, in reality an alien from the blood of the Persians, and differing widely from our mild course of government, having been hospitably entertained by us, obtained so large a share of our universal kindness as to be called our father, and to continue the person next to the royal throne, reverenced of all; he however, overcome by pride, endeavored to deprive us of our dominion, and our life; having by various and subtle artifices demanded for destruction both Mordecai our deliverer and perpetual benefactor, and Esther the blameless consort of our kingdom, along with their whole nation. For by these methods he thought, having surprised us in a defenseless state, to transfer the dominion of the Persians to the Macedonians. But we find that the Jews, who have been consigned to destruction by the most abominable of men, are not malefactors, but living according to the most just laws, and being the sons of the living God, the most high and mighty, who maintains the kingdom, to us as well as to our forefathers, in the most excellent order. You will therefore do well in refusing to obey the letter sent by Haman the son of Hammedatha, because he who has done these things has been hanged with his whole family at the gates of Susa, Almighty God having swiftly returned to him a worthy punishment. We enjoin you then, having openly published a copy of this letter in every place, to give the Jews permission to use their own lawful customs and to strengthen them, that on the thirteenth of the twelfth month Adar, on the self-same day, they may defend themselves against those who attack them in a time of affliction. For in the place of the destruction of the chosen race, Almighty God has granted them this time of gladness. Therefore you also, among your notable feasts, must keep a distinct day with all festivity, that both now and hereafter it may be a day of deliverance to us and who are well disposed toward the Persians, but to those that plotted against us a memorial of destruction. And every city and province collectively, which shall not do accordingly, shall be consumed with vengeance by spear and fire. It shall be made not only inaccessible to men, but most hateful to wild beasts and birds forever. Let the copies be posted in conspicuous places throughout the kingdom. Let all the Jews be ready against this day, to fight against their enemies.
Ekegusii: Omorwoti omonene Ahaswero, ne rituko erio nigo rirabe eria ikomi na gatato ri’omotienyi o ikomi na kabere okorokwa Adari.

English: So the horsemen went forth with haste to perform the king’s commands. The ordinance was also published in Susa.
Ekegusii: Abanto abange abwo baetwe amasikani goetera ase baria babatang’anerete nigo bakoba abaenenu. Teisaini ase bare korigia korwa ase abanto baito chingoma, korende tibakonyara gosira oborito bw’amamocho abo barobwo abanyene erio baonchoka bachaka koroberia mamincha ya baria bare igoro yabo.

English: Mordecai went out robed in royal apparel, wearing a golden crown and a diadem of fine purple linen. The people in Susa saw it and rejoiced.
Ekegusii: Tibaisanegeti n’egesururo korwa ase enkoro ya mwanyabaanto, korende nigo bakogokigwa n’abanto abwo bagwakanwa ase amaya, batamanyeti ng’a onsi nigo are ase amaiso a Nyasae, nigo bakagerete ng’a mbetange korwa ase endamwamu yaye y’ogokumia gochia ase abanyabibe.

English: The Jews had light and gladness
Ekegusii: Yabeire bo ase baria bare n’okobua, nigo bakwegena abasani babo nagwancha kobwatia omonguso obo, nigo benyorire bagosanga nabarobwo ase egesusuro egetindi,

English: in every city and province where the ordinance was published. Wherever the proclamation took place, the Jews had joy and gladness, feasting and mirth. Many of the Gentiles were circumcised and became Jews for fear of the Jews.
Ekegusii: okorengereria okoronge kw’abarai kwamerirwe n’okorengeria okobe.

English: Now in the twelfth month, on the thirteenth day of the month, which is Adar, the letters written by the king arrived.
Ekegusii: Rituko ria ikomi na gatato ri’omotienyi o ikomi na kabere, noro omotienyi bw’Adari, rigaika. Ase rituko ria ikomi na gatato ekero ogochika kw’omorwoti kware gocha goikeranigwa, ababisa b’Abayahudi nigo basemeretie ng’a mbaababue, korende amang’ana konya aonchokire ng’a Abayahudi mbabue ababisa babo.

English: In that day, the adversaries of the Jews perished; for no one resisted, through fear of them.
Ekegusii: Bono Abayahudi bagasangererekana amo ase emechie yabo yonsi, na ase chingongo chionsi chi’obogambi bw’omorwoti Ahaswero, erinde baite abanto baria barigetie kobasiria. Monto onde tarenge onyarete kobatanga, ekiagera obwoba ase engencho y’abwo konya bwasoire ase abanto bonsi.

English: For the chiefs of the local governors, and the princes and the royal scribes, honored the Jews; for the fear of Mordecai was upon them.
Ekegusii: Ase igo abanene bonsi be chingongo chiria, na abagabana, na abagaambi abanene bonsi b’oborwoti, baria baare gokora emeremo y’omorwoti, bagakonya Abayahudi, ekiagera boboete Modekai.

English: For the order of the king was in force, that he should be celebrated in all the kingdom.
Ekegusii: Modekai nigo arenge omonene ase enyomba y’omorwoti, na akamenta koba n’okobua, na igo chinkuma chiaye chigasarera ase chingongo chionsi chi’oborwoti boria.

English: In the city Susa the Jews killed five hundred men,
Ekegusii: Ase igo Abayahudi bakabua ababisa babo bonsi, bakabakenya na kobasiria; bagakora buna banchete ase abwo baabagechete.

English: including Pharsannes, Delphon, Phasga,
Ekegusii: Agwo ase eburi ya Susa, Abayahudi bagaita abanto amagana atano, bakabasiria.

English: Pharadatha, Barea, Sarbaca,
Ekegusii: Bagaita Parisanidata, na Dalifoni, na Asipata;

English: Marmasima, Ruphaeus, Arsaeus, and Zabuthaeus,
Ekegusii: Porata na Adalia, na Aridata;

English: the ten sons of Haman the son of Hammedatha the Bugaean, the enemy of the Jews; and they plundered their property on the same day.
Ekegusii: Parimasita, na Arisai, na Aridai, na Waisata,

English: The number of those who perished in Susa was reported to the king.
Ekegusii: abamura ikomi b’omobisa oria bw’Abayahudi, Hamani, mosinto bwa Hamedata. Korende tibakunete ebinto biabo kobisakora.

English: Then the king said to Esther, “The Jews have slain five hundred men in the city Susa. What do you think they have done in the rest of the country? What more do you ask, that it may be done for you?”
Ekegusii: Ase rituko erio erio omorwoti akarenterwa omobaro bw’abaitetwe aria Susa, omochie omonene,

English: Esther said to the king, “Let it be granted to the Jews to do the same to them tomorrow. Also, hang the bodies of the ten sons of Haman.”
Ekegusii: na omorwoti agateebia Esiteri enting’ana: “Agwo ase eburi ya Susa, Abayahudi baitire abanto amagana atano, baabasiririe, boigo baitire abamura ikomi ba Hamani. Onye ere igo, Inee, ngento ki bakorire ase chinsemo chinde ase chingongo chi’oborwoti bwane? Bono ninki naende oganetie? Nokeegwe. Nteebia ngento ki naende otarakorerwa. Nakerokio nokorerwe.”

English: He permitted it to be done; and he gave up to the Jews of the city the bodies of the sons of Haman to hang.
Ekegusii: Esiteri akamoiraneria: “Omorwoti korarore mbuya, Abayahudi aba bare agwo Susa baegwe ribaga ankio boigo bakore koreng’ana nogochika kwa reero; tiga abamura ba Hamani ikomi batongwe ase chimbambo igoro.”

English: The Jews assembled in Susa on the fourteenth day of Adar and killed three hundred men, but plundered no property.
Ekegusii: Omorwoti agachiika ayio akorwe; ogochika okwo gokararigwa agwo Susa, na abamura baria ikomi ba Hamani bagatongwa ase chimbambo igoro.

English: The rest of the Jews who were in the kingdom assembled, and helped one another, and obtained rest from their enemies; for they destroyed fifteen thousand of them on the thirteenth day of Adar, but took no spoil.
Ekegusii: Abayahudi abarenge Susa bagasangerereka amo naende, ase rituko ria ikomi na kane, omotienyi bw’Adari, bagaita abanto amagana atato aroro, korende tibakunete ebinto biabo kobisakora.

English: They rested on the fourteenth of the same month, and kept it as a day of rest with joy and gladness.
Ekegusii: Abayahudi bande abarenge ase chingongo chinde chi’obogambi obwo bagasangerereka amo ase okoegera obogima bwabo, ase okwenyorera obotoereru na gwetooria korwa ase ababisa babo.

English: The Jews in the city of Susa assembled also on the fourteenth day and rested; and they also observed the fifteenth with joy and gladness.
Ekegusii: Bagaita abanto chilifu emerongo etano na ebere na isano (75,000), korende tibakuneti ebinto biabo kobisakora,

English: On this account then, the Jews dispersed in every foreign land keep the fourteenth of Adar as a holy day with joy, each sending gifts of food to his neighbor.
Ekegusii: korende ase Abayahudi ba Susa, abwo basangerekanete ase rituko ria ikomi na gatato na ikomi na kane, rituko ria ikomi na gatani n’erituko batimogete, bakarikora rikaba rituko ri’ogochenga na kogoka.

English: Mordecai wrote these things in a book and sent them to the Jews, as many as were in the kingdom of Ahasuerus, both those who were near and those who were far away,
Ekegusii: Eke nakio gekogera Abayahudi abwo bamenyete ase emechie n’ebinyoro, abwo bamenyete ase atagitiri, bakorenda rituko ria ikomi na kane ase omotienyi bwa Adar buna rituko ri’omochengo na koragera barobwo ase barobwo,

English: to establish these as joyful days and to keep the fourteenth and fifteenth of Adar;
Ekegusii: Ase igo, Abayahudi abamenyete ase emechie emeke etagiteire, nigo barenge korenda rituko ria ikomi na kane ri’omotienyi bw’Adari koba rituko ri’omogooko na eri’omoyega, Rituko Rinene, bagatomerana ebiegwa bi’endagera engiya baroisetie.

English: for on these days the Jews obtained rest from their enemies; and in that month, which was Adar, in which a change was made for them from mourning to joy, and from sorrow to a holiday, to spend the whole of it in good days of feasting and gladness, sending portions to their friends and to the poor.
Ekegusii: Modekai akariika amang’ana ayio, na agatoma amarube ase Abayahudi bonsi abarenge ang’e na aare ase chingongo chionsi chi’oborwoti bw’Ahaswero,

English: And the Jews consented to this as Mordecai wrote to them,
Ekegusii: akabateebia ng’a barende rituko ria ikomi na kane, na eria ikomi na gatano, ase omotienyi bw’Adari, omwaka ase omwaka, abe Amatuko Amanene.

English: showing how Haman the son of Hammedatha the Macedonian fought against them, how he made a decree and cast lots to destroy them utterly;
Ekegusii: Amatuko ayio naro Abayahudi barabe bakoinyora buna banyorete obotoereru na ogotooreka korwa ase ababisa babo, na buna ase omotienyi oyio emechando yabo yaonchoretwe ekaba omogooko, na omoichano obo okaba omochengo. Ase ayio babe bagokora amatuko ayio abe ay’omoyega na ay’omogooko, amatuko ay’ogotomerana ebiegwa bi’endagera babe bakoroisia naende bae abataka ebiegwa.

English: also how he went in to the king, telling him to hang Mordecai; but all the calamities he tried to bring upon the Jews came upon himself, and he was hanged, along with his children.
Ekegusii: Ase igo Abayahudi bagancha kwenaria gokora buna bachaagete, na buna Modekai abariikerete bakore.

English: Therefore these days were called Purim, because of the lots (for in their language they are called Purim) because of the words of this letter, and because of all they suffered on this account, and all that happened to them.
Ekegusii: Hamani Omoagagi mosinto bwa Hamedata, omobisa bw’Abayahudi bonsi, konya orobeirie igoro y’Abayahudi ng’a abasirie, na konya oakire obomera bokorokwa Puri ase okoumokera Abayahudi mobosokano na kobasiria.

English: Mordecai established it, and the Jews took upon themselves, upon their offspring, and upon those who were joined to them to observe it, neither would they on any account behave differently; but these days were to be a memorial kept in every generation, city, family, and province.
Ekegusii: Korende ekero Esiteri achete ase omorwoti na komoteebia amang’ana ayio, Omorwoti akarua ogochika ase amarube ng’a omoroberio oria Hamani akorete mamincha y’Abayahudi omoiraneire ere omonyene, na ere na abamura baye bagatongwa ase chimbambo igoro.

English: These days of Purim shall be kept forever, and their memorial shall not fail in any generation.
Ekegusii: Amang’ana ayio akagera Amatuko ayio Amanene arendwe, ayio akorokwa Purimu kobwatekana nerieta ri’obomera boria bokorokwa Puri. Ase engencho y’amang’ana onsi ay’amaruube ayio, na ase aria baroche abanyene, na ayio onsi abanyorete.

English: Queen Esther the daughter of Aminadab and Mordecai the Jew wrote all that they had done, and gave the confirmation of the letter about Purim.
Ekegusii: Abayahudi bagachiika ase barabwo abanyene, na ase chinderia chiabo, na ase abande bonsi babwatanete nabarabwo ng’a babe bakorenda amatuko ayio abere kera omwaka, naende bayabwate koreng’ana buna bachiikire, ne chingaki chichiikire.

English: Mordecai and Esther the queen established this decision on their own, pledging their own well-being to their plan.
Ekegusii: Amatuko ayio abe akoinyorwa na kobwatwa ebiaare ase ebiaare, ase kera eamate na ase kera orogongo, na kera omochie. Amatuko ayio a Purimu tabaisa gotigwa korendwa ase egati y’Abayahudi, gose ekeinyorio ki’amatuko ayio tikemocha koba ase chinderia chiabo.

English: And Esther established it by a command forever, and it was written for a memorial.
Ekegusii: Erio enting’ana Esiteri, omosubati bw’Abihaili, na Modekai, Omoyahudi oria, bakariika riruube ri’ogokong’ia amang’ana ye riruube riria ria kabere igoro y’okorenda Purimu.

English: The king levied a tax upon his kingdom both by land and sea.
Ekegusii: Omorwoti Ahaswero akarusia ebango ase abanto b’ense yaye, na ase ebisinka bie chinyancha.

English: As for his strength and valour, and the wealth and glory of his kingdom, behold, they are written in the book of the Persians and Medes for a memorial.
Ekegusii: Bono amang’ana onsi igoro y’ogokora kwaye gwonsi, na okobua kwaye, amo n’amang’ana onsi buna aimokereretie Modekai igoro, nigo ariikire ase Egetabu ki’ogokora kw’abarwoti b’Abamedia na ab’Abaayemi.

English: Mordecai was viceroy to King Ahasuerus, and was a great man in the kingdom, honored by the Jews, and lived his life loved by all his nation.
Ekegusii: Modekai, Omoyahudi oria, nere orenge oyo o kabere ase omorwoti Ahaswero. Nigo arenge omonene ase Abayahudi, osikire nabamwabo bonsi, ekiagera nigo arenge korigia amaya ase abanto baye, na akerua ase okobarentera omorembe.

English: Mordecai said, “These things have come from God.
Ekegusii: Ase igo, kera omwaka, “Ase chingaki chigochia goocha chionsi,

English: For I remember the dream which I had concerning these matters; for not one detail of them has failed.
Ekegusii: abanto ba Omonene inabasangererekane ase obosio bwaye ase rituko ria gikomi na kane na ikomi na gatano ase omotienyi bw’Adari na koyachengera ekiare ekemo goika ekiare kende.”

English: There was the little spring which became a river, and there was light, and the sun and much water. The river is Esther, whom the king married and made queen.
Ekegusii: Ase omwaka o kane bw’oborwoti bwa Tolemani na mokaye Kileopatura,

English: The two serpents are Haman and me.
Ekegusii: omonto gete orenge korokwa Dositheo naende okweroka Omokuani Omolawi,

English: The nations are those which combined to destroy the name of the Jews.
Ekegusii: akarenta riruube rigokwanera rituko rinene rie Chipuri.

English: But as for my nation, this is Israel, even those who cried to God and were delivered; for the Lord delivered his people. The Lord rescued us out of all these calamities; and God worked such signs and great wonders as have not been done among the nations.
Ekegusii: Ere nigo arenge gotunyanwa nomwana oye omoisia orenge korokwa Tolemai na barabwo bakararia buna riruube erio n’eriekeene na buna nigo riaonchoretwe na Lisimako omwana omomura o Tolemai oyomo bwa abamenyi b’omochie o Yerusalemu.

English: Therefore he ordained two lots. One for the people of God, and one for all the other nations.
Ekegusii: Agachora abanto babere abwo barenge koba omoerio bwabanto oyomo ase abanto baye, noyonde ase chinse chionsi.

English: And these two lots came for an appointed season, and for a day of judgment, before God, and for all the nations.
Ekegusii: Nabwo nigo bare gokora emeremo ase chingaki nebiro abio Nyasae achorete ase chinse chionsi.

English: God remembered his people and vindicated his inheritance.
Ekegusii: Ase enchera eyio Nyasae oinyore abanto baye na obomenyo bwaye boigo;

English: They shall observe these days in the month Adar, on the fourteenth and on the fifteenth day of the month, with an assembly, joy, and gladness before God, throughout the generations forever among his people Israel.
Ekegusii: na ase bare amatuko aya, rituko ria ikomi na kane n’eria ikomi na gatano ase omotienyi bwa Adari, nigo are amatuko y’omosangerekano, y’omogoko n’omochengo ase Nyasae, goetera ase ebisaku bionsi na goika kare na kare ase abanto baye Israeli.

English: In the fourth year of the reign of Ptolemeus and Cleopatra, Dositheus, who said he was a priest and Levite, and Ptolemeus his son brought this letter of Purim, which they said was authentic, and that Lysimachus the son of Ptolemeus, who was in Jerusalem, had interpreted.
Ekegusii: Ase omwaka o kane bw’okogamba gwa Ptomemi na kiropata, Dosites oyio bwancheranere buna nigo arenge Omokuani na Omolawi, na Putolemi omwana oye akareta riruube igoro ya Purimu. Bakaebereria erio amang’ana ayio ancherwe, ogonchora nigo gwakoretwe na Lisimako mosinto o Putolemi, oyio orenge oyomo ase ekeombe ki’Abayahudi.

English: Love righteousness, all you who are judges of the earth. Think of the Lord with a good mind. Seek him in singleness of heart,
Ekegusii: Ancha gokorera ekeene inwe abarai b’ense. Beeka ebirengererio biaino ase Omonene na momorigie n’echinkoro chiaino.

English: because he is found by those who don’t put him to the test, and is manifested to those who trust him.
Ekegusii: Ekiagera ere nigo are ang’e nabwo batari komoteema, na nigo akweorokia ase abwo bamosemeretie.

English: for crooked thoughts separate from God. His Power convicts when it is tested, and exposes the foolish;
Ekegusii: Ebirengererio ebikorekanu nigo bigwatanana abanto korwa ase Nyasae, na ekero chinguru chiaye chigotemwa, nigo chikoorokia oboriri bwaito.

English: because wisdom will not enter into a soul that devises evil, nor dwell in a body that is enslaved by sin.
Ekegusii: Obong’aini tibogosoa ase omonto omong’ainereria gose ase omonyabibe.

English: For a holy spirit of discipline will flee deceit, and will depart from thoughts that are without understanding, and will be ashamed when unrighteousness has come in.
Ekegusii: Oyore omochenu nigo agwetanga korwa ase obongainereria. Omonto oyio nigo akwerusanania korwa ase ebirengererio bi’oboriri, na nigo akoba n’obwoba ekero ekeene getari gwanchwa.

English: For wisdom is a spirit who loves man, and she will not hold a blasphemer guiltless for his lips, because God is witness of his inmost self, and is a true overseer of his heart, and a hearer of his tongue.
Ekegusii: Obong’aini nigo bobwate omoyo bw’amaabera, korende tibokwabera onde bwensi orabe mamincha ya Nyasae. Nyasae namanyete ebirengererio biaito na nigo akoigwa kera ring’ana togokwana.

English: Because the spirit of the Lord has filled the world, and that which holds all things together knows what is said.
Ekegusii: Omoika bw’Omonene nigo agoichora ense yonsi na kobeka ebinto bionsi amo, na komanya kera egento bwanyabaanto agokwana.

English: Therefore no one who utters unrighteous things will be unseen; neither will Justice, when it convicts, pass him by.
Ekegusii: Onde bwensi orakwane mamincha yaye takonyara kwebisa, na ekero ekiina gekonachwa ere naegwe egesusuro kegwenerete.

English: For in his counsels the ungodly will be searched out, and the sound of his words will come to the Lord to bring his lawless deeds to conviction;
Ekegusii: Ebirengererio bi’abanyabibe mbiorokigwe maiso marore n’Omonene nanyore amang’ana a kera omonto, erio abae egesusuro kobwatekana nogokora kwabo.

English: because a jealous ear listens to all things, and the noise of murmurings is not hidden.
Ekegusii: Omonene nigo aigwete kera egento na onde taiyo orebise korwa ase are.

English: Beware then of unprofitable murmuring, and keep your tongue from slander; because no secret utterance will go on its way void, and a lying mouth destroys a soul.
Ekegusii: Ase igo eatanane korwa ase okwemurungania na tobaisa gosega abanto. Nyasae nigo akoigwa nonya n’okwemurungania kwa bobisi. Oy’ogokwana oborimo nigo agosiria omoyo oye ere omonyene.

English: Don’t court death in the error of your life. Don’t draw destruction upon yourselves by the works of your hands;
Ekegusii: Ase igo tibweretera amakweri ase engencho y’ebibe biao, gose koarigania ogosirigwa ase engencho y’ogokora kwao okobe.

English: because God didn’t make death, neither does he delight when the living perish.
Ekegusii: Amakweri tarentetwe na Nyasae, ekiagera Nyasae tari kogokera ogokwa kwa monto onde bwensi.

English: For he created all things that they might have being. The generative powers of the world are wholesome, and there is no poison of destruction in them, nor has Hades royal dominion upon earth;
Ekegusii: Nyasae nigo atongete ebitongwa bionsi bigenderere koba ao, Ime yebitongwa ebi gento kende nkiarengeo kegoita, makweri tabwate kobua ase ense eye

English: for righteousness is immortal,
Ekegusii: ekiagera ekeene kia Nyasae tikegokwa.

English: but ungodly men by their hands and their words summon death; deeming him a friend they pined away. They made a covenant with him, because they are worthy to belong with him.
Ekegusii: Korende baria batamoirogeti Nyasae nigo bakwerangereria amakweri goetera ase ogokora kwabo boigo n’amang’ana bagokwana, nigo bagokora okobwatana n’amakweri; bono barabwo mbabe abasomba b’amakweri.

English: For they said within themselves, with unsound reasoning, “Our life is short and sorrowful. There is no healing when a man comes to his end, and no one was ever known who was released from Hades.
Ekegusii: Abanyabibo nigo bakorengereria na gokwana ase chinkoro chiabo iga obogima bwaito nobwenge na obw’emechando, ekero amakweri agocha nchera teiyo toretange naro monto onde taiyo oranyare korusia oyonde ase abakure.

English: Because we were born by mere chance, and hereafter we will be as though we had never been, because the breath in our nostrils is smoke, and reason is a spark kindled by the beating of our heart,
Ekegusii: Nigo twaiboretwe ase egesio, ekero torakwe nigo erabe buna titwarenge oo riinde. Omoika oito nigo onga buna erioki rigosira, ebirengererio biato nigo bire bosa

English: which being extinguished, the body will be turned into ashes, and the spirit will be dispersed as thin air.
Ekegusii: Ekero enkoro yatigire goaka emebere yaito nigo egoonchoka yaba riibu nomoyo oito nigo ogosira buna embeo.

English: Our name will be forgotten in time. No one will remember our works. Our life will pass away as the traces of a cloud, and will be scattered as is a mist, when it is chased by the rays of the sun, and overcome by its heat.
Ekegusii: Ase ekero egeke twebwe na onde taiyo orainyore emeremo yaito, obogima bwaito mbweete buna riire gose buna ritaturi rigweta gati y’omobaso.

English: For our allotted time is the passing of a shadow, and our end doesn’t retreat, because it is securely sealed, and no one turns it back.
Ekegusii: Amagima aito nigo anga buna omorengari, na ekero torakwe titokoirana korwa aroro. Rituko ri’ogokwa gwaito nigo rirobeirie na onde taiyo oraritange.

English: “Come therefore and let’s enjoy the good things that exist. Let’s use the creation earnestly as in our youth.
Ekegusii: Ase igo tiga twegokie na kende gionsi ekiya kere ase ense, twegokie nebitongwa bionsi.

English: Let’s fill ourselves with costly wine and perfumes, and let no spring flower pass us by.
Ekegusii: Tiga tweigoti ase okonywa edivai y’erigori na manukato boigo twerigerie amaua.

English: Let’s crown ourselves with rosebuds before they wither.
Ekegusii: Twechabere amaua magega atarasusana.

English: Let none of us go without his share in our proud revelry. Let’s leave tokens of mirth everywhere, because this is our portion, and this is our lot.
Ekegusii: Kera oyomo asange ase omoyega na totige ebimanyererio bw’emegoko yaito kera ase, ekiagera obwo nabwo obogima.

English: Let’s oppress the righteous poor. Let’s not spare the widow, nor regard the gray hair of the old man.
Ekegusii: Omotaka naba omuya goika tomochande, boigo titokororera ababoraka amaabera gose gosika omogaka obwate chimbuche.

English: But let our strength be a law of righteousness; for that which is weak is proven useless.
Ekegusii: Chinguru chiaito nachio ekeorekererio gw’ekeene oyotari nechinguru tabwati kende.

English: But let’s lie in wait for the righteous man, because he annoys us, is contrary to our works, reproaches us with sins against the law, and charges us with sins against our training.
Ekegusii: Omonto omonyaboronge n’emechando ase tore, ere nigo akoba mamincha y’ayatogokora, nigo bagototogonyera ekero twasaririe amachiiko a Musa, ase igo tiga tobasirie.

English: He professes to have knowledge of God, and calls himself a child of the Lord.
Ekegusii: Omonto omuya nigo akorigia komomanya Nyasae na bweroka omwana bw’Omonene.

English: He became to us a reproof of our thoughts.
Ekegusii: Omonto onga buna oyio nigo are egetango ase tore.

English: He is grievous to us even to look at, because his life is unlike other men’s, and his paths are strange.
Ekegusii: Nonya nase okomorigereria nigo are egurube ase tore ase engencho nigo amenyete enchera engao korwa ase abanto bande.

English: We were regarded by him as something worthless, and he abstains from our ways as from uncleanness. He calls the latter end of the righteous happy. He boasts that God is his father.
Ekegusii: Ere nigo agotorora buna abanto abakorekanu na kende gionsi togokora tikeri kiya. Nigo akwerora buna Nyasae niise boigo nana kwegena buna abanyaboronge nabwo boka bagokwa bare n’omogooko.

English: Let’s see if his words are true. Let’s test what will happen at the end of his life.
Ekegusii: Bono intwe tiga torore gose amang’ana aye nayekeene, tiga torore ayaramonyore ekero arakwe.

English: For if the righteous man is God’s son, he will uphold him, and he will deliver him out of the hand of his adversaries.
Ekegusii: Onye ekeene ere n’omwana o Nyasae, Nyasae namokonye nakomorusia ase chinchera chi’ababisa baye.

English: Let’s test him with insult and torture, that we may find out how gentle he is, and test his patience.
Ekegusii: Ase igo bono tiga tomoteme tiga tomobere abatindi na kobachanda torore oberemereria bwaye.

English: Let’s condemn him to a shameful death, for he will be protected, according to his words.”
Ekegusii: Tiga tomonachere ekiina kiogokwa kw’obosoku ekiagera buna ateeba Nyasae namotorie.

English: Thus they reasoned, and they were led astray; for their wickedness blinded them,
Ekegusii: Nabo abariri bakorengereria iga korende nigo bakong’aineka ase obobe bwabo.

English: and they didn’t know the mysteries of God, neither did they hope for wages of holiness, nor did they discern that there is a prize for blameless souls.
Ekegusii: Tibamanyeti emeroberio ya Nyasae ya bobisi barabwo tibanya gotwara okogania komenya obogima obuya botari na mamocho.

English: Because God created man for incorruption, and made him an image of his own everlastingness;
Ekegusii: Nyasae nigo atongete Mwanyabaanto ase omogwekano oye omonyene bamenye kare na kare

English: but death entered into the world by the envy of the devil, and those who belong to him experience it.
Ekegusii: Korende ase engencho yendamwamu ya Saitani, ebibe bigasoa ense na bonsi baria bare ensemo ya Saitani nigo bagokwa.

English: But the souls of the righteous are in the hand of God, and no torment will touch them.
Ekegusii: Korende abanto abaronge nigo bare ase amaboko a Nyasae mechando ende yonsi tekobanyora.

English: In the eyes of the foolish they seemed to have died. Their departure was considered a disaster,
Ekegusii: Noboririri korengereria buna abanyaboronge nigo bagokwa ogokwa kw’oboriri.

English: and their travel away from us ruin, but they are in peace.
Ekegusii: Okorwao kwabo nigo kwarorekanete ase tore buna n’emechando korende ekeene abanyaboronge nigo bare n’omorembe.

English: For even if in the sight of men they are punished, their hope is full of immortality.
Ekegusii: Nigo torakagere buna nigo banyorire egesusuro, korende nigo bare n’ogosemeria gw’ogotakwa.

English: Having borne a little chastening, they will receive great good; because God tested them, and found them worthy of himself.
Ekegusii: Nigo baetwe egesusuro ake, korende bono mbaegwe ekeegwa ekenene, ekiagera Nyasae nigo abatemete akanyora buna nabo bakomenya ase are.

English: He tested them like gold in the furnace, and he accepted them as a whole burnt offering.
Ekegusii: Akabateema buna etaabu ebekire ase omorero, na akabaarigania buna ekengwanso kw’ogosambwa.

English: In the time of their visitation they will shine. They will run back and forth like sparks among stubble.
Ekegusii: Chingaki chi’okoegwa egutwa nigo bagocha komekameka buna chinsase ase obonyansi obwomo.

English: They will judge nations and have dominion over peoples. The Lord will reign over them forever.
Ekegusii: Mbagambie na kogambera chinse chionsi n’Omonene nabe omorwoti obo goika kare na kare.

English: Those who trust him will understand truth. The faithful will live with him in love, because grace and mercy are with his chosen ones.
Ekegusii: Bonsi baria bamwegenete Nyasae mbamanye ekeene kiaye; bonsi baria bare abegeeni ase are mbamenye ase are n’obwanchani, ekiagera ere nigo akobaa obuya na kobarorera amaabera abachoore baye, na nigo akobarigereria buya abwo achorire.

English: But the ungodly will be punished even as their reasoning deserves, those who neglected righteousness and revolted from the Lord;
Ekegusii: Korende abanyabibe mbaegwe egesusuro kobwatekana n’ebirengererio biabo ebibe, ekiagera barabwo nigo bangete koigwera Omonene na bagachaya gokora amaya.

English: for he who despises wisdom and discipline is miserable. Their hope is void and their toils unprofitable. Their works are useless.
Ekegusii: Bonsi baria bagochaaya obosemia gose chisemi nigo bakomenya obogima obobe; tibabwati gosemeria konde, ogwechanda kwabo tigokobakonya kende boigo n’ogokora kwabo n’okwabosa.

English: Their wives are foolish and their children are wicked.
Ekegusii: Abakungu babo nigo bare abariri na abana babo n’ababe.

English: Their descendants are cursed. For the barren woman who is undefiled is happy, she who has not conceived in transgression. She will have fruit when God examines souls.
Ekegusii: Abanto b’oroiboro rwaye mbaragererigwe. Nasesenirie omokungu omogomba oyotana gokora obotomani oyio nanyore engeria ekero Nyasae agocha kogambia chinkoro chia Mwanyabaanto.

English: So is the eunuch which has done no lawless deed with his hands, nor imagined wicked things against the Lord; for a precious gift will be given to him for his faithfulness, and a delightful inheritance in the Lord’s sanctuary.
Ekegusii: Boigo nasesenirie omosacha osaririe obosacha bwaye ekiagera ere nache kogoka onye tanya gosaria ogochika kw’Omonene. Ekiagera ere ebeete omwegenwa, nanyore ekeegwa ekiya mono ki’obogima bwa kare na kare gwetania konyora abana.

English: For good labors have fruit of great renown. The root of understanding can’t fail.
Ekegusii: Ase engencho obomaene nigo bonga omote oyio okwama amatunda y’ogokumia. Obong’aini nigo bonga obori ore moyo oyio oranyare gokinia amato amayia kera engaki.

English: But children of adulterers will not come to maturity. The seed of an unlawful union will vanish away.
Ekegusii: Abana b’abatayayi nigo barakwe bare abake boigo n’oroiboro rwabatayayi ndosirigwe kegima.

English: For if they live long, they will not be esteemed, and in the end, their old age will be without honor.
Ekegusii: Nabaisa komenya amatuko amange goika bagote, okogota kwabo nigo korabe okw’obosoku.

English: If they die young, they will have no hope, nor consolation in the day of judgment.
Ekegusii: Baise gokwa bare abasae tibakoba nagosemeria, na onde taiyo orabaremie engaki y’ekina.

English: For the end of an unrighteous generation is always grievous.
Ekegusii: Ekiagera abanto batari koigwera nigo barakoore bobe.

English: It is better to be childless with virtue, for immortality is in the memory of virtue, because it is recognized both before God and before men.
Ekegusii: Mbuya gotwara erieta rigiya kobua abana ekiagera aye noinyorwe na Nyasae n’abanto bonsi kare na kare.

English: When it is present, people imitate it. They long after it when it has departed. Throughout all time it marches, crowned in triumph, victorious in the competition for the prizes that are undefiled.
Ekegusii: Obuya bwao mboe abanto omobwekano omuya bakobwatia erio ekero orarwe oo abanto babe bagokoinyora. Kera rituko rigoeta nigo orabe gokobekerwa egutwa y’obobui.

English: But the multiplying brood of the ungodly will be of no profit, and their illegitimate offshoots won’t take deep root, nor will they establish a sure hold.
Ekegusii: Korende oroiboro rw’abaanto abange abwo batamosigeti Nyasae tibaisani kende, abana babo tibakoba n’oboroso obuya tibakoira emeri are.

English: For even if they grow branches and flourish for a season, standing unsure, they will be shaken by the wind. They will be uprooted by the violence of winds.
Ekegusii: Nabaisa kobeka amato, nigo arabe aye egeka egeke barabwo nigo baranyegerigwe n’embeo nagotogoka.

English: Their branches will be broken off before they come to maturity. Their fruit will be useless, never ripe to eat, and fit for nothing.
Ekegusii: Chinsagia chiabo nigo chirabuneke chitaraba, boigo nonya n’amatunda abo takwama ariegwe nigo arabe bosa.

English: For unlawfully conceived children are witnesses of wickedness against parents when they are investigated.
Ekegusii: Abana baiboire ase oboamate botari obuya mbabe kirori ase abaibori babo rituko ri’ekiina.

English: But a righteous man, even if he dies before his time, will be at rest.
Ekegusii: Korende abanyaboronge neisa koba bakuure nigo barabe n’omorembe.

English: For honorable old age is not that which stands in length of time, nor is its measure given by number of years,
Ekegusii: Obogotu tibori gosikwa ase engencho y’amatuko gose obonge bw’emiaka;

English: but understanding is gray hair to men, and an unspotted life is ripe old age.
Ekegusii: korende obongaini n’obogima obuya n’ekemanyererio ki’omongaini; ebi nigo bigocha n’obogotu.

English: Being found well-pleasing to God, someone was loved. While living among sinners he was transported.
Ekegusii: Narengeo omonto omogogeti Nyasae na Nyasae akamwancha, ekero amenyete gati y’abanyabibe, Nyasae akamoira igoro.

English: He was caught away, lest evil should change his understanding, or guile deceive his soul.
Ekegusii: Nigo amonganyetie erio obobe tiboonchora ebirengererio biaye gose obongainereria tibosiria omoyo oye.

English: For the fascination of wickedness obscures the things which are good, and the whirl of desire perverts an innocent mind.
Ekegusii: Omonguso bw’obobe nigo ogotuuma amaya takororekana; monto takorora nonya ingana rinde igiya bosio bwaye; omorindo bw’ ogosanera nigo ogosiria ebirengererio bi’omonto otamanyeti kende.

English: Being made perfect quickly, he filled a long time;
Ekegusii: Ere nigo akoretwe koba omochenu ase ekero egeke, erio akamenya emiaka emenge.

English: for his soul was pleasing to the Lord. Therefore he hurried out of the midst of wickedness.
Ekegusii: Omoyo oye nigo omogogetie Omonene erio akamwayereria akamorusia ase ense y’obobe. Abanto bakarora ring’ana eri korende tibamanya engencho yaye; tibamanya ring’ana eri erimo;

English: But the peoples saw and didn’t understand, not considering this, that grace and mercy are with his chosen, and that he visits his holy ones;
Ekegusii: buna Nyasae n’obuya o; omonge bw’amaabera; ere nigo akorenda baria bare abaye.

English: but a righteous man who is dead will condemn the ungodly who are living, and youth who is quickly perfected will condemn the many years of an unrighteous man’s old age.
Ekegusii: Omonto omonyaboronge oikire gokwa nagambie abwo bare moyo batamoirogeti Nyasae. Omosae oyio obeire omochenu nabasokie abanto abagotu abwo batamoirogeti Nyasae.

English: For the ungodly will see a wise man’s end, and won’t understand what the Lord planned for him, and why he safely kept him.
Ekegusii: Abanyabibe mbarore omonyaboronge ogokwa korende tibakomanya emeroberio y’Omonene ase omonto oyio, boigo tibakomanya nase ki Omonene ababekire buya.

English: They will see, and they will despise; but the Lord will laugh them to scorn. After this, they will become a dishonored carcass and a reproach among the dead forever;
Ekegusii: Mbachecherie ogokwa kw’omonyaboronge, korende Omonene nabaseke. Barabwo ekero barakwe tibagotindekwa namasikani; nonya nabakuure tibakobasika.

English: because he will dash them speechless to the ground, and will shake them from the foundations. They will lie utterly waste. They will be in anguish and their memory will perish.
Ekegusii: Omonene nabatugute inse nakobakiria kiri; nabanyegerie korwa ase oboroso bwabo erio batigare bosa nagosoka ase obororo. Monto onde taiyo arabainyore rinde.

English: They will come with coward fear when their sins are counted. Their lawless deeds will convict them to their face.
Ekegusii: Abanyabibe mbagambigwe ase obobe n’obwoba ekero ebibe biabo birabarwe, ogokora kwabo okobe nkobagambie ase obosio bwabo.

English: Then the righteous man will stand in great boldness before the face of those who afflicted him, and those who make his labors of no account.
Ekegusii: Ase rituko erio omonyaboronge natenene n’oboremu ase obosio bwa baria bare komochanda boigo na baria basiereretie emeremo yaye.

English: When they see him, they will be troubled with terrible fear, and will be amazed at the marvel of salvation.
Ekegusii: Ekero baramorore nigo baratengechigwe na koondoka mono, mbakumie mono buna atorigwe barabwo batarochi.

English: They will speak among themselves repenting, and for distress of spirit they will groan, “This was he whom we used to hold in derision, as a parable of reproach.
Ekegusii: Barabwo mbaangame nagweitia ase emioyo yabo bagoteeba,

English: We fools considered his life madness, and his end without honor.
Ekegusii: “Oyo noria tware gochecheria, tokamorora koba bosa; ekeene intwe nigo twarenge abariri. Nigo twakagerete buna ere nebarimo, na ekero akwete titwamweete masikani.

English: How was he counted among sons of God? How is his lot among saints?
Ekegusii: Inaki ekonyarekana bono ere are n’abana ba Nyasae na gotwara ribaga gati y’abachenu!

English: Truly we went astray from the way of truth. The light of righteousness didn’t shine for us. The sun didn’t rise for us.
Ekegusii: Korende intwe twangete chinchera chia boronge! Titwamenyete ase oborabu bw’ekeene, gose borabu bwaye tibwatobarerete.

English: We took our fill of the paths of lawlessness and destruction. We traveled through trackless deserts, but we didn’t know the Lord’s way.
Ekegusii: Intwe nigo twaichire n’obobe n’obosareku; nigo tware goetenana ase erooro totabwateti nchera, gose titwamanyete enchera y’Omonene.

English: What did our arrogance profit us? What good have riches and boasting brought us?
Ekegusii: Okweimokereria gwaito igoro ninki gwatokonyire? Ngeria ki twanyorire ase obonda togwetogeria?

English: Those things all passed away as a shadow, like a rumor that runs by,
Ekegusii: Ebio bionsi biaetire buna omorengari; buna egento okoigwa naende kweba.

English: like a ship passing through the billowy water, which, when it has gone by, there is no trace to be found, no pathway of its keel in the waves.
Ekegusii: Buna emeri ekwamereria emerindo nyancha, korende ekero yaetire teri gotiga nchera, gose tokobwatia orore ase yaetera gati gati yemerindo.

English: Or it is like when a bird flies through the air, no evidence of its passage is found, but the light wind, lashed with the stroke of its pinions, and torn apart with the violent rush of the moving wings, is passed through. Afterwards no sign of its coming remains.
Ekegusii: Gose buna enyoni ekoiruruka ase embeo etari gotiga kemanyererio kende gionsi ase egoetera; ero nigo egoaka aka embeo inke inke ase chimbaba chiaye, ero nigo egoeta ase embeo korende teri gotiga kemanyererio ase yaetire.

English: Or it is like when an arrow is shot at a mark, the air it divided closes up again immediately, so that men don’t know where it passed through.
Ekegusii: Boigo nonya nensara ekero yarutirwe nigo egoeta ase embeo korende teri gotiga enchera ase embeo, gose monto onde tokomanya ase yaetera.

English: So we also, as soon as we were born, ceased to be; and we had no sign of virtue to show, but we were utterly consumed in our wickedness.”
Ekegusii: Boigo naitwe magega kotwaiboirwe, nigo togosira na titori gotiga kemanyererio kende ki’obuya, korende nigo togosira ase obobe bwaito intwe abanyene.”

English: Because the hope of the ungodly man is like chaff carried by the wind, and as foam vanishing before a tempest; and is scattered like smoke by the wind, and passes by as the remembrance of a guest who stays just a day.
Ekegusii: Ogosemeria kw’omonyabibe nigo konga buna embeo; nigo konga buna riuro rikoirwa n’emerindo; nigo rigwatananwa buna erioki bosio bw’embeo, rigoeta nagotainyorwa buna omogeni bwe rituko erimo.

English: But the righteous live forever. Their reward is in the Lord, and the care for them with the Most High.
Ekegusii: Korende abanto abaya nigo bakomenya kare na kare nengeria yabo nigo ere ase Omonene; ee Nyasae Omonene nere okobaakana.

English: Therefore they will receive the crown of royal dignity and the diadem of beauty from the Lord’s hand, because he will cover them with his right hand, and he will shield them with his arm.
Ekegusii: Ase igo barabwo mbanyore engeria eng’ikeranu n’egutwa ekomekameka ase okoboko kw’Omonene, ekiagera ere nabatube ase okoboko kwaye gw’okorio na kobakengera okoboko kwaye gw’echinguru.

English: He will take his zeal as complete armor, and will make the whole creation his weapons to punish his enemies:
Ekegusii: Omonene naorokie obwanchani bwaye obonene buna ebirwanero bi’esegi erio aboyie abanto baye barwanie ababisa baye.

English: He will put on righteousness as a breastplate, and will wear impartial judgment as a helmet.
Ekegusii: Ekeene nkebe buna engoba y’egekuba, okogaambigwa gw’ekeene nkobe buna ekegogwa kia motwe.

English: He will take holiness as an invincible shield.
Ekegusii: Obochenu mbobe buna enguba yaye.

English: He will sharpen stern wrath for a sword. The universe will go with him to fight against his frenzied foes.
Ekegusii: Natieri endamwamu yaye enene buna omoro, na ense yonsi nebwaterane nere korwania ababisa abwo batabwati semi.

English: Shafts of lightning will fly with true aim. They will leap to the mark from the clouds, as from a well-drawn bow.
Ekegusii: Enkoba neche rimo rioka igoro ase amare buna chinsara korwa ase obota.

English: Hailstones full of wrath will be hurled as from a catapult. The water of the sea will be angered against them. Rivers will sternly overwhelm them.
Ekegusii: Embura y’amagena nebachere buna chinsara n’eritimo; amacha anyancha nache ase obororo ase engencho yabo, nechindoche nchibasiri chitari n’mabera.

English: A mighty wind will encounter them. It will winnow them away like a tempest. So lawlessness will make all the land desolate. Their evil-doing will overturn the thrones of princes.
Ekegusii: Embeo entindi neche ase engencho yabo, nakobairurukia gochia are buna ekembugambugu. Obone mborete ogosira ense yonsi; ogokora okobe nkonyegeri abanene b’ense.

English: Hear therefore, you kings, and understand. Learn, you judges of the ends of the earth.
Ekegusii: Tegerera inwe abarwoti moigwe, inwe abagaambi be’ense yonsi maya aya.

English: Give ear, you rulers who have dominion over many people, and make your boast in multitudes of nations,
Ekegusii: Integerere inwe aba mokogambera emeganda ya’banto n kwegokia ase chinse chionsi.

English: because your dominion was given to you from the Lord, and your sovereignty from the Most High. He will search out your works, and will inquire about your plans,
Ekegusii: Obonene more nabwo nigo mwaetwe n’Omonene; boigo n’okobua gwonsi nigo mwakonyorete ase Nyasae Omonene. Ere narenge emeremo yaino na koringoria emeroberio yaino.

English: because being officers of his kingdom, you didn’t judge rightly, nor did you keep the law, nor did you walk according to God’s counsel.
Ekegusii: Ekiagera buna abakoreri ase oborwoti bwaye, tibwagambete buya, onye timokobwatia amachiiko, gose kobwatia emeroberio ya Nyasae;

English: He will come upon you awfully and swiftly, because a stern judgment comes on those who are in high places.
Ekegusii: nabachere ng’ora na kobaa egesusuro egetindi, ekiagera egesusuro egetindi nigo kogochera baria bare nokobua.

English: For the man of low estate may be pardoned in mercy, but mighty men will be mightily tested.
