Ekegusii: Tobaisa goteeba Ng’a: “Ninki nganetie naende? Gose, Ninki ndanyore ase engaki egochia gocha?”

English: For it is an easy thing in the sight of the Lord to reward a man in the day of death according to his ways.
Ekegusii: Naende, toteeba ng’a: “Ninde na kera egento eki gekong’isanekia. Mbokong’u ki Mbwate ntanyare, gose borambue?”

English: The affliction of an hour causes delights to be forgotten. In the end, a man’s deeds are revealed.
Ekegusii: Ekero ebinto bitari buya, abanto nigo bakweba, mbari korengereria ng’a chingaki nchireo chinkong’u, n’engaki y’emechando onde taiyo okoinyora amagenderero.

English: Call no man happy before his death. A man will be known in his children.
Ekegusii: Nyasae nabo araganye goika engaki twakure, ekero gi’ekina kera oyomo aragambigwe koreng’ana n’amakora aye,

English: Don’t bring every man into your house, for many are the tricks of a deceitful man.
Ekegusii: engaki enyeng’e igo omonto akwebera omogooko oye, erio omonto nigo rirorio akomanyekana buna are ekero ere aikire omoerio bw’obogima bwaye,

English: Like a decoy partridge in a cage, so is the heart of a proud man. Like a spy, he looks for your weakness.
Ekegusii: na mbuya omonto atarakwa, ekiagera amaroro onsi nigo akorentwa ekero omonto akure,

English: For he lies in wait to turn things that are good into evil, and assigns blame in things that are praiseworthy.
Ekegusii: toigwera onde obororo ase nyomba mwao; ekiagera emetego y’abanto abanyaborimo n’emenge.

English: From a spark of fire, a heap of many coals is kindled, and a sinful man lies in wait to shed blood.
Ekegusii: Omonto omwerori nigo anga buna ekebekerero gekobekwa maiso marore, buna omotuki bw’amang’ana, erinde oyatuka ase okworokia oboreu bwaye.

English: Take heed of an evil-doer, for he plans wicked things, lest perhaps he ruin your reputation forever.
Ekegusii: Omonto oyio nigo akoonchora amang’ana amaya koba amabe, na korora obobe ase ayare amaya.

English: Receive a stranger into your house, and he will distract you with arguments and estrange you from your own family.
Ekegusii: Ensase eyemo y’omorero nabo egwokia

English: If you do good, know to whom you do it, and your good deeds will have thanks.
Ekegusii: Onye gotagete gokora amaya chora omonto ogokorera; erio naye n’osesenigwe ase amaya ao.

English: Do good to a godly man, and you will find a reward— if not from him, then from the Most High.
Ekegusii: Kora amaya ase omonto omoirogete Nyasae naye n’osesenigwe; naye n’otogigwe n’omonto oyio, gose n’Omonene.

English: No good will come to him who continues to do evil, nor to him who gives no alms.
Ekegusii: Kende kiya nkeiyo kerarwe ase omonto ogendererete gokora amabe, gose omonto otari korua ekengwanso.

English: Give to the godly man, and don’t help the sinner.
Ekegusii: Koonya abanto baria bamoirogete Nyasae, korende, tiga gokoonya abanyabibe.

English: Do good to one who is lowly. Don’t give to an ungodly man. Keep back his bread, and don’t give it to him, lest he subdue you with it; for you would receive twice as much evil for all the good you would have done to him.
Ekegusii: Kora amaya ase abaitongo korende, tiga kobaa kende gionsi ase abanto baria batamoirogetii Nyasae. Abanto buna abwo tobaisa kobaa ndagera ende yonsi, ekiagera endegera eyio nigo eragere bakoiyerie korwa ase ekerogo kiao, naye bono n’oakanwe n’obobe ara kabere.

English: For the Most High also hates sinners, and will repay vengeance to the ungodly.
Ekegusii: Nonya ’Omonene nigo agechete abanyabibe. Nere n’abae egesusuro abatamoirogetie.

English: Give to the good man, and don’t help the sinner.
Ekegusii: Omonto ore omuya moe ekia aganetie, korende toa omonyabibe.

English: A man’s friend won’t be fully tried in prosperity. His enemy won’t be hidden in adversity.
Ekegusii: Nigo ere akong’u kegima komanya ng’a ning’o omosani na kegima ekero ebinto bire buya, korende ekero kiobokong’u nigo ere aororo komanya omobisa oo.

English: In a man’s prosperity, his enemies are grieved. In his adversity, even his friend leaves.
Ekegusii: Ekero omonto asesenigwe, abasani baye nigo bakoba n’obororo mono kegima. Nonya nabo, ekero ki’obokong’u nonya n’abasani baye abanyene nigo bakomotama.

English: Never trust your enemy, for his wickedness is like corrosion in copper.
Ekegusii: Tobaisa kweba erio bwegene omobisa oo; obobe bwaye nigo bonga obobosu ase gento kende gionsi.

English: Though he humbles himself and walks bowed down, still be careful and beware of him. You will be to him as one who has wiped a mirror, to be sure it doesn’t completely tarnish.
Ekegusii: Nonya noria ogwekeeyia na gotugama bosio bwao, erende ase amabe aye. Omonto buna oyio nigo anga buna ekerore kiabosiire onye tikeri kogenderera kona gosibigwa.

English: Don’t set him next to you, lest he overthrow you and stand in your place. Don’t let him sit on your right hand, lest he seek to take your seat, and at the last you acknowledge my words, and be pricked with my sayings.
Ekegusii: Tiga kobeka omobisa ang’e naye, ekiagera nigo akogoonchora na gokobeka aase otagwenereti. Tobaisa komoikaransia ase okoboko kwao gwokorio, ekiagera nigo araire egento kiao kiamasikani, erio nario oramomanye obomaene kegima buna omonto oyio are. Erio ng’a bweitie ase ayio nagotebirie.

English: Who will pity a charmer that is bitten by a snake, or any who come near wild beasts?
Ekegusii: Omonto karabe ogokora echeche n’eng’iti engenda inse na keramorome na ero, gose ching’iti chinde chi’orosana chintindi; tomororera amaabera!

English: Even so, who will pity him who goes to a sinner, and is associated with him in his sins?
Ekegusii: Ase igo, monto taiyo oramorore amaabera.

English: For a while he will stay with you, and if you falter, he will not stay.
Ekegusii: Omonyene ebibe nakwane ng’a naye, korende gokonyorwa n’emechando nigo akogotama ogotiga gochia abwo igo.

English: The enemy will speak sweetly with his lips, and in his heart plan to throw you into a pit. The enemy may weep with his eyes, but if he finds opportunity, he will want more blood.
Ekegusii: Omobisa oo nigo aragokwanere n’amang’ana amaya mono kegima, korende ase omoyo oye ime nigo agendererete koroberia akonyore engoro ime. Omobisa oo nigo akorera amariga amange, korende aise konyora ribaga iga, na sirie obogima bwao.

English: If adversity meets you, you will find him there before you. Pretending to help you, he will trip you.
Ekegusii: Oise konyorwa n’obokong’u, nagwo okomonyora okoganyete, okwebonia ng’a nkogokonya are, na anii, nigo aroberetie kogokoora kegima.

English: He will shake his head, clap his hands, whisper much, and change his countenance.
Ekegusii: Omonto nasingisie omotwe na goaka chinkobi, namonyererwe amange erio aonchoke na koba omonto omoao kegima.

English: He who touches pitch will be defiled. He who has fellowship with a proud man will become like him.
Ekegusii: Monto onde bwensi ogokuna eramu nigo agwetiringa, n’oyo okobwaterana n’omonto omwerori. Nigo akobweka.

English: Don’t take up a burden above your strength. Have no fellowship with one who is mightier and richer than yourself. What fellowship would the earthen pot have with the kettle? The kettle will strike, and the pot will be dashed in pieces.
Ekegusii: Tibwancha kobogoria egurube ebuete chinguru chiao, tobaisa kobwaterana n’omonto omonyanguru, gose omonto omotenenku. Enyongo erosirie korwa ase amoroba naki eranyarekane ebwaterane n’ebirika eroiserie echuma? Enyongo eye amo n’ebirika bise gotwomana, n’enyongo erateke.

English: The rich man does a wrong and threatens. The poor is wronged and apologizes.
Ekegusii: Omonto omotenenku nigo akomochia omonto naende omenta koongora. Korende omotaka ko agoseire omonto, nigo akobeterereka gosaba amabera.

English: If you are profitable, he will exploit you. If you are in need, he will forsake you.
Ekegusii: Omonto omotenenku nigo akororera abataka emeremo ngaki ende yonsi arooche ng’a nanyore eng’eria korwa ase ore. Korende ekero aye otagete ere agokoonye nigo akogotiga gochia agwo igo.

English: If you own something, he will live with you. He will drain your resources and will not be sorry.
Ekegusii: Omotenenku oyio akorore kore n’egento nigo agokoberera ang’e, na onagosakora ebinto biao ng’ora-ng’ora goika obikoora kegima. Atari n’amaabera.

English: Does he need you? Then he will deceive you, smile at you, and give you hope. He will speak kindly to you and say, “What do you need?”
Ekegusii: Ekero omonto oyio are na kogania konde gwonsi nigo agokong’aina, nigo akogosekera erio okoa ogosemeria. Ekero akoboria egento nigo akoboria n’obwororo kegima: “Noganetie kende?”

English: He will shame you by his delicacies until he has made you bare twice or thrice, and in the end he will laugh you to scorn. Afterward he will see you, will forsake you, and shake his head at you.
Ekegusii: Ekero agokoarigania ase endagera yaye, nigo arabaisa gokoa obosooku. Ekero akourire egento ara kabere gatato iga, igo akogosekerera. Oise kogenda komorora omonto oyio ng’ora nigo agwekora buna takomanyeti, erio osingisia omotwe na gokana kegima.

English: Beware that you are not deceived and brought low in your enjoyment.
Ekegusii: Renda tobaisa gosirigwa, na koegwa obosooku ase omoyega oo.

English: If a mighty man invites you, be reserved, and he will invite you more.
Ekegusii: Onye gwachikirwe n’omonto bw’amasikani, kabe omonto bw’omoroberio; erio nario aragochiike naende.

English: Don’t press him, lest you be thrust back. Don’t stand far off, lest you be forgotten.
Ekegusii: Tiga kw’eira ase omoyega bw’omonto n’endamwamu, ekiagera nigo orabaisa goserigwa. Korende, naende oise komobeera are nigo agokweba.

English: Don’t try to speak with him as an equal, and don’t believe his many words; for he will test you with much talk, and will examine you in a smiling manner.
Ekegusii: Tiga kwereng’ania nere, gose kwegena amang’ana aye amaang’e. Ekiagera nigo oranyore ngoteema are ase amang’ana aye amaange, erio agosekerere ase okona kogoitona.

English: He who doesn’t keep secrets to himself is unmerciful. He won’t hesitate to harm and to bind.
Ekegusii: Omonto otari kogacha obobisi nigo anga buna omoiti. Takoganya kogokorera bobe gose gokosiba enkendu ime

English: Keep them to yourself and be careful, for you walk in danger of falling.
Ekegusii: Renda obobisi bwao na mbuya kwerenda, ekiagera nigo ogatara ase amakweri.

English: Every living creature loves its own kind, and every man loves his neighbor.
Ekegusii: Kera egetongwa nigo kegwancha egetongwa kende gekebwekaine, naboigo Mwanyabaanto nigo agwancha Mwanyabaanto omwabo.

English: All flesh associates with their own kind. A man will stick to people like himself.
Ekegusii: Bitongire binde bionsi nigo bire n’oboamate n’ebitongire biamwabo, n’omonto nere otwara oboamate n’omobwekaine oye.

English: What fellowship would the wolf have with the lamb? So is the sinner to the godly.
Ekegusii: Esese y’orosana n’emanwa yeng’ondi mboamate ki bibwate? Nigo ere akong’u mono; ase enchera buna eyio, nigo ere akong’u omonyabibe kobwaterana gati yomonyabibe amo n’omonto omoirogete Nyasae.

English: What peace is there between a hyena and a dog? What peace is there between a rich man and the poor?
Ekegusii: Inee, omorembe nore gati y’enyang’au n’esese? Naende, inee, omorembe nore gati y’omonda amo n’omotaka?

English: Wild donkeys are the prey of lions in the wilderness; likewise poor men are feeding grounds for the rich.
Ekegusii: Rigwari nigo rire ogotwara kw’endo; naboigo omotaka nigo are oborisia bw’abatenenku.

English: Lowliness is an abomination to a proud man; likewise a poor man is an abomination to the rich.
Ekegusii: Okogechia igo okogechia okonene mono ase omonto omwerori, ase enchera eyio eyio, omotaka igo kore okogechia gochia ase omotenenku.

English: When a rich man is shaken, he is supported by his friends, but when the humble is down, he is pushed away even by his friends.
Ekegusii: Ekero omonto omonda akogochwa nigo agosiirwa n’abasani baye, korende omotaka aise kogwa abasani baye nigo bakomotama.

English: When a rich man falls, there are many helpers. He speaks things not to be spoken, and men justify him. A humble man falls, and men rebuke him. He utters wisdom, and is not listened to.
Ekegusii: Omontenenku akore amamocho, abanto bakomokoonya nigo bakoba abange kegima; ng’a nonya n’ekero agokwana amang’ana ataisaini, ayio nigo akoba buna enguba asare. Ko bono omotaka aise komocha, agwo-agwo nigo bakomotogonyera; naisa gokwana n’echisemi, onde taiyo okomoigwa ng’a nareo.

English: A rich man speaks, and all keep silence. They extol what he says to the clouds. A poor man speaks, and they say, “Who is this?” If he stumbles, they will help to overthrow him.
Ekegusii: Omotenenku aise gokwana, abanto bonsi nigo bagokira kiri. Abanto nigo bagotogia enkwano yaye gochia amare igoro; tiga bono omonto omotaka akwane, abanto bonsi bana goteeba iga: “N’oyio nere ning’o?” Ekero omotaka akogochwa, abanto nigo bakomotwomerania gochi inse.

English: Riches are good if they have no sin. Poverty is evil only in the opinion of the ungodly.
Ekegusii: Obotenenku n’obuya mono ekero botabwataini n’ekebe. Obotaka n’obobe ase baria batamomanyeti Nyasae.

English: The heart of a man changes his countenance, whether it is for good or for evil.
Ekegusii: Keria kere ime y’omonto nakio gekororekana isiko y’omonto.

English: A cheerful countenance is a sign of a prosperous heart. Devising proverbs takes strenuous thinking.
Ekegusii: Obosio bosasogete nigo bore ekemanyererio ki’omogooko ase omoyo, nabo okorekana kore n’omogooko. Korende, oyo ogotegora emebayeno eye goika abe omong’aini.

English: Blessed is the man who has not slipped with his mouth, and doesn’t suffer from sorrow for sins.
Ekegusii: Omonto otari komocha ase oromeme rwaye; tagwenereti gokumia ekiagera onarire ayio ng’a omochire.

English: Blessed is he whose soul does not condemn him, and who has not given up hope.
Ekegusii: Amarimu aye tari komogambia ekiina na tari gosiria ogosemeria, amaene nigo agotogigwa oria otararusia moyo

English: Riches are not appropriate for a stingy person. What would a miser do with money?
Ekegusii: bwomochayi koba ang’e gochaka. Obotenenku ninki boisaine onye omonto ore omwegimeria?

English: He who gathers by denying himself gathers for others. Others will revel in his goods.
Ekegusii: Onye akwerina, igo ere nigo akonibera abanto bande? Erio abwo bakoira omwando nigo bagosiakeria enibo eyio ase okwegokia.

English: If one is mean to himself, to whom will he be good? He won’t enjoy his possessions.
Ekegusii: Oyio omonyene enibo, nigo arabe omoitongo ase ng’o, n’onye tari kwegokia ere omonyene?

English: There is none more evil than he who is grudging to himself. This is a punishment for his wickedness.
Ekegusii: Monto tari ore omobe kobua omonto okweng’itiera ere omunyene.

English: Even if he does good, he does it in forgetfulness. In the end, he reveals his wickedness.
Ekegusii: Ekero akorire egento ekiya, nigo akogekora mosiabano, ase igo bworokia buna are omoriri ere omonyene.

English: A miser is evil. He turns away and disregards souls.
Ekegusii: Omonto ore n’endamwamu oyio n’omoriri; nigo akorigereria ’nse ase ogosiereria abande,

English: A covetous man’s eye is not satisfied with his portion. Wicked injustice dries up his soul.
Ekegusii: oyio naende otari goisaneka n’ekio are nakio, n’ogochaaya okwo nigo kogosaria omoyo bw’omonto.

English: A miser begrudges bread, and it is lacking at his table.
Ekegusii: Abanto bande nigo bare abang’iti mono ase ogotereka endagera emesa;

English: My son, according to what you have, treat yourself well, and bring worthy offerings to the Lord.
Ekegusii: ase igo ebinto biao tibikonyara kogoisanekia buna egwenerete, korende morue ekengwanso keria keganeirie.

English: Remember that death will not wait, and that the covenant of Hades hasn’t been shown to you.
Ekegusii: Inyora ng’a amakweri tari koganya, ngocha are engaki ende yonsi, nonya rituko tirimanyekaneti ekero orakwe.

English: Do good to your friends before you die. According to your ability, reach out and give to them.
Ekegusii: Kora aya are amaronge otarachia gokwa; kabe omoitongo, na moe buna okonyara kwao kore.

English: Don’t deprive yourself of a good day. Don’t let your share of a desired good pass you by.
Ekegusii: Tibwerina omogooko nonya nerituko erimo. Tobaisa gotiga ensemo yao y’omogooko eyio ere enchera yogokogwenia.

English: Won’t you leave your labors to another, and your toils be divided by lot?
Ekegusii: Rituko erimo n’obatigere abanto bande eng’eria y’ebigeri biao; enibo yao yonsi eyio kwarigirie n’ebigeri biao negabanwe ase ogoaka ekura.

English: Give, take, and treat yourself well, because there is no seeking of luxury in Hades.
Ekegusii: Ase Igo karue ekio obwate ase abande, erio bwegokie kore moyo. Korende, naende ancha koegwa, ekiagera tokwegokia ase abakuure.

English: All flesh grows old like a garment, for the covenant from the beginning is, “You must die!”
Ekegusii: Omobere o Mwanyabaanto nigo okogota buna eanga, ekiagera korwa kare omobere: “Goika okwe.”

English: Like the leaves flourishing on a thick tree, some it sheds, and some grow, so also are the generations of flesh and blood: one comes to an end and another is born.
Ekegusii: Buna omote omonene oichire n’amato are machani, erio make aaroroka erinde ayande naende aseboka; nabo mwanyanto are igo, ase omobere n’amanyinga aye: oyomo nigo agokwa, naende oyonde oiborwa.

English: Every work rots and falls away, and its builder will depart with it.
Ekegusii: Kende gionsi kerosirie nigo gekogota erio gesira, n’oyo ogokerosia nere osira n’emeremo yaye boigo.

English: Blessed is the man who meditates on wisdom, and who reasons by his understanding.
Ekegusii: Omonto okorengereria bweka naende ore n’obong’aini nere bweka oraikeere ayio.

English: He who considers her ways in his heart will also have knowledge of her secrets.
Ekegusii: Onde bwensi ogosoma ase enchera y’echisemi naende oyokorengereria igoro y’obobisi bwekerengerio kiaye.

English: Go after her like a hunter, and lie in wait in her paths.
Ekegusii: Rigia chisemi koreng’ana buna omotwari akorigia na koganyerera ase chinchera na koganyerera.

English: He who peers in at her windows will also listen at her doors.
Ekegusii: Rigereria gochia ase chitirisa chi’echisemi.

English: He who lodges close to her house will also fasten a nail in her walls.
Ekegusii: Chisemi nigo chire buna omonto okobera aang’e n’enyomba yaye, erio osiba eema yaye ase ekeroochi na koyesiba ase enyasi y’enyomba eyio yaye.

English: He will pitch his tent near at hand to her, and will lodge in a lodging where good things are.
Ekegusii: Eema yaye aang’e nere erio oikaransa ase egeikaro kiaye egetoereru.

English: He will set his children under her shelter, and will rest under her branches.
Ekegusii: Nigo akobeka abana baye

English: By her he will be covered from heat, and will lodge in her glory.
Ekegusii: ekiriri eki gekomokengera omogaso, nere oikaransa n’obotoereru bwaye.

English: He who fears the Lord will do this. He who has possession of the law will obtain her.
Ekegusii: Omonto omoirogete Nyasae, omonto obwatete ebirage biaye n’amonyore chisemi.

English: She will meet him like a mother, and receive him like a wife married in her virginity.
Ekegusii: Ere chisemi n’akwariganie buna omokungu omonyanyangi akoarigania omonywomi.

English: She will feed him with bread of understanding and give him water of wisdom to drink.
Ekegusii: Nyasae nakoe obong’aini buna omonto akoegwa endagera amo n’ekenyugwa.

English: He will be stayed upon her, and will not be moved. He will rely upon her, and will not be confounded.
Ekegusii: Omonto n’agamerere chisemi erio chimokoonye tagwa erinde anyore obosooku.

English: She will exalt him above his neighbors. She will open his mouth in the midst of the congregation.
Ekegusii: Ere chisemi nakoimokererie igoro kobua abaamate bao; n’ekero ogokwana gati-gati y’abanto ere chisemi nakoe ekio orakwane.

English: He will inherit joy, a crown of gladness, and an everlasting name.
Ekegusii: Ase chisemi aye n’onyore omogooko n’omogooko bw’ekeene, erio erieta riao ng’a riinyorwe goika kare na kare.

English: Foolish men will not obtain her. Sinners will not see her.
Ekegusii: Korende, abanto abariri amo n’abanyabibe tibakonyora chisemi.

English: She is far from pride. Liars will not remember her.
Ekegusii: Chisemi nigo chire aare korwa abanto aberori; chisemi tichigosoa ase ebirengererio biabang’ainereria.

English: Praise is not attractive in the mouth of a sinner; for it was not sent to him from the Lord.
Ekegusii: Omonyabibe tagwenereti goteera amateera yokomotogia Nyasae, ekiagera ogosasiima kwaye tikori korwa enkoro yaye ime.

English: For praise will be spoken in wisdom; The Lord will prosper it.
Ekegusii: Amateera goika abe ekemanyererio gi’echisemi. Ekio gegokong’usa gochia ase Nyasae.

English: Don’t say, “It is through the Lord that I fell away;” for you shall not do the things that he hates.
Ekegusii: Tiga gotaamera ng’a: Nyasae ogera namocha. Naki aragere okore ekebe nere ogechete ekebe?

English: Don’t say, “It is he that caused me to err;” for he has no need of a sinful man.
Ekegusii: Tobaisa goteeba ng’a Nyasae nere ogerire, ekiagera ere taganetie ogokoonya kwomonyabibe.

English: The Lord hates every abomination; and those who fear him don’t love them.
Ekegusii: Nyasae nigo angete okogecha gwonsi. Nonya mbaria bamoirogete Nyasae nigo bayangete ayio.

English: He himself made man from the beginning and left him in the hand of his own counsel.
Ekegusii: Agwo ritang’ani kegima, Omonene nere otongete mwanyabaanto, akamoa obosibore bw’ogwechorera amang’ana aye ereomonyene.

English: If you choose, you can keep the commandments. To be faithful is a matter of your choice.
Ekegusii: Onye koganetie, nabo okoigwera ebirage bia Nyasae, erio omenye ase okwegena gose ochore buna origetie.

English: He has set fire and water before you. You will stretch forth your hand to whichever you desire.
Ekegusii: Omonene obekire bosio bwao omorero amo n’amache: rambora okoboko kwao, bwechorere keria oganeti.

English: Before man is life and death. Whichever he likes, it will be given to him.
Ekegusii: Mwanyabaanto obekeirwe bosio bwaye obogima amo n’amakweri; ase ebio bibere, keria agochora nakio akoegwa.

English: For the wisdom of the Lord is great. He is mighty in power, and sees all things.
Ekegusii: Chisemi chia Nyasae n’echinene kegima; ere nigo abwate chinguru chi’obomanyi bwa kera egento.

English: His eyes are upon those who fear him. He knows every act of man.
Ekegusii: Omonene nigo arigereretie ase obuya; ere nigo amanyete aya Mwanyabaanto agokora.

English: He has not commanded any man to be ungodly. He has not given any man license to sin.
Ekegusii: Chisemi tichianya kobetereria monto onde bwensi komoiroka Nyasae, gose gochika onde gokora ekebe.

English: Don’t desire a multitude of unprofitable children, neither delight in ungodly sons.
Ekegusii: Toba n’okogania gotwara abana abange batari n’engencho asore; gose kwerorera abana abamura batamoirogeti Nyasae.

English: If they multiply, don’t delight in them unless the fear of the Lord is in them.
Ekegusii: Nonya kobwate abana abaange mbosa onye mbamoirogeti Nyasae.

English: Don’t trust in their life. Don’t rely on their numbers; for one can be better than a thousand, and to die childless than to have ungodly children.
Ekegusii: Abana buna abwo, tobeeka ogosemeria kwao ase bare; abange babo tobaisa gosemeria ase bare. Ekiagera omwana oyomo nigo are omuya kobua abana elifu batari nagokoonya asore. Ase engencho ende, mbuya nokwa otari namwana kobua gotwara abana batamoirogeti Nyasae.

English: For from one who has understanding, a city will be populated, but a race of wicked men will be made desolate.
Ekegusii: Enka ya abanto nabo egokiina ase chisemi chia omonto oyomo, ko bono, egeku ekegima ki’abaanto batari n’erichiko nabo ogotigara bosa.

English: I have seen many such things with my eyes. My ear has heard mightier things than these.
Ekegusii: Amoiso ane arorire amang’ana amange buna aya; n’amato ane ategereire amang’ana amange y’ogokumia kobua ayio.

English: In a congregation of sinners, a fire will be kindled. In a disobedient nation, wrath is kindled.
Ekegusii: Omorero n’outwe gati y’erisango ri’abaanto abanyabibe, gose obororo ng’a boitekere abaenenu.

English: He was not pacified toward the giants of old time, who revolted in their strength.
Ekegusii: Nyasae Taaberete amamonto aria akare ayio egenete chinguru chiabo erio akagenda mamincha yaye.

English: He didn’t spare Lot’s neighbors, whom he abhorred for their pride.
Ekegusii: Nyasae tarorerete eamate ya Loti amaabera; baria agechetigwe n’obwerori bwabo.

English: He didn’t pity the people of perdition who were taken away in their sins,
Ekegusii: Nyasae taorogeti maabera egesaku keria kiare gochia gosirigwa, egesaku keria giatinyeretigwe inse okoba ebibe biaye,

English: or in like manner, the six hundred thousand footmen who were gathered together in the hardness of their hearts.
Ekegusii: nonya omoganda oria bw’abasikari chielifu amagana atano narimo b’amagoro abwo basangererekanete ase aamo, bakaenenera Nyasae ase obwerori bwabo.

English: Even if there is one stiff-necked person, it is a marvel if he will be unpunished; for mercy and wrath are both with him who is mighty to forgive, and he pours out wrath.
Ekegusii: Nonya ere ng’a nomonto oyomo ore omwerori, nigo erabe ogokumia mono onye oyio takoegwa egesusuro.

English: As his mercy is great, so is his correction also. He judges a man according to his works.
Ekegusii: Ekiagera egesusuro kia Nyasae n’ekeroro buna koreng’ana n’amaabera aye.

English: The sinner will not escape with plunder. The perseverance of the godly will not be frustrated.
Ekegusii: Ere nigo akogambia kera omonto n’ogokora kwaye. Na ogosemeria gwokomoiroka Nyasae tikori okwabosa.

English: He will make room for every work of mercy. Each man will receive according to his works.
Ekegusii: Omonto omwegenwa nanyore aya amogwenerete koreng’ana n’amakora aye.

English: Don’t say, “I will be hidden from the Lord,” and “Who will remember me from on high?” I will not be known among so many people, for what is my soul in a boundless creation?
Ekegusii: Tobaisa goteeba ng’a: Ninyebise aare korwa ase Nyasae; erio niinyebise aase onde atanyoore gose kong’inyora! Ninyebisa ase abanto bare abange igo tinkororekana, ekiagera ribaga riane ninki ase ebitongire bitari n’omobaro.

English: Behold, heaven, the heaven of heavens, the deep, and the earth, will be moved when he visits.
Ekegusii: Ama bono, igoro ya igoro kegima, omosunte n’omobaso, ebio bionsi ng’a biteengechigwe ekero Nyasae arachiche.

English: The mountains and the foundations of the earth together are shaken with trembling when he looks at them.
Ekegusii: Ebitunwa amo n’oboroso bw’ense mbitengeche ekero Nyasae arabirigererie.

English: No heart will think about these things. Who could comprehend his ways?
Ekegusii: Korende Mwanyabaanto taiyo orengereretie ayio; niing’o oranyare komanya chinchera chia Nyasae?

English: Like a tempest which no man can see, so, the majority of his works are hidden.
Ekegusii: Tobaisa goteeba ng’a: Niinsa gokora ekebe onde taiyo ondoche. Niinkora igo bobisi kegima ning’o oramanye?

English: Who will declare his works of righteousness? Who will wait for them? For his covenant is afar off.
Ekegusii: Naende, ninkora amaya ning’o orayatore? Ning’o mokorengia oraganye erio atebigwe amageni? Ere nigo akoganya mono aikeranie egetebanio kiaye.

English: He who is lacking in understanding thinks about these things. An unwise and erring man thinks foolishly.
Ekegusii: Naboigo ase omonto okorengereria ime yaye; omonto omoriri osiriigwe nabo akorengereria ase oboriri bwaye.

English: My son, listen to me, learn knowledge, and heed my words with your heart.
Ekegusii: Omwana one, ntegerere erio onyore obong’aini. Tega ogoto erio otegerere amang’ana ane.

English: I will impart instruction with precision, and declare knowledge exactly.
Ekegusii: Niinkoe chisemi chindito naende nkworokererie obong’aini boria bogoisaine.

English: In the judgment of the Lord are his works from the beginning. From the making of them he determined their boundaries.
Ekegusii: Ekero Nyasae akorete emeremo y’ogotonga agwo ritang’ani kegima, nigo abagete kera egento ase omoroberio.

English: He arranged his works for all time, and their beginnings to their generations. They aren’t hungry or weary, and they don’t cease from their works.
Ekegusii: Erio Nyasae akaa kera egetongwa omoroberio goika kare na kare kera ekemo ase omoroberio oyio. Korwa agwo goika reero iga kera ekemo nkeremeiri kobwata omoroberio oye.

English: No one pushes aside his neighbor. They will never disobey his word.
Ekegusii: Kende nkeiyo nonya n’ekemo kegotwomana n’ekende, na kera egento kiaigwera Nyasae.

English: After this also the Lord looked at the earth and filled it with his blessings.
Ekegusii: Magega yayio, ekero Nyasae akorire aya onsi, akayerigereria ense akayeichoria n’ebinto biaye ebiya.

English: All manner of living things covered its surface, and they return into it.
Ekegusii: Nigo atubete ense nebitongwa bia kera engencho, ebio bigokwa na koirana ase riroba.

English: The Lord created mankind out of earth, and turned them back to it again.
Ekegusii: Nyasae nigo atongete Mwanyabaanto korwa ase amaroba, naende Mwanyabaanto nairane ase riroba.

English: He gave them days by number, and a set time, and gave them authority over the things that are on it.
Ekegusii: Nyasae nigo aroberetie amatuko Mwanyabaanto akomenya ase obosio bw’ense; na kobaa chinguru chi’okogambera kera egetongwa ase ense yonsi.

English: He endowed them with strength proper to them, and made them according to his own image.
Ekegusii: Nigo abaete chinguru buna echiaye ere omonyene, ekiagera nigo atongete Mwanyabaanto ase omobwekano oye ere omonyene.

English: He put the fear of man upon all flesh, and gave him dominion over beasts and birds.
Ekegusii: Erio Nyasae akabikora ebitongwa bionsi bimoiroke Mwanyabaanto, erinde akaa Mwanyabaanto chinguru igoro y’eching’iti chionsi chi’orosana amo n’echinyoni chikoiruruka.

English: He gave them counsel, tongue, eyes, ears, and heart to have understanding.
Ekegusii: Erio Nyasae akaa Mwanyabaanto chimeme, amaiso n’amato, erinde akabaa n’omoyo bw’okorengereria.

English: He filled them with the knowledge of wisdom, and showed them good and evil.
Ekegusii: Na Nyasae akabaichoria n’echisemi, abaorokererie okomanya na koigwa gati y’amaya n’amabe.

English: He set his eye upon their hearts, to show them the majesty of his works.
Ekegusii: Erio naende Nyasae akabeka nere eriso riaye ime yabo ase okobookia obosibore bw’egasi yabo.

English: And they will praise his holy name, that they may declare the majesty of his works.
Ekegusii: Mwanyabaanto nanyore ribaga ri’okoritogia erieta richenu ria Nyasae, na koraria obosiani bw’ememo yaye.

English: He added to them knowledge, and gave them a law of life for a heritage.
Ekegusii: Nyasae akabaa bosio bwabo chisemi, na kobaa ebirage bi’obogima.

English: He made an everlasting covenant with them, and showed them his decrees.
Ekegusii: Erio akabakora nabarabwo babe n’egetebanio gia kare na kare, na kobamaanorera ebirengererio biaye.

English: Their eyes saw the majesty of his glory. Their ears heard the glory of his voice.
Ekegusii: Erio amaiso abo akarora obonene bwaye, na mato abo akarora obonene bw’eriogi riaye.

English: He said to them, “Beware of all unrighteousness.” So he gave them commandment, each man concerning his neighbor.
Ekegusii: Nyasae akabateebia iga: “Timobaisa gokora bobe bonde bwonsi,” erio akabateebereria enchera bakomenya n’abamate babo.

English: Their ways are ever before him. They will not be hidden from his eyes.
Ekegusii: Nyasae nabo aroocche orogendo rwa Mwanyabaanto; mbakonyara kwebisa bosio bwaye.

English: For every nation he appointed a ruler, but Israel is the Lord’s portion.
Ekegusii: Obekire omogambi bosio bwa kera egesaku, korende Israeli n’obotenenku bwa Nyasae omonyene.

English: All their works are as clear as the sun before him. His eyes are continually upon their ways.
Ekegusii: Amakora y’abanto onsi nigo are maiso marore ase Nyasae, na kende gionsi Mwanyabaanto agokora ere nigo agokerora bosio bwaye.

English: Their iniquities are not hidden from him. All their sins are before the Lord.
Ekegusii: Obobe bwa Mwanyabaanto tibori konyara kobiseka bosio bwaye.

English: With him the alms of a man is as a signet. He will keep a man’s kindness as the pupil of the eye.
Ekegusii: Ekengwanso ki’omotaka nigo kenga omoori asare. Ere nigo akobwaterera amakora amaya buna ebioge bie riso riaye.

English: Afterwards he will rise up and repay them, and give their repayment upon their head.
Ekegusii: Agwo magega n’ababekere kobaakania egesiomba kera oyomo ekemogwerete.

English: However to those who repent he grants a return. He comforts those who are losing hope.
Ekegusii: Korende, baria bamoitabete omokia nabae enema baria abakuure emioyo abae ogosemeria erio bamoiranere.

English: Return to the Lord, and forsake sins. Make your prayer before his face offend less.
Ekegusii: Inchuo ase Nyasae, tiga gokora ebibe, saba ase obosio bwaye na otige amamocho ao.

English: Turn again to the Most High, and turn away from iniquity. Greatly hate the abominable thing.
Ekegusii: Moiranere Omonene n’otigane amabe ao; gecha ekebe n’omoyo oo bwonsi na tiga ogokora gwokogechia.

English: Who will give praise to the Most High in Hades, in place of the living who return thanks?
Ekegusii: Agwo ase omosunte ning’o oratererie Omonene Nyasae? Mbaria boka bare moyo baranyare komwakera buya.

English: Thanksgiving perishes from the dead, as from one who doesn’t exist. He who is in life and health will praise the Lord.
Ekegusii: Abakuure na bataiyo naende tibakonyara komotogia Nyasae; mbaria boka bare moyo naende bare buya, abwo nabwo boka baramotogie.

English: How great is the mercy of the Lord, and his forgiveness to those who turn to him!
Ekegusii: Naki amaabera a Nyasae akare amanene, naende naki okwabera kwaye okonene ase baria bakomoiranera.

English: For humans are not capable of everything, because the son of man is not immortal.
Ekegusii: Ntwe Mwanyabaanto titokonyara gotwara kera egento keria toganetie; ekiagera intwe twensi n’ebitongire biria bigokwa.

English: What is brighter than the sun? Yet even this can be eclipsed. So flesh and blood devise evil.
Ekegusii: Ngeto ki naende gekomesa buna risase? Nonya nabo risase narirorio nkonyoora rire enyakoira. Korende, Mwanyabaanto oyio oyio ore egetongwa ere nigo akorengereria amabe oka.

English: He looks upon the power of the height of heaven, while all men are earth and ashes.
Ekegusii: Nyasae nigo akoyetarera enuko y’abasikari baye ba igoro, korende Mwanyabaanto nigo are orotu bosa amo n’eribu.

English: He who lives forever created the whole universe.
Ekegusii: Nyasae ere oyomenyete goika kare na kare, nere otongete ense yonsi.

English: The Lord alone is just.
Ekegusii: Nyasae bweka nere ogokora ebinto bionsi ase oboikeranu.

English: He has given power to declare his works to no one. Who could trace out his mighty deeds?
Ekegusii: Taramoa monto onde chinguru naende chi’okoraria emeremo yaye; na monto tari oranyare koyetuka.

English: Who could measure the strength of his majesty? Who could also proclaim his mercies?
Ekegusii: Ning’o naende oranyare korenga chinguru chiaye chinene? Ning’o oranyare ase oboikerenu chinema chiaye.

English: As for the wondrous works of the Lord, it is not possible to take from them nor add to them, neither is it possible to explore them.
Ekegusii: Tekonyarekana ase ogokeia chinguru gose komenta emeremo yaye. Tekonyarekana koyamanya amang’ana amakumia a Nyasae.

English: When a man has finished, then he is just at the beginning. When he stops, then he will be perplexed.
Ekegusii: Ekero Mwanyabaanto agoika omoerio bw’amang’ana ayio nigo akwenyora ng’a ko nario omochakano bw’amang’ana; n’ekero atigire, nario bono agotabanana.

English: What is mankind, and what purpose do they serve? What is their good, and what is their evil?
Ekegusii: Omonto ning’o naende ninki aisaine?

English: The number of man’s days at the most are a hundred years.
Ekegusii: Omonto ekero aikire emiaka rigana, oyio omenyire emiaka emenge.

English: As a drop of water from the sea, and a pebble from the sand, so are a few years in the day of eternity.
Ekegusii: Korende, ekero okorigereria buna entonyi y’amache korwa nyancha na buna koreng’ana omochanga ore ase engegu y’enyancha; naboigo ere emiaka ere emeke kobua obogima bwa kare na kare.

English: For this cause the Lord was patient over them, and poured out his mercy upon them.
Ekegusii: Ase igo, Nyasae nigo akobaremereria gocha ase tore na amaabera, naboigo tore n’oboremereria ase okororerana amaabera.

English: He saw and perceived their end, that it is evil. Therefore he multiplied his forgiveness.
Ekegusii: Ere nigo agotorigereria na korora buna toragereirie ase ogokwa; nakio gekogera are ang’e gotwabera

English: The mercy of a man is on his neighbor; but the mercy of the Lord is on all flesh: reproving, chastening, teaching, and bringing back, as a shepherd does his flock.
Ekegusii: Omonto nigo akoba n’amaabera ase omoamate oye, korende amaabera a Nyasae nigo are gochia ase ebitongire biaye bionsi. Ere nigo agotogonyera naende bw’orokereria, na obasomia, na nigo akobarenda buna omorisia akorenda riicho riaye.

English: He has mercy on those who accept chastening, and that diligently seek after his judgments.
Ekegusii: Nyasae nigo abwate amaabera baria akoraa na banchete bakobwata na bakoigwera ogochika kwaye.

English: My son, don’t add reproach to your good deeds, and no harsh words in any of your giving.
Ekegusii: Omwana one, toburukania amakora ao amaya n’echingencho chimbe chi’okoragererigwa. K’ogokoonya omotaka tiga komosiibia obororo n’amang’ana ao.

English: Doesn’t the dew relieve the scorching heat? So a word is better than a gift.
Ekegusii: Inee, rimi tiriri kogokia ebimeri ase engaki y’omorakera, boigo eng’ana yao eyemo enke nigo eisaine kobua ekeegwa.

English: Behold, isn’t a word better than a gift? Both are with a gracious person.
Ekegusii: Ring’ana erimo ndisaine kobua ekegeni, n’omonto omwororo nigo abwate ebio bionsi bibere.

English: A fool is ungracious and abusive. The gift of a grudging person consumes the eyes.
Ekegusii: Omonto omoriri, ere n’omoiti. Ekeegwa kiomonto omochayi, nigo kegotuba amaiso.

English: Learn before you speak. Take care of your health before you get sick.
Ekegusii: Eorokererie ritang’ani otarachaka gokwana. Renda obuya bw’omobere oo ritang’ani otararwara.

English: Before judgment, examine yourself, and in the hour of scrutiny you will find forgiveness.
Ekegusii: Eitone na kweitia rituko r’ekina ritaraika, ase rituko erio, ekero gwaikire, ng’a n’onyore amaabera.

English: Humble yourself before you get sick. In the time of sins, repent.
Ekegusii: Ekeyie aye omonyene otarachia koegwa egesusuro ki’obebe bwao.

English: Let nothing hinder you to pay your vow in due time. Don’t wait until death to be released.
Ekegusii: Onye kwabeekire egeteebanio na Nyasae, koranche ikerania egeteebanio ekio ase obwango buna ekonyarekana, tobaisa koganya amakweri, ng’a erio omanye kw’aberwa.

English: Before you make a vow, prepare yourself. Don’t be like a man who tests the Lord.
Ekegusii: Eariganie ritang’ani kegima otarachia gokora ebitebanio; erio tobaisa koba buna omonto okomoteema Nyasae.

English: Think about the wrath coming in the days of the end, and the time of vengeance, when he turns away his face.
Ekegusii: Rengereria! Inyora ekeririanda kia Nyasae ekio kerabeo rituko riria orakwe kore n’ekebe. Ere nigo arakoererie amagega rituko ria ekiina.

English: In the days of fullness remember the time of hunger. Remember poverty and lack in the days of wealth.
Ekegusii: Ekero oigotete, inyora engaki y’enchara; n’ekero y’obotenenku, inyora engaki y’obotaka.

English: From morning until evening, the time changes. All things are speedy before the Lord.
Ekegusii: Korwa mambia chuni goika mogoroba, chingaki nigo chikona goncha-onchokana. Nyasae nare n’okobua kwogonchora omoroberio bw’ebitongire biaye bionsi.

English: A wise man is cautious in everything. In days of sinning, he will beware of offense.
Ekegusii: Omonto ore n’echisemi oyio n’omonto okorigereria mono ase kera egento kere bosio bwaye. Ekero aikereirwe n’ekebe nigo akwerenda tamocha.

English: Every man of understanding knows wisdom. He will give thanks to him who found her.
Ekegusii: Kera omonto okorengereria namanyete chisemi, na nigo agotogia kera omonto ochinyorire.

English: They who were of understanding in sayings also became wise themselves, and poured out apt proverbs.
Ekegusii: Abanto baria bagotegerera chimbachero nigo bagochia baba n’echisemi; nabarabwo nigo baichire n’emebayeno.

English: Don’t go after your lusts. Restrain your appetites.
Ekegusii: Tobaisa kobwatia erang’o yao embe, korende keyia okogania kwao.

English: If you give fully to your soul the delight of her desire, she will make you the laughing stock of your enemies.
Ekegusii: Oise gwechwara ase okwegokia n’erang’o y’amabe, nigo oranyore kweirire aye bweka ababisa bao bagosekerere.

English: Don’t make merry in much luxury, and don’t be tied to its expense.
Ekegusii: Tobaisa gwesoia ase emegoko emenge yabosa, ekiagera enengo eyio nigo ekogotakaia.

English: Don’t be made a beggar by banqueting with borrowed money when you have nothing in your purse.
Ekegusii: Tiga gwekora omotaka ase okonagosaberera, erio gotwara chitaabu chi’emeyega emeneene ekero aye otari nagento ase ekemoya kiao ime.

English: A worker who is a drunkard will not become rich. He who despises small things will fall little by little.
Ekegusii: Omokori emeremo omoriri, oyio tagotenenka. Oyogosiereria amang’ana amake-amake naboigo nere nigo akonakogwa ng’ora-ng’ora.

English: Wine and women will make men of understanding go astray. He who joins with prostitutes is reckless.
Ekegusii: Edivai amo n’okorigia abakungu, ebio bibere nigo bigosiria abasacha b’echisemi,

English: Decay and worms will have him as their heritage. A reckless soul will be taken away.
Ekegusii: n’omosaacha ogwechwara igo oyio nasirie obogima bwaye.

English: He who is hasty to trust is shallow-hearted. He who sins offends against his own soul.
Ekegusii: Omonto okwegena abanto bande bwango-bwango, oyio tari nobong’aini. N’oyogokora ebibe, oyio nigo agwesiria ere omonyene.

English: He who rejoices in wickedness will be condemned.
Ekegusii: Omonto okogokera ekebe, oyio nagambigwe.

English: He who hates gossip has less wickedness.
Ekegusii: Eginge n’echikwana chitari ndonge, erio mbweriite n’amang’ana amabe.

English: Never repeat what is told you, and you won’t lose anything.
Ekegusii: Tiga kona koirorera amang’ana kwaigure boire-boire, erio nario naye nario oreongore korwa ase amang’ana amange.

English: Whether it is of friend or foe, don’t tell it. Unless it is a sin to you, don’t reveal it.
Ekegusii: Tobaisa goteebia monto, naaba omosani gose omobisa oo, otatiga ekero rioka erabe ekebe onye togoteeba.

English: For if he has heard you and observed you, when the time comes, he will hate you.
Ekegusii: Ekiagera nabo erabe ng’a omonto gete okoigure na gokorora, n’ekero engaki yaikire nigo arakwange bobe.

English: Have you heard something? Let it die with you. Be brave: it will not make you burst!
Ekegusii: Inee! Kwana koigwa kende? Na tiga gekwe amo naye. Korende tibwoboa! Erio tirikogera okwe.

English: A fool will travail in pain with a word, as a woman in labor with a child.
Ekegusii: Omonto omoriri otagete kobisa ’ng’ana rinde rionsi, oyio nigo akoberebencha n’obororo buna boria bw’omokuungu okoibora.

English: As an arrow that sticks in the flesh of the thigh, so is gossip in a fool.
Ekegusii: Buna riria ensara yamobetire omonto ase ekenama kiaye, nabo ere igo igo ase omonto omoriri oyio origetie goteeba ring’ana aigure.

English: Question a friend; it may be he didn’t do it. If he did something, it may be that he may do it no more.
Ekegusii: Kooraigwe ng’a omosani oo omochire, ’mbuya ritang’ani omoborie ere omonyene, ekiagera nabo oranyore ng’a amang’ana ayio tari ay’amaene. Korende eisa koba amaene omonto oyio takoirorera rimocho erio naende.

English: Question your neighbor; it may be he didn’t say it. If he has said it, it may be that he may not say it again.
Ekegusii: Koraigwe ng’a omoamate oo okwanire ring’ana ritagwenereti, karamoria ritang’ani, nabo oranyore ng’a tarikwaneti. N’onye orikwanete, takorirorera naende.

English: Question a friend; for many times there is slander. Don’t trust every word.
Ekegusii: Onye kwaigure ring’ana riibe igoro y’omosani oo, nabo oranyore tarikwaneti. Ase igo, tobaisa kwegena kera egento ekio kwaigure.

English: There is one who slips, and not from the heart. Who is he who hasn’t sinned with his tongue?
Ekegusii: Omonto nabo arakwane egetagwenereti, ekio ere omonyene ategeneti. Korende, ning’o ere otanagokora ekebe?

English: Reprove your neighbor before you threaten him; and give place to the law of the Most High.
Ekegusii: Koraigwe kende igoro y’omwamate oo; moborie, tobaisa komogosa! Kae ebirage bia Nyasae ribaga bikore emeremo.

English: All wisdom is the fear of the Lord. In all wisdom is the doing of the law.
Ekegusii: Chisemi chionsi bombera, n’okomanya Nyasae; n’echisemi chionsi nigoro y’okoigwera ebirage bia Nyasae.

English: The knowledge of wickedness is not wisdom. The prudence of sinners is not counsel.
Ekegusii: Korende okomanya amabe tari korokwo chisemi, n’ogosemia kw’omonyabibe tari obong’aini.

English: There is a wickedness, and it is an abomination. There is a fool lacking in wisdom.
Ekegusii: Nabo eranyarekane omonto gokorera obong’ainereria ase chinchera chimbe ase okogechia gwoka. Korende nareo omonto omoriri otari na semi.

English: Better is one who has little understanding, and fears God, than one who has much intelligence and transgresses the law.
Ekegusii: Mbuya ase omonto omoirogete Nyasae otari na semi kobua omonto ore omong’aini, ko bono okobuna amachiiko.

English: There is an exquisite subtlety, and it is unjust. And there is one who perverts favor to gain a judgment.
Ekegusii: Mbareo abanto bare abang’ainereria, abwo batari gokora ayare aboronge; mbareo n’abande abwo bagosiria obuya bare nabwo ase okonyora ebi baganetie.

English: There is one who does wickedly, who hangs down his head with mourning; but inwardly he is full of deceit,
Ekegusii: Mbareo abanto bande abwo bagotirigoya, bagwetakoria ng’a mbare n’obororo, korende ime yabo nigo baichoirwe n’oborimo bwoka.

English: bowing down his face, and pretending to be deaf in one ear. Where he isn’t known, he will take advantage of you.
Ekegusii: Abanto buna abwo nigo bakobisa amasio erio boorokia ng’a mbarochi kende; korende nigo bare buna abatari kororekana, na abwo nigo baragosirie.

English: And if for lack of power he is hindered from sinning, if he finds opportunity, he will do mischief.
Ekegusii: Onye ase enchera eyemo gose eyende tibari neribaga riogokora amabe, ekero bagochia konyora ribaga erio, goika bakore ebibe.

English: A man will be known by his appearance. One who has understanding will be known by his face when you meet him.
Ekegusii: Omonto nigo akomanyekana koreng’ana buna akororekana, n’omonto ore n’ echisemi nigo okomomanya ekero mwaumeranire nere.

English: A man’s attire, grinning laughter, and the way he walks show what he is.
Ekegusii: Enchera omonto aboyetie n’echiaanga chiaye, n’enchera agoseka na gotaara, ebio bibere nabo bikomoorokia buna are.

English: There is a reproof that is not timely; and there is a person who is wise enough to keep silent.
Ekegusii: Omonto nabo aratogonyerwe ase engaki etagweneretie; ogokira nkore okwo gokworokia ng’a omonto nare n’echisemi.

English: How good is it to reprove, rather than to be angry. He who confesses will be kept back from harm.
Ekegusii: Korende nigo ere buya komoonya omonto kobua koba n’obororo nere.

English: As is the lust of a eunuch to deflower a virgin, so is he who executes judgments with violence.
Ekegusii: Omonto ogwancha amamocho aye oyio nigo agwetanga korwa ase okoragererigwa.

English: There is one who keeps silent and is found wise; and there is one who is hated for his much talk.
Ekegusii: Buna ere akong’u ase omosacha entang’ana kogania omoiseke, naboigo ere akong’u ase omonto konacha ekiina n’egekuba.

English: There is one who keeps silent, for he has no answer to make; And there is one who keeps silent, knowing when to speak.
Ekegusii: Omonto nare ekero akirire kiri okororekana koba n’echisemi; n’oyonde kogechwa ase engencho ng’ere n’omogenki, oria omobe kegima.

English: A wise man will be silent until his time has come, but the braggart and fool will miss his time.
Ekegusii: Omonto onde nere okira kiri ekiagera tari na gento agoteeba; ekiagera namanyete engaki egwenerete ekero omonto agokwana.

English: He who uses many words will be abhorred. He who takes authority for himself will be hated in it.
Ekegusii: Omonto ore n’echisemi nakire kiri takwana goika engaki egwenerete; ko bono, omonto omoetania naende omoriri tari komocha engaki egwenerete komocha.

English: There is a prosperity that a man finds in misfortunes; and there is a gain that turns to loss.
Ekegusii: Omonto ore n’amang’ana amaange nere n’agechwe, na mono kegima oyo otari koa bande ribaga ri’ogokwana.

English: There is a gift that will not profit you; and there is a gift that pays back double.
Ekegusii: Omonto nabo aranyore egesio korwa ase emechando, naende nabo ekonyarekana ng’a kiarentire emechando.

English: There are losses because of glory; and there is one who has lifted up his head from a low estate.
Ekegusii: Nkereo ekeegwa getakoretere ’ng’eria ende yonsi, korende nkereo ekeegwa kende kerarete eng’eria ara kabere.

English: There is one who buys much for a little, and pays for it again sevenfold.
Ekegusii: Engaki ende ogosikwa nigo kogosiria enibo. Korende naende mbareo abanto bande banyoorire ogosikwa korwa ase atagwenereti.

English: He who is wise in words will make himself beloved; but the pleasantries of fools will be wasted.
Ekegusii: Omonto okogora egento ase ogoaka rigori goika riakea, korende oyio chingaki chinde onyoora ng’a oakanire ara gatano na kabere goetania.

English: The gift of a fool will not profit you, for he looks for repayment many times instead of one.
Ekegusii: Ekero omonto anachire ekiina n’echisemi, oyio nigo agosikwa ase chisemi chiaye naende bwenyorera abasani abaange, korende obuya bw’omonto omoriri nigo bore bosa kegima.

English: He will give little and insult much. He will open his mouth like a crier. Today he will lend, and tomorrow he will ask for it back. Such a one is a hateful man.
Ekegusii: Ekeegwa ki’omonto omoriri, tigegokobwenera gento, ekiagera nigo akogania amange korwa ase ore, gose tari aganto.

English: The fool will say, “I have no friend, and I have no thanks for my good deeds. Those who eat my bread have an evil tongue.”
Ekegusii: Omonto bun’oyio nigo agokoa egento gekeigo, korende bwetogia, na koraria aria onsi agokoreire. Ere nigo agokoa singo reero, mambia yaye ogania omoiranerie. Omonto bun’oyio nigo akogechia mono.

English: How often, and of how many, will he be laughed to scorn!
Ekegusii: Omonto omoriri nigo agoteeba iga: “Tindi na mosani. Onde tari okong’akera ng’a mbuya mono ase obuya bwane. Nigo bakoria endagera yane, ekero baigotire bachaka gonkwana bobe.”

English: A slip on a pavement is better than a slip with the tongue. So the fall of the wicked will come speedily.
Ekegusii: Namaa! Oyio nigo akogenderera gochecherigwa n’abange.

English: A man without grace is a tale out of season. It will be continually in the mouth of the ignorant.
Ekegusii: Nigo ere buya omonto goterererigwa kagotamboka gochia nyomba na kogwa, kobua ogoterererigwa kw’oromeme; ogosirigwa kw’abanyabibe nigo kore bwango mono kegima.

English: A parable from a fool’s mouth will be rejected; for he won’t tell it at the proper time.
Ekegusii: Omonto otari goaka buya ase keria akorereirwe, gose anyoorire; omonto oyio nigo anga buna emegano etarochi nchera, eyio ekona koganwa n’abanto abariri baria bakona koyeirorera.

English: There is one who is hindered from sinning through lack. When he rests, he will not be troubled.
Ekegusii: Ekero emebayeno ekorwa ase omonto omoriri teri gwancheranwa, ekiagera teri gokwanwa ase engaki egwenerete.

English: There is one who destroys his soul through bashfulness. By a foolish countenance, he will destroy it.
Ekegusii: Omonto nabo agotangwa gokora ekebe ase engencho are omotaka, ase igo nigo agotimoka ekiagera tari na kende agweiteria.

English: There is one who for bashfulness makes promises to his friend; and he makes him his enemy for nothing.
Ekegusii: Omonto nabo arasirie obogima bwaye bwonsi, ekiagera ere akorora obosooku; gose abosirie ase okwoboa abanto.

English: A lie is an ugly blot on a person. It will be continually in the mouth of the ignorant.
Ekegusii: Onye kogokora egeteebanio n’omosani oo ase okorara bobe komosokia, aye gwakorire omonto oyio koba omobisa oo bosa.

English: A thief is better than a man who is continually lying, but they both will inherit destruction.
Ekegusii: Oborimo n’ekemoa ekebe kegima ase chimbwa chi’omonto, korende eke nakio abanto abariri bagokora botaambe.

English: The destination of a liar is dishonor. His shame is with him continually.
Ekegusii: Mbuya omonto koba omoibi kobua koba omonyaborimo; korende aba bonsi babere goika basire kegima.

English: He who is wise in words will advance himself. And one who is prudent will please great men.
Ekegusii: Chimbwa chi’onagokwana oborimo nigo chikoreta ogocharangia, okwo gokobao ase engaki etaambe ase oria ogokwana oborimo.

English: He who tills his land will raise his harvest high. He who pleases great men will get pardon for iniquity.
Ekegusii: Omonto ogokwana n’echisemi, oyio mbuya are; oyore n’echisemi nigo akogokia abanto bare n’engencho.

English: Favors and gifts blind the eyes of the wise, and as a muzzle on the mouth, turn away reproofs.
Ekegusii: Omonto okorema na gosimeka endagera, nigo akonyoora rigesa rinene; erio ogokia baanene baye, na kwenyoorera oboronge.

English: Wisdom that is hidden, and treasure that is out of sight— what profit is in either of them?
Ekegusii: Amasoya nigo agoukoria abare n’echisemi, ekio n’egesibo ki’omonwa gekoginga omonto takora amabe.

English: Better is a man who hides his folly than a man who hides his wisdom.
Ekegusii: Inee! Chisemi chi’obobisi ninki chisaine? Chisemi buna echio mbosa.

English: My son, have you sinned? Do it no more; and ask forgiveness for your past sins.
Ekegusii: Omwana one. Inee! Gwakorire ekebe? Tokora ekebe naende. Ko bono saba amaabera ase aria gwakorire.

English: Flee from sin as from the face of a snake; for if you go near, it will bite you. Its teeth are like lion’s teeth, slaying people’s souls.
Ekegusii: Tama ekebe buna koreng’ana ogotama eng’iti; ekiagera oise gosukerera eng’iti goika ekorome. Amaino y’ekebe igo anga buna amaino y’Endo. Ekebe nigo kegosiria emioyo y’abanto.

English: All iniquity is as a two-edged sword. Its stroke has no healing.
Ekegusii: Okobuna ebirage nigo konga buna omoro otieririe chinsemo chionsi, omoro buna oyio oise kogokeba nigo okoroisia riote ritari kogwena.

English: Terror and violence will waste away riches. So the house of an arrogant man will be laid waste.
Ekegusii: Okogosereria amo n’oboiti nigo bigosaria enibo; enyomba y’omonto omwerori nigo ekorenta obosooku.

English: Supplication from a poor man’s mouth reaches to the ears of God, and his judgment comes speedily.
Ekegusii: Ogosaba kw’omotaka nigo gokoigwekana as Nyasae, n’okoiraneria kwaye nigo kore bwango mono kegima.

English: One who hates reproof is in the path of the sinner. He who fears the Lord will repent in his heart.
Ekegusii: Omonto okwanga kogorororwa ekero are ase ebibe, korende oy’omoirogete Nyasae nigo akweitia omoyo oye ime.

English: He who is mighty in tongue is known far away; but the man of understanding knows when he slips.
Ekegusii: Omonto nabo arabe ogokwana n’obong’aini na komanyekana gochia aare, korende nigo akoraua n’oyore n’echisemi.

English: He who builds his house with other men’s money is like one who gathers stones for his own tomb.
Ekegusii: Omonto okwagacha enyomba ase chifeta chi’abaanto bande, igo anga buna oy’ogosangereria amagena y’embera yaye.

English: The congregation of wicked men is as a bundle of tow with a flame of fire at the end of them.
Ekegusii: Omosangererekano bw’abakori amabe, nigo onga buna engori egwoka agwo ase baraumerane kw’omorero ekerage okobumbucha.

English: The way of sinners is paved with stones; and at the end of it is the pit of Hades.
Ekegusii: Eng’eria y’omokori amabe nigo eroosegete buya, korende enchera eyio nigo ekoerera ase engoro y’amakweri.

English: He who keeps the law becomes master of its intent. The fulfilment of the fear of the Lord is wisdom.
Ekegusii: Onde bwensi okobwatia ebirage oyio nigo agamberete ebirengererio biaye; chisemi N’oboikeranu bw’okomomanya Nyasae.

English: He who is not clever will not be instructed. There is a cleverness which makes bitterness abound.
Ekegusii: Omonto otari nasemi, oyio nomosomia tari koigwa. Korende koba n’echisemi n’okomenta obororo.

English: The knowledge of a wise man will be made to abound as a flood, and his counsel as a fountain of life.
Ekegusii: Emeroberio y’omonyene chisemi nigo ekomentekana buna okoyaaba kw’amache ekero gi’etoigo. N’ogosemia nigo konga buna ensoko entuboka.

English: The inward parts of a fool are like a broken vessel. He will hold no knowledge.
Ekegusii: Chisemi chio omonto omoriri nigo chinga buna egetaabo kebochogete, kende gionsi omonto oyio agosoma nigo kegoeta rioka getari kogoma, erinde giasira kegima: tari kobwata gento.

English: If a man of knowledge hears a wise word, he will commend it and add to it. The wanton man hears it, and it displeases him, so he throws it away behind his back.
Ekegusii: Ekero omonto omong’aini akoigwa ring’ana ri’echisemi nigo akoritogia na korimenta kegima. Korende omonto osirete ekero akoriigwa nigo akorisiereria, na koritugutera aare kegima.

English: The chatter of a fool is like a burden in the way, but grace will be found on the lips of the wise.
Ekegusii: Engambo ya abanto abariri igo enga buna egurube omonto abogoretie nchera kogenda; korende omogooko nigo okonyorekana korwa ase ebirengerio bi’omonto omong’aini.

English: The utterance of the prudent man will be sought for in the congregation. They will ponder his words in their heart.
Ekegusii: Ase omosangererekano abanto nigo bakorigia ebirengererio bio omonto omong’aini; na barabwo nigo bakoarigania amang’ana aya ase emioyo yabo ime.

English: As a house that is destroyed, so is wisdom to a fool. The knowledge of an unwise man is talk without sense.
Ekegusii: Ase omonto omoriri chisemi nigo chinga buna enyomba yagure; n’emeroberio y’omonto omoriri igo are amang’ana atari na moroberio.

English: Instruction is as fetters on the feet of an unwise man, and as manacles on the right hand.
Ekegusii: Ase omonto omoriri ogosoma nigo konga buna egesibo kere magoro, enga buna efeta ase okoboko okorio.

English: A fool lifts up his voice with laughter, but a clever man smiles quietly.
Ekegusii: Omonto omoriri nigo agoseka n’eriogi, korende omonyene chisemi nigo akona goseka ng’ora igo.

English: Instruction is to a prudent man as an ornament of gold, and as a bracelet upon his right arm.
Ekegusii: Omonto omoririri nigo agoseka gochia igoro n’eriogi, korende ase omonto ore n’echisemi nigo akona goseka ng’ora igo. Ase omonto ore omong’aini chesemi nigo chinga buna ebonyi y’amagena ’amaabera, nigo enga buna ebonyi ase okoboko kwaborio.

English: The foot of a fool rushes into a house, but a man of experience will be ashamed of entering.
Ekegusii: Omonto omoriri nigo akoayerera gosoa gochia nyomba mwabande, omonto omong’aini nigo akoganyera gesieri n’amasikani.

English: A foolish man peers into the door of a house, but a man who is instructed will stand outside.
Ekegusii: Omonto omoriri nigo akoayerera gosoa ime y’echinyomba chiabande; Korende ase omonto ore n’echisemi nigo akoganyera isiko n’amasikani. Omonto otari n’echimbwa chingiya nigo agosiomeria gochia nyomba mwabande, korende oyore n’amasikani, nigo akoganyera isiko.

English: It is rude for someone to listen at a door, but a prudent person will be grieved with the disgrace.
Ekegusii: Nigo ere chimbwa chimbe ekero omonto agotegerera amang’ana y’abanto bande ase ebisieri biabo, korende ase baria bare n’obong’aini gokora egento buna ekio n’obososku obonene kegima.

English: The lips of strangers will be grieved at these things, but the words of prudent men will be weighed in the balance.
Ekegusii: Abanto abetakori nigo bachete konakoirorera amang’ana aria baigure korwa ase abanto bande, korende baria bare n’obong’aini nigo bare n’amang’ana are n’echinguru.

English: The heart of fools is in their mouth, but the mouth of wise men is their heart.
Ekegusii: Ekerengererio ki’abaonto abariri nigo kere ang’e n’emenwa yabo, korende eki bagoteeba abanyene chisemi nigo gekorwa ase ebirengererio biabo.

English: When the ungodly curses an adversary, he curses his own soul.
Ekegusii: Ekero omonto omobe akoragereria ekerecha, nigo akweragereria ere omonyene.

English: A whisperer defiles his own soul, and will be hated wherever he travels.
Ekegusii: Omonto omwemurungania nigo agosaria obogima bwaye ere omonyene, naende kera omonto ase eamate yaye nigo amogechete mono kegima.

English: A slothful man is compared to a stone that is defiled. Everyone will hiss at him in his disgrace.
Ekegusii: Omonto omobe nigo akoreng’anigwa n’erigena rire n’eubi; kera omonto komorora omonto buna oyio nigo akweringa ase engencho y’obososoku bwaye oyio.

English: A slothful man is compared to the filth of a dunghill. Anyone who picks it up will shake it out of his hand.
Ekegusii: Omonto omobe nigo arabwekanigwe n’orosao rw’amabi; Kera omonto okorokuna orosao orwo nigo akoyaserera aare

English: An undisciplined child is a disgrace to his father, and a foolish daughter is born to his loss.
Ekegusii: N’okoragererigwa ase omonto ore n’baana ko otaari n’amasikani, n’okoibora kw’omwana omwana omoiseke otari n’echimbwa chingiya nigo enga ogosirerigwa.

English: A prudent daughter will inherit a husband of her own. She who brings shame is the grief of her father.
Ekegusii: Omoiseke bw’echimbu chingiya nigo akonyora omosacha, ko bono, oyogokora amang’ana amabe nigo akorenta obosooku ase ise.

English: She who is arrogant brings shame on father and husband. She will be despised by both of them.
Ekegusii: Omoiseke ore n’echimbu chiimbe nigo akorentera ise gose omosacha oye obosooku, na nigo arasierererigwe na bosi babere.

English: Ill-timed conversation is like music in mourning, but stripes and correction are wisdom in every season.
Ekegusii: Kogambia abana bao chingaki chinde nabo enga buna omonto ogotereria abanto bare ase ebirero. Koa abana egesusuro na kobagambera ase obuya nigo ere egento kiengencho enene mono kobwa.

English: He who teaches a fool is like one who glues potsherds together, even like one who wakes a sleeper out of a deep sleep.
Ekegusii: Goteema komosemia omonto omoriri nigo enga buna kobekerania chindogio chi’enyongo ase okoyebarera, gose igo enga buna gotura omonto oraire n’ore n’echitoro chinyinge mono kegima.

English: He who teaches a fool is as one who teaches a man who slumbers. In the end he will say, “What is it?”
Ekegusii: Koeresa omonto omoriri egento nigo enga buna nigo okoeresa omonto oraire chitoro; ekero gwakoorire koeresa omoriri oyio naende okoboria: “Ninki buno kware goteeba?”

English: Weep for the dead, for he lacks light. Weep for a fool, for he lacks understanding. Weep more sweetly for the dead, because he has found rest, but the life of the fool is worse than death.
Ekegusii: Oyo kworokereria omonto omoriri, oyio nigo anga buna omonto ogosangereria ebigonkorio, gose buna oy’otura omonto ore n’echitoro erinde amosabe singo.

English: Mourning for the dead lasts seven days, but for a fool and an ungodly man, it lasts all the days of his life.
Ekegusii: Onde bwensi okoganera omoriri omgano, igo enga buna gokwana n’omonto ore n’echitoro chindito.

English: Don’t talk much with a foolish man, and don’t go to one who has no understanding. Beware of him, lest you have trouble and be defiled in his onslaught. Turn away from him, and you will find rest, and you won’t be wearied in his madness.
Ekegusii: Moreere oyo kure ekiage ere tari goikeera borabu bonde; naende moreere omonto omoriri ekiagera tari na semi. Tobaisa komoreera moono omonto okuure ekigera ere otimokire; korende moreere omonto omoriri, ekiagera obogima bwaye n’obobe kobwa amakweri.

English: What would be heavier than lead? What is its name, but “Fool”?
Ekegusii: Ebirero nigo bigokorwa ase amatuko atano n’abere, korende ebirero bi’omonto omoriri oyo otamomanyeti Nyasae, nigo akobosiria obogima bwaye bwonsi ere omonyene.

English: Sand, salt, and a mass of iron is easier to bear than a man without understanding.
Ekegusii: Tobaisa konakogamba n’omonto omoriri; gose komobeera omonto otari na semi. Mwebachere erio nario nere aranyare gwetanga korwa ase emechando; erio ekero ere aresibie, aye nobe n’eubi. Mwebachere omonto omoriri erio nario naye oranyore omorembe, gose tobaisa korosigwa n’obobarimo bwaye.

English: Timber girded and bound into a building will not be released with shaking. So a heart established in due season on well advised counsel will not be afraid.
Ekegusii: Ngento ki kere ekerito kobwa embende? Erieta ri’egento buna ekio nigo gekorokwa “Ekeiriri!”

English: A heart settled upon a thoughtful understanding is as an ornament of plaster on a polished wall.
Ekegusii: Okobogoria amaroba, omonyo n’echuma nigo bire buya kobwa komoremereria omonto omoriri.

English: Fences set on a high place will not stand against the wind; so a fearful heart in the imagination of a fool will not stand against any fear.
Ekegusii: Esiro ere n’oboroso obokong’u ase enyomba, omotengecho bw’ense noocha tokonyara koyeiyeria. Naboigo, n’omoyo oteneine bokong’u naende obwate oboroso bw’oboroso bwe chisemi tokoba nabwoba nonya na ase engaki y’emechando.

English: He who pricks the eye will make tears fall. He who pricks the heart makes it show feeling.
Ekegusii: Omoyo okong’igwe n’ebirenererio bi’echisemi nigo onga buna orwaki rochabeire.

English: Whoever casts a stone at birds scares them away. He who insults a friend will dissolve friendship.
Ekegusii: Amagena amake ayio abakereire igoro y’orwaki tagotigara aroro agwo ekero ekerambauti kegochicha. Ase enchera buna eyio eyio n’omoyo n’ebingererio bi’oboriri; tokonyaro keremereria ayagocha korwa ase obobe buna obwo.

English: If you have drawn a sword against a friend, don’t despair, for there may be a way back.
Ekegusii: Oise gotongia eriso riao, nigo rikorera na korwa amariga; naboigo oise koara omoyo oo nario ereigwere obororo boreo.

English: If you have opened your mouth against a friend, don’t be afraid, for there may be reconciliation, unless it is for insulting, arrogance, disclosing of a secret, or a treacherous blow— for these things any friend will flee.
Ekegusii: Oisekoruta chinyoni amagena nigo ogochiseria; n’ekero okomotogonyera omosani oo, oise gokora bo, igo kwabunire obosani bwao amo nere.

English: Gain trust with your neighbor in his poverty, that in his prosperity you may have gladness. Stay steadfast to him in the time of his affliction, that you may be heir with him in his inheritance.
Ekegusii: Nonya gwaikigwe gotwara enkwano enkong’u n’omosani oo, tokwa omoyo; ekiagera naende nabo obosani bokogorororwa naende bobeo

English: Before fire is the vapor and smoke of a furnace, so insults precede bloodshed.
Ekegusii: Onye gwakwanire egento ekebe igoro y’omosani oo, toiroka ogonsonsoranigwa nkoreo naende nabo gokonyarekana. Korende ogokwana amang’ana abosi na koraama amo n’obwerori, n’okobasagania abande mosiabano, ebio nabio ebinto bigoseria abasani.

English: I won’t be ashamed to shelter a friend. I won’t hide myself from his face.
Ekegusii: Tiga omoamate oo akwegene ekero are n’obotaka bwaye, erio bwegokie amo nere chingaki akonyora ng’eria ende yonsi. Mokoonye ekero akonyoora emechando, erinde naye n’onyore eng’eria korwa ase ensemo yaye eye araegwe.

English: If any evil happens to me because of him, everyone who hears it will beware of him.
Ekegusii: Erioki n’ekiorokerio ki’omorero, oroguto n’erioki ri’omorero okogakara nigo bigotang’ana gochicha. Ase enchera eyio eyio, n’okorama nabo kore buna ekemanyererio kiamakweri.

English: Who will set a watch over my mouth, and a seal of shrewdness upon my lips, that I may not fall from it, and that my tongue may not destroy me?
Ekegusii: Tinkoba n’obosooku ase okomorenda omosani one, gose tinkonyara kwebisa korwa asare.

English: O Lord, Father and Master of my life, don’t abandon me to their counsel. Don’t let me fall because of them.
Ekegusii: Aye Nyasae Tata, n’omogaambi bw’obogima bwane, ase ogwancha kwao tintiga erio insirigwe na n’emechando yane; gose obaisa gwancha nkore amabe ase engencho yaye.

English: Who will set scourges over my thought, and a discipline of wisdom over my heart, that they spare me not for my errors, and not overlook their sins?
Ekegusii: Onye nokobua, ango ebirengererio biane nigo biare gochwatwa ebiranya, n’omoyo one bworokererigwe chimbua chi’obong’aini. Abwo bono tinaregotigwa nkona kogororwa korwa ase amamocho aane, n’ekebe kiane kende gionsi kegosusurwa;

English: Otherwise my errors might be multiplied, and my sins abound, I fall before my adversaries, and my enemy rejoice over me.
Ekegusii: erio amamocho aane tamentekana mono kegima, n’ebibe biane mbimentekana. Ase igo tingwa ase amaboko y’ababisa.

English: O Lord, Father and God of my life, don’t give me a haughty eyes,
Ekegusii: Aye Nyasae, Tata na Omogambi bw’obogima bwane, nagosororire nkoonye timbaisa koba n’obwerori.

English: and turn away evil desire from me.
Ekegusii: Aye Nyasae koranche nagosoroire onginge korwa ase okogania kwane okobe.

English: Let neither gluttony nor lust overtake me. Don’t give me over to a shameless mind.
Ekegusii: Tobaisa gwancha gontiga mbe omochayi gose mbe n’okogania okobe. Tontiga ngaamberwe n’okogania okonge okobe

English: Listen, my children, to the discipline of the mouth. He who keeps it will not be caught.
Ekegusii: Abana baane, tegerera erinde moigwe okworokereria igoro y’ogokwana okuya; omonto okoyaigwa na koyabwatia amang’ana ayio, oyio takogwa ase omotego.

English: The sinner will be overpowered through his lips. By them, the insulter and the arrogant will stumble.
Ekegusii: Omonyabibe nigo akobwatwa ase okweimokereria na amang’ana aye omonyene.

English: Don’t accustom your mouth to an oath, and don’t be accustomed to naming the Holy One,
Ekegusii: Tobaisa kwenaria gose konara chingeencho chiogotiana gose kona gwatora erieta richenu ri’Omonene ase ogokora echeche.

English: for as a servant who is continually scourged will not lack bruises, so he also who swears and continually utters the Name will not be cleansed from sin.
Ekegusii: Buna ere ase omokori emeremo okorendwa mono atari komocha goakwa ebiranya, boigo, oria okona gotiana ase okoriatora erieta ria Omonene Nyasae, ekeene ere tagotamboka korwa ase ogokora ebibe.

English: A man of many oaths will be filled with iniquity. The scourge will not depart from his house. If he offends, his sin will be upon him. If he disregards it, he has sinned doubly. If he has sworn falsely, he will not be justified, for his house will be filled with calamities.
Ekegusii: Omonto okona gotiana boire nigo agoichorwa n’obobe na obokong’u tibokorwa ase enyomba yaye. Ere abe taikerania aria atianete ere goika abe nokomocha; naende karasiererie nabe nokomocha ara kabere. Karabe otianire bosa, takorengererigwa buna oyo otari na komocha, ase ayio ere nomomochi rioka, ere goika aegwe egesusuro; na ase enyomba yaye ogokwa nkobeo botambe.

English: There is a manner of speech that is clothed with death. Let it not be found in the heritage of Jacob, for all these things will be far from the godly, and they will not wallow in sins.
Ekegusii: Ogokwana nkoreo konga ogokwa okonyene. Okwo tikobaisa koba ase abaiborwa ba Yakobo. Baria bamoirogete Omonene Nyasae barabwo inabatamboke amomocho ayio onsi igo barabwo tibagwesigooria ase ebibe.

English: Don’t accustom your mouth to gross rudeness, for it involves sinful speech.
Ekegusii: Tobaisa konaria ebikoba biao gokwana obogundo, ekiagera ase ogokwana okwo nigo kobwataine nebibe.

English: Remember your father and your mother, for you sit in the midst of great men, that you be not forgetful before them, and become a fool by your bad habit; so you may wish that you had not been born, and curse the day of your birth.
Ekegusii: Ekero oraikaranse na abanene oinyore iso na nyoko, tobaisa kobeeba agwo ase obosio bwa abanene erio ororekane omoriri ase obosio bwa abanene ase chinchera chiao. Agwo aye inabweitie na koragereria rituko riria aye kwaiboretwe.

English: A man who is accustomed to abusive language won’t be corrected all the days of his life.
Ekegusii: Omonto onarete amang’ana amagundo ituko ndiri arabe n’amasikani ase obogima bwaye bwensi.

English: Two sorts of people multiply sins, and the third will bring wrath: a hot passion, like a burning fire, will not be quenched until it is consumed; a fornicator in the body of his flesh will never cease until he has burned out the fire.
Ekegusii: Abanto be chinchera ibere nigo bakoiranerera ebibe, ab’enchera ya gatato nigo bakorenta endamwamu y’Omonene. Omonto nigo agosogwa n’ogwoka gwokogania buna omorero otakende goika orimirigwe. Omonto ogosambwa n’omorero bw’ogokorera omobere oye omonyene obonyaka tagotiga goika ere omonyene osiriigwe ase omorero.

English: All bread is sweet to a fornicator. He will not cease until he dies.
Ekegusii: Ase omonto omonyaka, kera omokungu nomwansu na takonyora ogoisaneka amatuko onsi ere amenyete.

English: A man who goes astray from his own marriage bed says in his heart, “Who sees me? Darkness is around me, and the walls hide me. No one sees me. Of whom am I afraid? The Most High will not remember my sins.”
Ekegusii: Omonto nigo akobuna eira yaye y’enyaangi na goteeba ase omoyo oye: “Ning’o ondooche? Omosunte nigo ong’etanaine nechinyasi nigo chimbisete! Monto taiyo ondooche, inche ninki ndoboere? Omonene takorora ebibe biane!”

English: The eyes of men are his terror. He doesn’t know that the eyes of the Lord are ten thousand times brighter than the sun, seeing all the ways of men, and looking into secret places.
Ekegusii: Obwoba bw’omonto oyio nase abanto boka. Ere tamanyeti buna amaiso y’Omonene nigo aramogetie ara chilifu ikomi kobua risase. Amaiso ayio nigo arigereretie chinchera chionsi chia Mwanyabaanto, goika nonya nchiria chionsi chibisegete.

English: All things were known to him before they were created, and also after they were completed.
Ekegusii: Ere nigo akomanyete aye konye otaraiborwa goika omoerio ekero ere akoorete gotonga ense.

English: This man will be punished in the streets of the city. He will be seized where he least expects it.
Ekegusii: Omonto oyio omonyabibe ere nabwatwe engaki eria atakagereti na koegwa egesusuro ase obosio bwa abanto bonsi.

English: So also is a wife who leaves her husband, and produces an heir by another man.
Ekegusii: Naboigo ere ase omokungu oria ogotiga omosacha oye na koibora abana nomosaacha onde.

English: For first, she was disobedient in the law of the Most High. Second, she trespassed against her own husband. Third, she played the adulteress in fornication, and had children by another man.
Ekegusii: Ritang’ani; omokungu oyio ochaayire ogochika kw’Omonene ore igoro mono, eriakabere; okorire okomocha ase omosacha oye, na eriagatato; okorire obonyaka ase obotayayi bwaye, na koibora abana n’omosaacha onde.

English: She shall be brought out into the congregation. Her punishment will extend to her children.
Ekegusii: Ere omonyene nigo arabeekwe ase obosio bw’ekegambero, naende naegwe egesusuro goetera ase abana baye.

English: Her children will not take root. Her branches will bear no fruit.
Ekegusii: Abana baye tibakonyara gotenena ase oboremu, na barabwo tibakonyoora okwama.

English: She will leave her memory for a curse. Her reproach won’t be blotted out.
Ekegusii: Ere natige okoragererigwa ase ense, na obosooku akorete tibokwebwa kare na kare.

English: And those who are left behind will know that there is nothing better than the fear of the Lord, and nothing sweeter than to heed the commandments of the Lord.
Ekegusii: Baria abatigari inabamanye buna ing’ana rinde ndiri rigiya kobua komoiroka Omonene, na tikeiyo egento egiansu kobua okoigwera amachiiko y’Omonene.

English: Wisdom will praise her own soul, and will proclaim her glory in the midst of her people.
Ekegusii: Obong’aini nigo bogwetogia obonyene na kweimokereria igoro ase egati ya abanto baye.

English: She will open her mouth in the congregation of the Most High, and proclaim her glory in the presence of his power.
Ekegusii: Inabwetogie ase obosio Omonene inabwetogie ase obosio bw’emeganda bogoteeba,

English: “I came out of the mouth of the Most High, and covered the earth as a mist.
Ekegusii: Inche nering’ana korwa ase omonwa oye ere oyore igoro mono oyio okengerete ense buna ritatuuri.

English: I lived in high places, and my throne is in the pillar of the cloud.
Ekegusii: Obomenyo bwane nigo bwarenge igoro, ekerogo kiane ase chisiiro chiamare.

English: Alone I surrounded the circuit of heaven, and walked in the depth of the abyss.
Ekegusii: Inche omonyene nigo naetete ase ense eetananete boigo ngaeta inse y’ense.

English: In the waves of the sea, and in all the earth, and in every people and nation, I obtained a possession.
Ekegusii: Igoro ase emerindo yechinyaancha chi’ense engima, nigo nkogamba ase egati ya abanto ne chinse chionsi.

English: With all these I sought rest. In whose inheritance shall I lodge?
Ekegusii: Inche nigo naetete ase onsi nkorigia ase ngoikaransa, ensemo yense ase ndaroisie obomenyo bwane.

English: Then the Creator of all things gave me a command. He who created me made my tent to rest, and said, ‘Let your dwelling be in Jacob, and your inheritance in Israel.’
Ekegusii: Agwo ere oria Omotongi o bionsi akang’a ogochika; ere oyio ontongete akandobereria ase inche ndabeeke obomenyo bwane. Ere aganteebia, “Roisia obomenyo bwao ase enyomba ya Yakobo, bogoria ensemo yao ase Israeli.”

English: He created me from the beginning, before the ages. For all ages, I will not cease to exist.
Ekegusii: Ere nigo antongete korwa agwo omochakano, igo inche nimbeo kare na kare naende tinkorwa ase oboiko bw’ense.

English: In the holy tabernacle, I ministered before him. So I was established in Zion.
Ekegusii: Inche nigo nabete nkomokorera ase obomenyo bwaye obochenu, inche ngakong’era agwo ase egetunwa gia Sayoni.

English: In the beloved city, likewise he gave me rest. In Jerusalem was my domain.
Ekegusii: Ere akambeka ntimoke ime ase omochie oye omwanchwa, obomenyo bwane nigo bwarenge agwo ase omochie o Yerusalemu.

English: I took root in a people that was honored, even in the portion of the Lord’s own inheritance.
Ekegusii: Inche nkabeeka emeri yane inse ase abanto abasike, ensemo yane ase abanto baye ere Omonene.

English: I was exalted like a cedar in Lebanon, And like a cypress tree on the mountains of Hermon.
Ekegusii: Inche ngatambea mono buna emeharuni ya Lebanoni, ee buna ebirobo bie egetunwa kia Herimoni.
