Ekegusii: Obong’aini bobe omochakano o kera ring’ana ogokora, na oboseemia botang’anere emeremo ende yonsi.

English: As a token of the changing of the heart,
Ekegusii: Ebirengererio bionsi nigo bire ase enkoro na korwa aroro ebinto biechingeencho inye nao bikororekana:

English: four kinds of things rise up: good and evil, life and death. That which rules over them continually is the tongue.
Ekegusii: Obuya nobobe, obomoyo na amakweri; na eki gekogambera ebio bionsi noromeme.

English: There is one who is clever and the instructor of many, and yet is unprofitable to his own soul.
Ekegusii: Omonto nabo aranyare koba nobong’aini na abe omworokia bw’abange, korende ere taba nengeencho gochia asare ere omonyene.

English: There is one who is subtle in words, and is hated. He will be destitute of all food.
Ekegusii: Omonto ore omwoge ase ogokwana nabo arabe okogeechia nonya ngoika ase akoborwa nonya nendagera akoria;

English: For grace was not given to him from the Lord, because he is deprived of all wisdom.
Ekegusii: ase engencho atanyoreti amaabera ase Omonene, ekiagera ere atabwati obong’aini bonde bwonsi.

English: There is one who is wise to his own soul; and the fruits of his understanding are trustworthy in the mouth.
Ekegusii: Oyonde nabo agotwara obong’aini ase okwegwenera ere omonyene, na koyarora amang’ana aye koba amaikeranu.

English: A wise man will instruct his own people. The fruits of his understanding are trustworthy.
Ekegusii: Omonto omong’aini nanyaare kobaseemia abanto baye, na ayakobwatekana nobomanyi bwaye abe amaikeranu.

English: A wise man will be filled with blessing. All those who see him will call him happy.
Ekegusii: Omonto omong’aini natogigwe ase obonge, na bonsi abarabe bakomorora inabamoroke omonyagesio.

English: The life of a man is counted by days. The days of Israel are innumerable.
Ekegusii: Amatuko yobogima bw’omonto nigo abarire korende amatuko a Israeli tari nomobaro.

English: The wise man will inherit confidence among his people. His name will live forever.
Ekegusii: Omonto omong’aini nenyorere esiko ase abanto bamwabo, nechinkuma chiaye nchibeo ase amatuko atakoera.

English: My son, test your soul in your life. See what is evil for it, and don’t give in to it.
Ekegusii: Aye omwana one, bwerenge omoyo oo ekero ore moyo; okerore ekere ekebe asore okiebachere.

English: For not all things are profitable for all men. Not every soul has pleasure in everything.
Ekegusii: Ekiagera tari kera egento kemogwenerete kera omonto gose tari kera omonto okogokera kera egento.

English: Don’t be insatiable in any luxury. Don’t be greedy in the things that you eat.
Ekegusii: Toba oyogosanera kera ebinto bi’okwegokia, gose toba omosomba bw’endagera.

English: For overeating brings disease, and gluttony causes nausea.
Ekegusii: Ekiagera okoria okonge nigo gokorenta oborwaire, enda embe nigo ekorenta ogosareka kw’omoyo.

English: Because of gluttony, many have perished, but he who takes heed shall prolong his life.
Ekegusii: Abanto abange bakuure ase okoria bobe, oyokwebachera obonyandambe, ere natambeyie obogima bwaye.

English: Honor a physician according to your need with the honors due to him, for truly the Lord has created him.
Ekegusii: Omoe omogwenia esiko yaye emogwenerete, ase engencho yemeremo agokora asore, ekiagera ere boigo atongetwe n’Omonene.

English: For healing comes from the Most High, and he shall receive a gift from the king.
Ekegusii: Ekiagera ekeegwa kiaye kioborwaria nigo kerwete ase Omonene; nere nigo akonyora ekeegwa korwa ase omorwoti.

English: The skill of the physician will lift up his head. He will be admired in the sight of great men.
Ekegusii: Obomanyi bwomogwenia nigo gokomorentera okomanyekana, nere nigo akonyoora esiko ase egati ya abanene.

English: The Lord created medicines out of the earth. A prudent man will not despise them.
Ekegusii: Omonene nigo atongete amariogo onsi korwa ase riroba, na omonto omong’aini takonyaara koyasiereria.

English: Wasn’t water made sweet with wood, that its power might be known?
Ekegusii: Inee, tari ase enyimbo amaache aonchoretwe agakorwa amaya erio Omonene aborokie abanto Chinguru chiaye?

English: He gave men skill that he might be glorified in his marvelous works.
Ekegusii: Omonene nigo abaete abanto chiseemi nobomanyi, erio ere atogigwe ase emeremo yaye yogokumia.

English: With them he heals and takes away pain.
Ekegusii: Ere nigo akobagwenia abanto ase amariogo na kobaruseria obosareru;

English: With these, the pharmacist makes a mixture. God’s works won’t be brought to an end. From him, peace is upon the face of the earth.
Ekegusii: omwochogania amariogo nigo akoroisia ogwochoganigwa kwaye. Emeremo y’Omonene teri nomoerio; obosera bw’emebere ase ense nigo bokorwa ase are ere.

English: My son, in your sickness don’t be negligent, but pray to the Lord, and he will heal you.
Ekegusii: Aye omwana one, ekero orarware tobaisa koba omworo ase engencho yoborwaire, korende omosabe Omonene nere nakogwenie.

English: Put away wrong doing, and direct your hands in righteousness. Cleanse your heart from all sin.
Ekegusii: Tiga amamocho ao, bwerwe gokora amaya, na gochena enkoro yao korwa ase ebibe biechingeencho chionsi.

English: Give a sweet savor and a memorial of fine flour, and pour oil on your offering, according to your means.
Ekegusii: Omorwere Omonene ekeng’wanso kiogosambwa kierimisu rigiya, nekeng’wanso ki’obosie obonuke gi’okoinyoria. Obiiterere ebing’wanso biao amaguta koreng’ana nokonyoora kwao.

English: Then give place to the physician, for truly the Lord has created him. Don’t let him leave you, for you need him.
Ekegusii: Erio ayande oyatigere omogwenia; ekiagera Omonene nere omotongete tobaisa komotiga arue asore ekiagera nomoganetie.

English: There is a time when recovery is in their hands.
Ekegusii: Ebiro mbire ekero okogwena kogoetera ase omogwenia.

English: For they also shall ask the Lord to prosper them in diagnosis and in healing for the maintenance of life.
Ekegusii: Ekiagera barabwo boigo nigo bagosaba Omonene abae okonyaara ase oboringoria bwabo, ase okogwenia ase ogotoria obogima.

English: He who sins before his Maker, let him fall into the hands of the physician.
Ekegusii: Omonto ogokora ebibe mamincha yomotongi oye, motige agwe ase amaboko yomogwenia.

English: My son, let your tears fall over the dead, and as one who suffers grievously, begin lamentation. Wind up his body with due honor. Don’t neglect his burial.
Ekegusii: Aye omwana one, omoreere omonto oria okuure; rera ase obororo bworokie amayianda ao. Oyobogorie omobere oye ase amasikani agwenerete gose aye tobaisa gosiereria ogotindekwa kwaye.

English: Make bitter weeping and make passionate wailing. Let your mourning be according to his merit, for one day or two, lest you be spoken evil of; and so be comforted for your sorrow.
Ekegusii: Orere ase obororo nenkoro yao, oikeranie ebirero buna egwenerete ase oria oraarire, okubie amatuko abere goika atato tobaisa gocha goteebwa; erio eremigwe korwa ase ogoichana kwao.

English: For from sorrow comes death. Sorrow of heart saps one’s strength.
Ekegusii: Ekiagera omoichano nigo okorenta amakweri, n’omoichano bw’enkoro nigo okonyunyunta chinguru chi’omonto.

English: In calamity, sorrow also remains. A poor man’s life is grievous to the heart.
Ekegusii: Ekero omonto arure ase ense, omoichano oye nigo okoera, korende obogima bw’obotaka nigo bokoremaria enkoro.

English: Don’t give your heart to sorrow. Put it away, remembering the end.
Ekegusii: Aye tibwanchera enkoro yao egamberwe nomoichano; oyoserie omoichano erio aye korengereretie omoerio oo.

English: Don’t forget it, for there is no returning again. You do him no good, and you would harm yourself.
Ekegusii: Tobaisa kweba buna okoirana magega tikoiyo, tokonyaara komokoonya nyagosira gento kende naende nigo ogwechaanda aye omonyene.

English: Remember his end, for so also will yours be: yesterday for him, and today for you.
Ekegusii: Oinyore buna naye nokwe buna ere akuure, igoro nere, ankio naye.

English: When the dead is at rest, let his remembrance rest. Be comforted for him when his spirit departs from him.
Ekegusii: Ekero nyagosira akobekwa ase ogotimoka ime ase oboina, okomoinyora gotigwe, naye tobaisa kogenderera komoreera ekero omoyo oye orure aroro.

English: The wisdom of the scribe comes by the opportunity of leisure. He who has little business can become wise.
Ekegusii: Ebiro nigo bikomoa omosomi chingaki chikonyoora obong’aini, omonto obwate emeremo emeke nabo aranyare konyoora obong’aini.

English: How could he become wise who holds the plow, who glories in the shaft of the goad, who drives oxen and is occupied in their labors, and who mostly talks about bulls?
Ekegusii: Inaki omonto ore ase obokombe riika aranyare koba nobong’aini? Omogooko oye nogotema chiombe na gochiraa chikuruure obokombe, boigo chinkwana chiaye chionsi nigo chibogoretie amang’ana yobotugi!

English: He will set his heart upon turning his furrows. His lack of sleep is to give his heifers their fodder.
Ekegusii: Ebirengererio biaye nogotema chiombe mogondo na korageria chimoori chiaye.

English: So is every craftsman and master artisan who passes his time by night as by day, those who cut engravings of signets. His diligence is to make great variety. He sets his heart to preserve likeness in his portraiture, and is careful to finish his work.
Ekegusii: Naboigo ere ase kera omokori emeremo nomobachi onde bwensi ogokora emeremo obotuko n’omobaso; abakobaacha amagena bakorigia chinchera chinyia; nigo bagokora omokia koroisia emegwekano emiya boigo bageesa goika botuko ase ogokoora emeremo yaabo.

English: So too is the smith sitting by the anvil and considering the unwrought iron. The smoke of the fire will waste his flesh. He toils in the heat of the furnace. The noise of the hammer deafens his ear. His eyes are upon the pattern of the object. He will set his heart upon perfecting his works. He will be careful to adorn them perfectly.
Ekegusii: Boigo nomoroisia ebioma ase eriiko riaye ase agosunyuntera ebioma nigo akorengereria keria agokorera ebioma biaye; ere nigo agosambwa nomorero, ogiramora na koremereria riberera, eriogi riogokong’onta nechinyundo riasaria amato aye, na gotogoria amaiso aye gochia ase ekioma keria akoroisia. Ere nigo abegete enkoro yaye ase ogokoora keria akoroisia ase oborigereria obonene goika atabokie omogwekano oria arigetie.

English: So is the potter sitting at his work and turning the wheel around with his feet, who is always anxiously set at his work. He produces his handiwork in quantity.
Ekegusii: Boigo omoroisia chinyongo ase emeremo yaye, ere nigo akorirundia rigari ase okogoro kwaye, ere nigo arendete emeremo yaye goika ogeesa erio aikeranie ekerengo giechinyongo keria keganeirie.

English: He will fashion the clay with his arm and will bend its strength in front of his feet. He will apply his heart to finish the glazing. He will be careful to clean the kiln.
Ekegusii: Ere obomba-bomba esike ase amaboko aye erio oyetacha na amagoro aye. Obeka ebirengererio kegima ase ogokoora emeremo yaye naboigo oba aroro goika nonya mbotuko gochena ekeoreri kiaye.

English: All these put their trust in their hands. Each becomes skillful in his own work.
Ekegusii: Abwo bonsi nigo basemeretie amaboko abo, na kera oyomo nigo are nobomanyi ase emeremo yaye.

English: Without these no city would be inhabited. Men wouldn’t reside as foreigners or walk up and down there.
Ekegusii: Batabeti aroro omochie tokoagacheka; na abanto tibakoyotaarera gose komenya aroro.

English: They won’t be sought for in the council of the people. They won’t mount on high in the assembly. They won’t sit on the seat of the judge. They won’t understand the covenant of judgment. Neither will they declare instruction and judgment. They won’t be found where parables are.
Ekegusii: Nonya nabo, abanto aba tibari gosoa ase ebigambero ebinene gose koegwa obonene ase egeikaranso ki’omosangererekano. Barabwo tibari abanachi ebiina gose tibari nobomanyi igoro yokonachwa ebiina.

English: But they will maintain the fabric of the age. Their prayer is in the handiwork of their craft.
Ekegusii: Tibakonyara gotebereria okonachwa ebiina okwo gose tibana kororekana bagokwana emereng’anio.

English: Not so he who has applied his soul and meditates in the law of the Most High. He will seek out the wisdom of all the ancients and will be occupied with prophecies.
Ekegusii: Korende ere oria okorigia kweorokereria amachiiko y’Omonene, nigo akorigia obong’aini bwa abakoro, na boigo gotunyana aria akwanetwe na ababani.

English: He will keep the sayings of the men of renown and will enter in amidst the subtleties of parables.
Ekegusii: Ere nigo akogacha chinkwana chia abanto abasike, na gotegora chimbachero chire ime ase emereng’anio.

English: He will seek out the hidden meaning of proverbs and be conversant in the dark sayings of parables.
Ekegusii: Nigo akounenkia chingeencho chibisegete ase emereng’anio, nechimbachero chinkong’u tichiri egento ase ere.

English: He will serve among great men and appear before him who rules. He will travel through the land of foreign nations, for he has learned what is good and evil among men.
Ekegusii: Ere nigo akobakorera abanene, na gwesookia ase obosio bwa abarai; nigo agotaara ase chinse chia isiko naboigo bw’emanyeire obuya nobobe bwa abanto.

English: He will apply his heart to return early to the Lord who made him, and will make supplication before the Most High, and will open his mouth in prayer, and will ask for pardon for his sins.
Ekegusii: Nigo akoboka mambia chuni ase okwerua nomokia ase okomosasiima Omonene oyio omotongete; nigo akomoirera Omonene ogosaba kwaye, oigora ebikoba biaye ase ogosorora naboigo gosaba amaabera ase amamocho aye.

English: If the great Lord wills, he will be filled with the spirit of understanding; he will pour forth the words of his wisdom and in prayer give thanks to the Lord.
Ekegusii: Bun’Omonene ore omonene kegima arigetie, ere nigo akomoichoria omonto oyio obong’aini, nere naitororoke amang’ana yobong’aini na komoakera buy’Omonene ase ogosaba kwaye.

English: He will direct his counsel and knowledge, and he will meditate in his secrets.
Ekegusii: Ere nayabogorie amorokererio nobomanyi bwaye buya, na korengereria mono igoro y’obobisi bw’Omonene.

English: He will show the instruction which he has been taught and will glory in the law of the covenant of the Lord.
Ekegusii: Naorokie obomanyi bwaye eorokereirie, na gwetogeria ogochika n’okobwatana kw’Omonene.

English: Many will commend his understanding. So long as the world endures, it won’t be blotted out. His memory won’t depart. His name will live from generation to generation.
Ekegusii: Obomanyi bwaye inabotogigwe nabaanto abange, naborobwo obwo tibokwebwa nonya ng’ake. Chinkuma chiaye tichigosira, nerieta riaye inarinyorwe ase ebiare bionsi.

English: Nations will declare his wisdom. The congregation will proclaim his praise.
Ekegusii: Ebisaku inabirarie obong’aini bwaye, na emeganda y’abanto inayatore ogotogigwa kwaye.

English: If he continues, he will leave a greater name than a thousand. If he finally rests, it is enough for him.
Ekegusii: Ere namenye obogima obotambe, natige erieta rikumete kobua bonsi; nayio nabe amoisanire ere ekero arakwe.

English: Yet more I will utter, which I have thought about. I am filled like the full moon.
Ekegusii: Ninde nayande amange ayio inche narengereirie ndakwane koreng’ana buna omotienyi orabire kegima.

English: Listen to me, you holy children, and bud forth like a rose growing by a brook of water.
Ekegusii: Montegerere inwe abana abaya, mosiiche buna ebisicha bia amaua y’obwanchani ayio asimekire rooche mbarabare.

English: Give a sweet fragrance like frankincense. Put forth flowers like a lily. Scatter a sweet smell and sing a song of praise. Bless the Lord for all his works!
Ekegusii: Sokia rimisu rigiya buna eriekoroso na gosiicha buna amaua yamagoma. Siarera rimisu riaino ase amateera yogotogia mobake Omonene ase amakora aye onsi.

English: Magnify his name and give utterance to his praise with the songs on your lips and with harps! Say this when you utter his praise:
Ekegusii: Togia obonene bw’erieta riaye, motogie goetera ase chingeero chikomotogia, momotogie ase ebikoba biaino namakano.

English: All the works of the Lord are exceedingly good, and every command will be done in its time.
Ekegusii: “Rora ebinto bionsi nigo biatongirwe n’Omonene ekiagera birobio nebiya mono. Kera keria achiikire, kerokio inagekoreke ase ebiro biaye.”

English: No one can say, “What is this?” “Why is that?” for at the proper time they will all be sought out. At his word, the waters stood as a heap, as did the reservoirs of water at the word of his mouth.
Ekegusii: Tobaisa koboria “Ngento kieke?” Gose, “Eke negiaki?” Ekiagera intwe inatwegere ebio bionsi ase chingaki chi’Omonene. Ase ring’ana riaye, amaache nigo agotiga goiteka yebekerania; ase ogokwana kw’omonwa oye amaache nigo amenyete ime ase ekiage kiaye.

English: At his command all his good pleasure is fulfilled. There is no one who can hinder his salvation.
Ekegusii: Ase ogochika kwaye kera keria arigetie nigo kegokoreka, onde taiyo oranyaare gokeyia chinguru chiaye chi’ogotoria.

English: The works of all flesh are before him. It’s impossible to be hidden from his eyes.
Ekegusii: Amakora yebitongwa nigo are maiso marore ase are ere, kende tikeiyo keranyaare kobiseka korwa ase obosio bwaye.

English: He sees from everlasting to everlasting. There is nothing too wonderful for him.
Ekegusii: Ere nigo akorora kare na kare na tikeri egekone ase ere.

English: No one can say, “What is this?” “Why is that?” for all things are created for their own uses.
Ekegusii: Tobaisa kobooria “Nkieke?” Gose “Eke negiaki?” Ekiagera kera egento nigo getongire ase emeremo yaye.

English: His blessing covered the dry land as a river and saturated it as a flood.
Ekegusii: Ogosesenia kwaye nigo kogoichoria ense enyomo buna ase orooche na gochinyiyia buna chioro chia amaache.

English: As he has made the waters salty, so the heathen will inherit his wrath.
Ekegusii: Endamwamu yaye nebiseerie ebisaku, buna koreng’ana akoonchora amaache amaya aba ay’omonyo.

English: His ways are plain to the holy. They are stumbling blocks to the wicked.
Ekegusii: Chinchera chiaye nigo chire chindonge ase baria bamoirogete, korende ase baria ababe chinchera chiaye nigo chire nebitango.

English: Good things are created from the beginning for the good. So are evil things for sinners.
Ekegusii: Ere Omonene nigo atongete ebinto ebiya ase baria bare abaya korwa agwo omochakano bw’ense, korende ase baria ababe ere nigo atongete ebinto ebiya naboigo ebibe.

English: The main things necessary for the life of man are water, fire, iron, salt, wheat flour, and honey, milk, the blood of the grape, oil, and clothing.
Ekegusii: Okogania kwengeencho ase Mwanyabaanto na amaache, omorero, ebioma nomonyo,; obosie, amabeere, oboke, edivai amaguta nechianga.

English: All these things are for good to the godly, but for sinners, they will be turned into evils.
Ekegusii: Ebi bionsi nigo bire ebinto ebiya ase baria bamosigete Omonene, korende birobio nigo bikoonchoka biaba ebibe ase abanyabibe.

English: There are winds that are created for vengeance, and in their fury they lay on their scourges heavily. In the time of reckoning, they pour out their strength, and will appease the wrath of him who made them.
Ekegusii: Nchireo chimbeo chiatongetwe kobaa abanto egesusuro, na chirochio ekero chiabeire nigo chikorwa egesusuro ekenene. Ase chingaki chikiina, nigo chikoorokia okobua kwaye ase ogotoereria endamwamu y’Omotongi obo.

English: Fire, hail, famine, and death— all these are created for vengeance—
Ekegusii: Omorero, embura yamagena, enchara n’oborwaire; ebi bionsi nigo biatongetwe bibae Mwanyabaanto egesusuro.

English: wild beasts’ teeth, scorpions, adders, and a sword punishing the ungodly to destruction.
Ekegusii: Amaino yeching’iti chintindi, amaagaga nechingeenda inse, naboigo omoro okobaa egesusuro baria batamoirogeti Omonene ase ogoita.

English: They will rejoice in his commandment, and will be made ready upon earth when needed. In their seasons, they won’t disobey his command.
Ekegusii: Bionsi nigo biraikeranie ogochika kw’Omonene; inabibe ang’e ase ense komokorera emeremo, na ekero ebiro biraike tibikogenda mamincha nogochika kwaye.

English: Therefore from the beginning I was convinced, and I thought it through and left it in writing:
Ekegusii: Inche nabeire nobomaene igoro ya ayio onsi korwa omochakano; nayarengereirie na koyaitona ase okoyariika.

English: All the works of the Lord are good. He will supply every need in its time.
Ekegusii: Emeremo y’Omonene yonsi nemiya, ere nigo akobaa abanto amagania abo ase ebiro bigwenerete.

English: No one can say, “This is worse than that,” for they will all be well approved in their time.
Ekegusii: Tobaisa goteeba: “Egento eke nekiya kobua keria,” ekiagera ebitoki bia kera ekemo mbirorekane ase ebiro bigwenerete.

English: Now with all your hearts and voices, sing praises and bless the Lord’s name!
Ekegusii: Ase igo bono, tera ogotogia ase enkoro yao yonsi na koritogia erieta ri’Omonene.

English: Great travail is created for every man. A heavy yoke is upon the sons of Adam, from the day of their coming forth from their mother’s womb, until the day for their burial in the mother of all things.
Ekegusii: Emeremo emerito nigo yatongetwe ase Mwanyabaanto bonsi, chigurube chindito nigo chire ase Mwanyabaanto bonsi korwa engaki baiboretwe goika ekero barairane sobo ase orotu, orwo narwo ng’ina abanto bionsi.

English: The expectation of things to come, and the day of death, trouble their thoughts, and cause fear in their hearts.
Ekegusii: Obwoba n’okwegosa kwabo gw’enkoro nokoiroka kwabo nigoro yerituko riogokwa.

English: From him who sits on a throne of glory, even to him who is humbled in earth and ashes,
Ekegusii: Ayio nigo akobanyora bonsi: korwa omorwoti ase obonene bwaye goika ase omwere oria ogoikaransa ase eubi na ase riibu;

English: from him who wears purple and a crown, even to him who is clothed in burlap,
Ekegusii: korwa ase omonda nechianga chiaye chimonyinga nekegogwa ase omotwe oye, goika ase omotaka okwambara chigunia.

English: there is wrath, jealousy, trouble, unrest, fear of death, anger, and strife. In the time of rest upon his bed, his night sleep changes his knowledge.
Ekegusii: Kera ekemo nemoko nekeririanda, obokong’u n’omoichano, obwoba bw’amakweri, obobisa n’eriomana. Goika nonya nekero omonto akoraara ase oborere bwaye chitoro nigo chigwochogania ebirengererio biaye.

English: He gets little or no rest, and afterward in his sleep, as in a day of keeping watch, he is troubled in the vision of his heart, as one who has escaped from the front of battle.
Ekegusii: Nigo akoraara chitoro chinke gose takoraara nonya ng’ake; naende nonya nekero araire nigo anga buna oria orooche. Ere nigo agochaandwa nemegwekano ase ebirengererio biaye, buna omonto oria otamire korwa bosio ase ogoitwa ase esegi.

English: In the very time of his deliverance, he awakens, and marvels that the fear is nothing.
Ekegusii: Ekero agotorigwa, obooka, oichana buna obwoba bwaye tibobwati ekeene.

English: To all creatures, human and animal, and upon sinners sevenfold more,
Ekegusii: Nabo ere igo ase ebitongwa bionsi, ching’iti amo na Mwanyabaanto naende nigo ere boigo ara gatano na kabere ase omonyabibe:

English: come death, bloodshed, strife, sword, calamities, famine, suffering, and plague.
Ekegusii: Amakweri kera engaki, ogoitera amanyinga, ogoitana neseegi, amakweri, enchara, emechaando na amarwaire.

English: All these things were created for the wicked, and because of them the flood came.
Ekegusii: Ebio bionsi nigo biatongetwe ase engencho ya abanyabibe, etoigo nigo yachete ase engencho yababegu.

English: All things that are of the earth turn to the earth again. All things that are of the waters return into the sea.
Ekegusii: Ebinto bionsi biaruete ase riroba mbirane naende ase riroba, buna boigo amaache onsi akoirana gochia ase enyaancha.

English: All bribery and injustice will be blotted out. Good faith will stand forever.
Ekegusii: Kera riaki nobobe, inabitinyigwe, korende okwegena okuya inakobeo ase ebiro bitakoera.

English: The goods of the unjust will be dried up like a river, and like a great thunder in rain will go off in noise.
Ekegusii: Enibo yababe nekamoke buna orooche, inayateke buna ogotitira ase engaki y’embura enyinge.

English: In opening his hands, a man will be made glad; so lawbreakers will utterly fail.
Ekegusii: Omonto omoitongo nanyoore omogooko, korende abamochi inabasire kegima.

English: The children of the ungodly won’t grow many branches, and are as unhealthy roots on a sheer rock.
Ekegusii: Abana ba baria batamoirogeti Omonene Nyasae tibakoba nomoseboko, barabwo nigo banga emeri emerosu ere ime ase egetare ekiomo.

English: The reeds by every water or river bank will be plucked up before all grass.
Ekegusii: Emerande ere mbarabare ase amaache gose orooche eyio nero egochia gotanga korusigwa aroro obonyansi bonde bwonsi botararusigwa aroro.

English: Kindness is like a garden of blessings. Almsgiving endures forever.
Ekegusii: Obuya nigo bonga omogondo bw’amaua oichire ogosesenigwa, n’esadaka ase omonto omotaka nigo ekomenya amatuko onsi.

English: The life of one who labors and is content will be made sweet. He who finds a treasure is better than both.
Ekegusii: Ase omonto oria bwetenenerete na omokori emeremo boigo, obogima nobuya; korende amaya abuete ayio nomonto oria onyorire obobisi bw’emonga.

English: Children and the building of a city establish a name. A blameless wife is better than both.
Ekegusii: Okoba na abana amo noboagacho nigo bikomoa omonto esiko, korende omokungu otari na komocha nigo abuete ebio bionsi bibere.

English: Wine and music rejoice the heart. The love of wisdom is better than both.
Ekegusii: Ebinyugwa bigotindia amo nechingeero chi’okogokia nigo bikomosasokia omonto, korende gwancha obong’aini nigo kere egento ekiya kobua ebio bibere.

English: The pipe and the lute make pleasant melody. A pleasant tongue is better than both.
Ekegusii: Esirimbi amo nekenanda nigo bikorua eriogi rigiya ase ogoteera, korende eriogi riokogokia nigo rire rigiya kobua.

English: Your eye desires grace and beauty, but the green shoots of grain more than both.
Ekegusii: Amaiso nigo akogokia ekieni nobuya bw’omonto, korende obuya bwokomera gwechintetere nigo boetanetie onsi.

English: A friend and a companion is always welcome, and a wife with her husband is better than both.
Ekegusii: Abasani na abanto abamo nigo bare abengeencho mono korende okobwatana kw’omokuungu nomosaacha oye nigo kore okuya kobua.

English: Relatives and helpers are for a time of affliction, but almsgiving rescues better than both.
Ekegusii: Okoba na abamino na gokonyana ase chingaki chi’obokong’u negento ekiya, korende ogokonya abataka nigo kore okuya kobua.

English: Gold and silver will make the foot stand sure, and counsel is esteemed better than both.
Ekegusii: Etaabu nechifeta nigo bikomokong’ia omonto, korende amorokererio amaya nigo abuete ebio bibere.

English: Riches and strength will lift up the heart. The fear of the Lord is better than both. There is nothing lacking in the fear of the Lord. In it, there is no need to seek help.
Ekegusii: Enibo nokobua nigo bikomokong’ia omonto, korende okomoiroka Omonene nokuya kobua. Ekemoa tikeri ase okomoiroka Omonene, oise koba nekeegwa ekio, aye tokogania obokonyi bonde.

English: The fear of the Lord is like a garden of blessing and covers a man more than any glory.
Ekegusii: Okomoiroka Omonene nigo konga omogondo bw’amaua osesenirie, nakorokwo nigo gokomorenda omonto kobua obonene bonde bwonsi.

English: My son, don’t lead a beggar’s life. It is better to die than to beg.
Ekegusii: Aye omwana one, tobaisa komenyera obogima bw’ogosaberera, nigo ere buya aye okwe kobua gosaberera.

English: A man who looks to the table of another, his life is not to be considered a life. He will pollute his soul with another person’s food, but a wise and well-instructed person will beware of that.
Ekegusii: Ekero omonto akomosemeria oyonde amoe endagera, ere nigo akomenya obogima botagwenereti Mwanyabaanto. Ogosemeria endagera y’omonto onde nokwea obosooku; omonto oorokereirie naende omong’aini, ere nigo akobwebachera obogima bonga buna obwo.

English: Begging will be sweet in the mouth of the shameless, but it kindles a fire in his belly.
Ekegusii: Ase omonto otari negesookero, ogosaberera nigo kore asere ogwansu, korende ime yaye nigo oreo omorero okomosaamba.

English: O death, how bitter is the memory of you to a man who is at peace in his possessions, to the man who has nothing to distract him and has prosperity in all things, and who still has strength to enjoy food!
Ekegusii: Aye amakweri! Ogokoinyora nobororo obonene, ase omonto ore moyo oyio omenyete nomorembe ase enibo yaye; ase omonto otari kwegosa, oyio okonyaara kera ring’ana, boigo ere oria ore nechinguru chi’okwegokeria endagera yaye.

English: O death, your sentence is acceptable to a man who is needy and who fails in strength, who is in extreme old age, is distracted about all things, is perverse, and has lost patience!
Ekegusii: Aye amakweri! Ekiina kiao nigo kere ring’ana rigiya ase omotaka oria ore birati boigo oereirwe chinguru, ase omonto omogaka oria ogweichandera kera ring’ana, omonto ore nobosareru boigo oereirwe okoremereria.

English: Don’t be afraid of the sentence of death. Remember those who have been before you and who come after. This is the sentence from the Lord over all flesh.
Ekegusii: Toiroka ogweitia kwa amakweri; oinyore baria bagotang’anerete na baria baragotunyane.

English: And why do you refuse when it is the good pleasure of the Most High? Whether life lasts ten, or a hundred, or a thousand years, there is no inquiry about life in Hades.
Ekegusii: Oyio nomoroberio Omonene ase ebitongwa bionsi. Ninki keragere oamereranie na keri’Omonene anchete goetia? Okomenya emiaka rigana gose elifu teri engencho ase purigatori.

English: The children of sinners are abominable children and they frequent the dwellings of the ungodly.
Ekegusii: Abana ba abanyabibe nokogechia; barabwo nigo bakona koombogana ase emechie etamosigeti Omonene.

English: The inheritance of sinners’ children will perish and with their posterity will be a perpetual disgrace.
Ekegusii: Omwando bw’abana ba abanyabibe nosire, boigo oroiboro rwabo inaromenye ase obosooku kare na kare.

English: Children will complain of an ungodly father, because they suffer disgrace because of him.
Ekegusii: Abana inabamoragererie ise oria otamoirogeti Omonene, ase engencho yobosooku akobarentera abana baye.

English: Woe to you, ungodly men, who have forsaken the law of the Most High God!
Ekegusii: Obobe nobwaino, inwe baria motamoirogeti Nyasae Ore Igoro Mono, inwe baria mwatigire ogochika kw’Omonene!

English: If you are born, you will be born to a curse. If you die, a curse will be your portion.
Ekegusii: Ekero morasesenigwe, okonyora kwaino inagosire; ekero moragoochwe timokoimoka naende; na ekero morakwe, okoragererigwa nakwo moranyore inwe.

English: All things that are of the earth will go back to the earth; so the ungodly will go from a curse to perdition.
Ekegusii: Kende gionsi gekorwa ase orotu, kerokio nigo gekoirana gochi ase orotu, ababe nigo bagochaakera okoragererigwa na gokorera obosiru.

English: The mourning of men is about their bodies; but the evil name of sinners will be blotted out.
Ekegusii: Abanto nigo bakoreera emebere yebitondo, korende erieta ribe ria abanto abanyabibe inarituguterwe are.

English: Have regard for your name, for it continues with you longer than a thousand great treasures of gold.
Ekegusii: Aye oria erieta riao ri’esiko ekiagera rirorio inarigotigarere, inarimenye goetania emonga elifu eyemo y’echitaabu.

English: A good life has its number of days, but a good name continues forever.
Ekegusii: Ebiro bi’okwegokia nigo bire nechingaki chinke igo, korende erieta rigiya nigo rikomenya amatuko atakoera.

English: My children, follow instruction in peace. But wisdom that is hidden and a treasure that is not seen, what benefit is in them both?
Ekegusii: Abana baane, tegerera amorokererio aane momenye nomorembe. Obong’aini bobisegete na emonga etari kororekana, inee ebio ninki bibwate?

English: Better is a man who hides his foolishness than a man who hides his wisdom.
Ekegusii: Nigo ere buya ase omonto obisete oboriri bwaye, kobua oria obisete obong’aini bwaye.

English: Therefore show respect for my words; for it is not good to retain every kind of shame. Not everything is approved by all in good faith.
Ekegusii: Aye oyasike amang’ana aane; ekiagera teri buya orore obosooku ase kera egento na tari kera egento kegwancherwa na kera omonto.

English: Be ashamed of sexual immorality before father and mother, of a lie before a prince and a mighty man,
Ekegusii: Aye obe nobosooku ase ogokora amang’ana amabe ase obosio bwa abaibori, ase ogoteeba oborimo ase obosio bw’omonene gose omogambi;

English: of an offense before a judge and ruler, of iniquity before the congregation and the people, of unjust dealing before a partner and friend,
Ekegusii: ase okomocha ase obosio bw’omonachi ebiina, na ase ogokora obobe ase obosio bw’emeganda;

English: and of theft in the place where you sojourn. Be ashamed in regard of the truth of God and his covenant, of leaning on your elbow at dinner, of contemptuous behavior in the matter of giving and taking,
Ekegusii: ase okomong’aina oyomino ase emeremo gose omosaani, ase okoiba ase aye omenyete.

English: of silence before those who greet you, of looking at a woman who is a prostitute,
Ekegusii: Orore obosooku ase okoborwa obwegenwa ase Omonene na okobwatana kwaye, igoro yokoborwa amasikani ase endagera;

English: of turning away your face from a kinsman, of taking away a portion or a gift, of gazing at a woman who has a husband,
Ekegusii: ase okoba omong’iti ekero ogosabwa egento, ase ogokira ekero ogokwanigwa,

English: of meddling with his maid—and don’t come near her bed, of abusive speech to friends—and after you have given, don’t insult,
Ekegusii: ase okomorigereria omokungu omotaayayi, ase okwanga komokoonya omonto bw’eamate yao;

English: of repeating and speaking what you have heard, and of revealing of secrets.
Ekegusii: ase okomounereria omonto enibo yaye, gose ase okomomogorera omokungu bw’omogisangio oo.

English: Don’t be ashamed of these things, and don’t sin to save face:
Ekegusii: Aya naro amang’ana otarorere obosooku koyakora, gose tokora ebibe ase okwoboa egento abanto barateebe:

English: of the law of the Most High and his covenant, of judgment to do justice to the ungodly,
Ekegusii: Tobaisa korora obosooku ase ogotunyana amachiiko y’Omonene amo n’okobwatana kwaye, tobaisa korora obosooku ase okobanachera ekiina kia boronge abare abamochi.

English: of reckoning with a partner and with travellers, of a gift from the inheritance of friends,
Ekegusii: Tobaisa korora obosooku ase okomokorera omokori emeremo omino gose omoeti, boigo ase okogabana omwando nomosani.

English: of exactness of scales and weights, of getting much or little,
Ekegusii: Tobaisa korora obosooku ase ogokorera ebinto biokorengera bi’ekeene,

English: of bargaining dealing with merchants, of frequent correction of children, and of making the back of an evil slave to bleed.
Ekegusii: kwenyoorera ebitoki ase abaonchoreria, koborokereria abana amasikani amanene, komoaka ebiranya omokori emeremo omobe.

English: A seal is good where an evil wife is. Where there are many hands, lock things up.
Ekegusii: Onye omokungu oo tari omwegeenwa, aye omobise amang’ana ao, na ase abanto abange aye osiekere ebinto biao.

English: Whatever you hand over, let it be by number and weight. In giving and receiving, let all be in writing.
Ekegusii: Aye omanye ekerengo gia kera egento okorwa, omanye ekerengo nomobaro oye, obeke ase amariiko okobwatana nobokoreri.

English: Don’t be ashamed to instruct the unwise and foolish, and one of extreme old age who contends with those who are young. So you will be well instructed indeed and approved in the sight of every living man.
Ekegusii: Torora obosooku komworokereria omoriri na oria otamanyeti gose omogaka okwomana na abasae. Agwo aye tokoba rioka kworokereriigwe, aye nonyoore ogwancherwa ase abanto bonsi.

English: A daughter is a secret cause of wakefulness to a father. Care for her takes away sleep— in her youth, lest she pass the flower of her age; when she is married, lest she should be hated;
Ekegusii: Omogaka obwate omoiseke nigo akogeesa bobisi ase engencho yomoiseke oye; chitang’utang’u chiaye ase omoiseke oye nigo chikomorina chitoro.

English: in her virginity, lest she should be defiled and be with child in her father’s house; when she has a husband, lest she should transgress; and when she is married, lest she should be barren.
Ekegusii: Ekero are omoiseke, ise nigo akwoboa buna nigo ere arasarigwe, gose nabaisa konyora oborito ekero ere are ase enyomba yaye; naende ekero asookire ise nigo akwoboa buna nigo arabaisa koba omogomba.

English: Keep a strict watch over a headstrong daughter, lest she make you a laughingstock to your enemies, a byword in the city and notorious among the people, and shame you in public.
Ekegusii: Omorende mono omoiseke omoenenu, onye taribo ere nagere osekererwe na ababisa bao, aye obe gokogambwa na oyore nerieta ribe ase abanto, akorentere obosooku ase risango riabaanto.

English: Don’t gaze at every beautiful body. Don’t sit in the midst of women.
Ekegusii: Tobaisa komogorera obuya bw’omoto onde bwensi, gose goikaransa kogamba nabakungu.

English: For from garments comes a moth, and from a woman comes a woman’s wickedness.
Ekegusii: Ekiagera esukubi nigo egosoka korwa ime yechianga, na obobe bw’omokuungu nigo bokorwa ase omokungu.

English: Better is the wickedness of a man than a pleasant woman, a woman who puts you to shame and disgrace.
Ekegusii: Obobe bw’omosaacha nigo bore gaigai kobua obuya bw’omokuungu; omokungu nere okorenta obosooku na amachaaya.

English: I will make mention now of the works of the Lord, and will declare the things that I have seen. The Lord’s works are in his words.
Ekegusii: Bono inche nimbainyorie emeremo y’Omonene na koraria aria narorire: emeremo y’Omonene nigo egokoreka goetera ase ring’ana riaye.

English: The sun that gives light looks at all things. The Lord’s work is full of his glory.
Ekegusii: Risase nigo rikomoreka kera egento kere inse yokomoreka kwaye, emeremo y’Omonene nigo eichire obonene bwaye.

English: The Lord has not given power to the saints to declare all his marvelous works, which the Almighty Lord firmly settled, that the universe might be established in his glory.
Ekegusii: Tari oyomo ase abamalaika b’Omonene oranyaare gwatora amakora aye onsi yogokumia ay’Omonene atenenirie. Erio ense etenene bokong’u ase obonene bwaye.

English: He searches out the deep and the heart. He has understanding of their secrets. For the Most High knows all knowledge. He sees the signs of the world.
Ekegusii: Ere nigo akorigereria emerindo n’echinkoro chia Mwanyabaanto, na korora emeroberio yaabo emebe. Ekiagera Omonene nigo amanyete chisemi chionsi chiria, naende nigo amanyete ebimanyererio bie chingaki.

English: He declares the things that are past and the things that shall be, and reveals the traces of hidden things.
Ekegusii: Ere nigo akoyararia aria abeire na aaria agochia goocha, naboigo kobisioria rinde rionsi ribisegete.

English: No thought escapes him. There is not a word hidden from him.
Ekegusii: Tikeiyo ekerengererio keramoete, tiriri nonya nering’ana erimo riranyaare kwebisa are korwa ase are ere.

English: He has ordered the mighty works of his wisdom. He is from everlasting to everlasting. Nothing has been added to them, nor diminished from them. He had no need of any counselor.
Ekegusii: Ere orobeirie obonene bw’obong’aini bwaye. Nere bweka oreo korwa kare goika kare. Ere takonyaara komenterwa egento gose kourwa egento; gose tarigeti omonto onde bwensi abe omotebereria oye.

English: How desirable are all his works! One may see this even in a spark.
Ekegusii: Inaki emeremo yaye ere eyokogookia! Inaki ekomesa emeremo yaye!

English: All these things live and remain forever in all manner of uses. They are all obedient.
Ekegusii: Ebinto ebio bionsi nao bire naende inabimenye kare na kare, nabirobio nigo bikomoigwera kera engaki biganeirie.

English: All things are in pairs, one opposite the other. He has made nothing imperfect.
Ekegusii: Ebitongire bionsi nigo birobeirie bibere bibere kera ekemo mamincha yekende; na tikeri akorete getari egeikeranu.

English: One thing establishes the good things of another. Who could ever see enough of his glory?
Ekegusii: Egento ekemo nigo kegoikerania obuya bw’egento kende. Ning’o oria oranyaare korosa ase okorigereria obonene bwaye?

English: The pride of the heavenly heights is the clear sky, the appearance of heaven, in the spectacle of its glory.
Ekegusii: Obonene bwa igoro aaria nokomesa kw’obware bwaye bwa igoro; obware bwaye nigo bokororekana bokomekameka ase obonene bwaye.

English: The sun, when it appears, bringing tidings as it rises, is a marvelous instrument, the work of the Most High.
Ekegusii: Ekero erioba rikooroka, rirorio nigo rikoraria okomesa kwaye. Ekio negento kiogokumia ere Omonene atongete.

English: At noon, it dries up the land. Who can stand against its burning heat?
Ekegusii: Rirorio nigo rigokamokia ense ase omobaso, ning’o oranyaare koremereria ogosamba kwaye?

English: A man tending a furnace is in burning heat, but the sun three times more, burning up the mountains, breathing out fiery vapors, and sending out bright beams, it blinds the eyes.
Ekegusii: Omonto nigo akoigereria riiko oigwa ogasamba kwaye, korende risase nigo rigosaamba ebitunwa goika ara gatato boigo. Risase nigo rikoraga okomesa kwaye kwomorero, na okomekameka kwamasase kwaukoria amaiso.

English: Great is the Lord who made it. At his word, he hastens on its course.
Ekegusii: Inaki are omonene Omobui oria oritongete, naende oyio ase ogochika kwaye rigendererete ase orogendo rwaye.

English: The moon marks the changing seasons, declares times, and is a sign for the world.
Ekegusii: Boigo omotienyi nigo okomesa ase ebiro biaye, oro boigo nekiorokererio getakoera; nigo okoraa chingaki amo n’ebiro.

English: From the moon is the sign of feast days, a light that wanes when it completes its course.
Ekegusii: Chingaki chia amatuko amanene nigo chikworokigwa nomotienyi; oborabu bwaye nigo bokoba obonene naende bwakea.

English: The month is called after its name, increasing wonderfully in its changing— an instrument of the army on high, shining in the structure of heaven,
Ekegusii: “Omotienyi” bw’amatuko yomotienyi nigo oeire erieta kobwatekana nokororekana kwaye, oro nigo ogokiina ase chinchera chi’ogokumia ase ebiro biaye; oro omonyene nekiorokererio kia abarwani ba igoro ekero okomesa ase obwaro bwaye aria igoro.

English: the beauty of heaven, the glory of the stars, an ornament giving light in the highest places of the Lord.
Ekegusii: Okomesa gweching’enang’eni nigo gokworokia obuya bwo obwaro bwa igoro Omonene buna bochabeire kegima aria igoro.

English: At the word of the Holy One, they will stand in due order. They won’t faint in their watches.
Ekegusii: Asa ogochika kwaye ere Omochenu nigo chiteneine aria ase chiachikeretwe; chirochio tichiri gotamboka nonya ng’ake ensemo yabo y’oborendi.

English: Look at the rainbow, and praise him who made it. It is exceedingly beautiful in its brightness.
Ekegusii: Rigereria omokubinyongo, oro nigo okomotogia ere oria oyotongete omokubunyongo nigo okogokia mono ase okomekameka kwaye!

English: It encircles the sky with its glorious circle. The hands of the Most High have stretched it out.
Ekegusii: Oro nigo oetanaine obwaro ase ekeng’ese ekemo kere ekiya, amaboko y’Omonene naro aywareretie.

English: By his commandment, he makes the snow fall and swiftly sends the lightnings of his judgment.
Ekegusii: Ase ogochika kw’Omonene obogoria amagena y’embura naboigo okomesa kw’embura buna ere akoyochiika gokora.

English: Therefore the storehouses are opened, and clouds fly out like birds.
Ekegusii: Boigo ebiage biaye nigo bikoigoka, amare airuruka korwa aroro buna chinyoni.

English: By his mighty power, he makes the clouds strong and the hailstones are broken in pieces.
Ekegusii: Ere ase obonene bwaye, nigo agosangereria amare na gwatia amagena agandire aba embura y’amagena.

English: At his appearing, the mountains will be shaken. At his will, the south wind will blow.
Ekegusii: Ekero akororekana, ebigoro nigo bigotengecha, ase okogania kwaye omwaga o Irianyi nigo okogusa.

English: The voice of his thunder rebukes the earth. So does the northern storm and the whirlwind. Like birds flying down, he sprinkles the snow. It falls down like the lighting of locusts.
Ekegusii: Eriogi riaye riokogukura nigo agotogonyera ense boigo nokogusa kwomwaga o sugusu ne ekerambauti. Nigo agoserebania okoganda kwaba gwaika gocha inse buna chinyoni, ee buna chingige chikogwa ase riroba.

English: The eye is dazzled at the beauty of its whiteness. The heart is amazed as it falls.
Ekegusii: Nigo togoichana korigereria obuya bw’oborabu bwaye, na twakumia ekero okogwa.

English: He also pours out frost on the earth like salt. When it is freezes, it has points like thorns.
Ekegusii: Ere nigo agosiarera obonyiu buna omonyo, na ekero b’okobwatana birorekana ebinto biteneine buna amagwa.

English: The cold north wind blows and ice freezes on the water. It settles on every pool of water. The water puts it on like it was a breastplate.
Ekegusii: Nigo akogusia omwaga omokendu o sugusu, amagena yembura aranda igoro ase amaache, atuberera chintuboka chionsi chia amaache, yaba buna enguba y’ogwekengera.

English: It will devour the mountains, burn up the wilderness, and consume the green grass like fire.
Ekegusii: Obisamba ebitunwa bw’erorooro naboigo kobirura ebitii, na gosusania obonyansi oborere buna obore ase omorero.

English: A mist coming speedily heals all things. A dew coming after heat brings cheerfulness.
Ekegusii: Korende riire riaonchora kera egento naende, ekero obonyiu bokororekana na gokendia.

English: By his counsel, he has calmed the deep and planted islands in it.
Ekegusii: Ase obong’aini bwaye nigo agotoereria enyancha enene na kobeeka ebisinka aroro.

English: Those who sail on the sea tell of its dangers. We marvel when we hear it with our ears.
Ekegusii: Baria bagotaara goetera ase chinyaancha nigo bagoteeba emegano yobwoba boreo, naintwe nigo togoichanigwa nayio tokoigwa.

English: There are also those strange and wondrous works in it— variety of all that has life and the huge creatures of the sea.
Ekegusii: Agwo ime ase enyancha mbireo ebitongwa bire ebiokogosa na kwoboyia, ebitongire ebinene kobua na ebiechingeencho chionsi bire moyo.

English: Because of him, his messengers succeed. By his word, all things hold together.
Ekegusii: Omonene nigo akomokora kera omotomwa oye konyora amaya, ase ring’ana riaye nigo agotenenia kera egetongwa.

English: We may say many things, but couldn’t say enough. The summary of our words is, “He is everything!”
Ekegusii: Natoisa goteeba amange, intwe titokonyaara goikera omoerio, ase obweng’e; “Omonene nere kera egento.”

English: How could we have strength to glorify him? For he is himself the greater than all his works.
Ekegusii: Intwe ng’ai toranyoore chinguru chi’okomotogia? Ekiagera ere nigo are omonene kobua emeremo yaye yonsi.

English: The Lord is awesome and exceedingly great! His power is marvelous!
Ekegusii: Omonene nigo are oyo bw’okoirokia naende omonene mono, okobua kwaye nokwogokumia mono.

English: Glorify the Lord and exalt him as much as you can! For even yet, he will surpass that. When you exalt him, summon your full strength. Don’t be weary, because you can’t praise him enough.
Ekegusii: Ekero aye okomotogia Omonene, motogie buna okonyaara, ekiagera ere nigo aetanetie ayio moimokereria igoro, moimokererie igoro ase okobua kwao gwonsi. Aye tobaisa korosa ekiagera tokonyaara komotogia buna egwenerete okore.

English: Who has seen him, that he may describe him? Who can magnify him as he is?
Ekegusii: Ere ning’o oyio omorooche ere erio anyare korwa omogano buna ere are? Gose, ning’o oranyaare komotogia aikeranie ekerengo kemogwenerete?

English: Many things greater than these are hidden, for we have seen just a few of his works.
Ekegusii: Amakumia amanene kobua aya, nigo abisegete, ekiagera twarorire emeremo yaye emeke igo.

English: For the Lord made all things. He gave wisdom to the godly.
Ekegusii: Ekiagera Omonene okorire ebinto bionsi, erio abae esiko baria bamoirogete.

English: Let us now praise famous men, our ancestors in their generations.
Ekegusii: Bono tiga tobatogie abanto b’esiko, abagaaka baito n’ebiare biaetire.

English: The Lord created great glory in them— his mighty power from the beginning.
Ekegusii: Omonene nigo abaete esiko enene, akabakinia koba abanene korwa amatuko a kare.

English: Some ruled in their kingdoms and were men renowned for their power, giving counsel by their understanding. Some have spoken in prophecies,
Ekegusii: Mbareo baria baraete amarwoti abo, abanto abanene ase okobua kwabo; abatebereria baichire nobong’aini abararia b’obobani.

English: leaders of the people by their counsels, and by their understanding, giving instruction for the people. Their words in their instruction were wise.
Ekegusii: Abange nigo baraete ebisaku ase ebirengererio biabo, bakaba nobong’aini amo nechiseemi ase okonyorera abanto obuya, bare ne chiseemi ase amang’ana na amorokererio abo.

English: Some composed musical tunes, and set forth verses in writing,
Ekegusii: Nigo baroisetie chingeero ase obong’aini bwabo, bakaroisia emeino na koyeriika.

English: rich men endowed with ability, living peaceably in their homes.
Ekegusii: Barabwo nigo barenge abatenenku bare nobonda obonge, boigo bamenyete n’obotoereru ase chinka chiabo.

English: All these were honored in their generations, and were outstanding in their days.
Ekegusii: Abwo bonsi nigo basikire ase ebiare biabo, bakaba nobonene ase chingaki chiabo.

English: Some of them have left a name behind them, so that others declare their praises.
Ekegusii: Abande ase egati yabo, bagatiga erieta rigiya ase ense, na abanto bakararia chinkuma chiabo goika reero iga.

English: But of others, there is no memory. They perished as though they had not been. They become as though they had not been born, they and their children after them.
Ekegusii: Mbareo boigo abande baria batainyoiri, abwo bagendete bakaba buna baria batamenyete ase ense. Nabo banga buna baria bataiboretwe, barabwo amo na abana babo barwete magega.

English: But these were men of mercy, whose righteous deeds have not been forgotten.
Ekegusii: Korende baria bande nigo barenge abanto abaya, abwo amakora abo amaya atana kwebwa.

English: A good inheritance remains with their offspring. Their children are within the covenant.
Ekegusii: Chinibo chiabo nigo chigotigara ase ababiare baabo, na oyio noro omwando obo.

English: Their offspring stand fast, with their children, for their sakes.
Ekegusii: Ababiare baabo nigo bagotunyana okobwatana gwakoretwe ase bare, na ase engencho eyio barabwo inabagenderere gokora boigo botambe.

English: Their offspring will remain forever. Their glory won’t be blotted out.
Ekegusii: Chinderia chiabo inachigenderere kare na kare, na esiko yaabo tegotinyigwa.

English: Their bodies were buried in peace. Their name lives to all generations.
Ekegusii: Emebere yaabo nigo yatindegetwe ase omorembe, amarieta abo nigo agendererete kobao ekiare ekemo goika ekende.

English: People will declare their wisdom. The congregation proclaims their praise.
Ekegusii: Abanto inabakwane obong’aini bwabo, nerisango ria abanto ndirarie chinkuma chiabo.

English: Enoch pleased the Lord, and was taken up, an example of repentance to all generations.
Ekegusii: Enoku nigo amogogetie Omonene, ere akairwa igoro. Ere akaba omogwekano omuya bw’okoorokia ebibe ase ebiare bionsi.

English: Noah was found perfect and righteous. In the season of wrath, he kept the race alive. Therefore a remnant was left on the earth when the flood came.
Ekegusii: Nuhu akarorekana koba omoikeranu na ore namasikani; ekero ogosirigwa gwachete, akaba omochakano omoyia o Mwanyabaanto. Ekiagera ngoetera asere abanto batigarete ase ense ekero etoigo yachete.

English: Everlasting covenants were made with him, that all flesh should no more be blotted out by a flood.
Ekegusii: Omonene agakora okobwatana amo nere gotakoera, egere ebitongwa tibibaisa naende gosirigwa ase enchera y’etoigo.

English: Abraham was a great father of a multitude of nations. There was none found like him in glory,
Ekegusii: Aburamu nigo arenge omogaka omanyekanete ase ebisaku ebinge, gose tarengeo omonto ore nesiko buna ere.

English: who kept the law of the Most High, and was taken into covenant with him. In his flesh he established the covenant. When he was tested, he was found faithful.
Ekegusii: Akabwatia amachiiko y’Omonene, nere Omonene agakora okobwatana nere, agaikerania ase omobere oye ekemanyererio giokobwatana okwo, boigo ekero Aburamu nigo atemetwe, akarorekana ere ore omoikeranu.

English: Therefore he assured him by an oath that the nations would be blessed through his offspring, that he would multiply him like the dust of the earth, exalt his offspring like the stars, and cause them to inherit from sea to sea, and from the Euphrates River to the utmost parts of the earth.
Ekegusii: Erio Omonene akamoriera chiira ogoteeba buna ebisaku bionsi inabisesenigwe goetera ase oroiboro rwaye; buna oroiboro rwaye inarobe nobonge buna oyo orotu rwense. Buna inababe abange buna ching’enang’eni na omwando obo buna orwaro oromo rwe enyaancha goika oronde, gochaakera ase orooche rw’Eufarati goika chinsinyo chi’ense.

English: In Isaac also, he established the same assurance for Abraham his father’s sake, the blessing of all men, and the covenant.
Ekegusii: Boigo Omonene akamoa Isaka erio aikeranie eira eria eria ase engencho ya Aburamu Ise. Ogosesenigwa ase abanto bonsi nokobwatana kwaye,

English: He made it rest upon the head of Jacob. He acknowledged him in his blessings, gave to him by inheritance, and divided his portions. He distributed them among twelve tribes.
Ekegusii: akabibeeka ase Yakobo. Akamotenenia Yakobo ase ogosesenigwa kwaye, akamoa ense eria ebe eyaye ere omonyene na koyegaba ase egati yebisaku ikomi na bibere.

English: He brought out of him a man of mercy, who found favor in the sight of all people, a man loved by God and men, even Moses, whose memory is blessed.
Ekegusii: Korwa ase Yakobo, omonene akamochoora omonto omuya oyio onyorete ogwancherwa ase egati ya abanto bonsi, aganchwa na abanto amo na Nyasae. Ere oyio nere Musa oyio tokogooka ase okomoinyora.

English: He made him equal to the glory of the saints, and magnified him in the fears of his enemies.
Ekegusii: Omonene akamokora abe nokobua buna okwa abamalaika, na oyorenge n’chinguru chi’okoirokia ase obosio bwa ababisa baye.

English: By his words he caused the wonders to cease. God glorified him in the sight of kings. He gave him commandments for his people and showed him part of his glory.
Ekegusii: Ase ring’ana ria Musa, Omonene agatenenia ebikone biria, akamokora gokuma ase obosio bw’abarwoti. Omonene akamoa Musa amachiiko ase engencho ya abanto baye, akamworokia orobega rw’obonene bwaye.

English: He sanctified him in his faithfulness and meekness. He chose him out of all people.
Ekegusii: Ase obwegenwa noboitongo bwaye, akamochoora korwa ase egati ya Mwanyabaanto bonsi.

English: He made him to hear his voice, led him into the thick darkness, and gave him commandments face to face, even the law of life and knowledge, that he might teach Jacob the covenant, and Israel his judgments.
Ekegusii: Omonene akamwanchera Musa koigwa eriogi riaye, akamoraa ase egati yomosunte omonene. Akamoa amachiiko aye obosio ase obosio, amachiiko y’obogima n’echiseemi, erio anyare koborokereria abanto ba Yakobo okobwatana kwaye, Koborokereria Abaisraeli amaganio aye.

English: He exalted Aaron, a holy man like Moses, even his brother, of the tribe of Levi.
Ekegusii: Omonene akamoimokereria igoro Aroni momura omwabo Musa, omonto omochenu buna Musa oyobwegesaku kia Lawi.

English: He established an everlasting covenant with him, and gave him the priesthood of the people. He blessed him with stateliness, and dressed him in a glorious robe.
Ekegusii: Agakora nere okobwatana gotakoera na akamoa obokuani bwa abanto baye. Akamoa chingobo chiesiko, akamobeekera ogochaberwa gwesiko.

English: He clothed him in perfect splendor, and strengthened him with symbols of authority: the linen trousers, the long robe, and the ephod.
Ekegusii: Omonene akamobekera Aroni oboikeranu obonene, akamotenenia ase ebimanyererio biokobua: erioo esirwari, ogochaberwa ase omotwe oye amo ne’kiebisio egechenu kia gekuba.

English: He encircled him with pomegranates; with many golden bells around him, to make a sound as he went, to make a sound that might be heard in the temple, for a reminder for the children of his people;
Ekegusii: Akamoetananeria chinchigiri amo nebingere ebinge bi’etaabu, ebio biranyaare goaka eriogi ekero agotaara, agwekane ase Hekalu, buna ekemanyererio ase abanto baye.

English: with a holy garment, with gold, blue, and purple, the work of the embroiderer; with an oracle of judgment—Urim and Thummim;
Ekegusii: Akamobeekera eganchwa enchenu ye etaabu, ye buru ne erangi e monyinga eyio yasonetwe nomosoni egiata, akamoa ebinto biokworokia ogotia ogoikeranu.

English: with twisted scarlet, the work of the craftsman; with precious stones engraved like a signet, in a setting of gold, the work of the jeweller, for a reminder engraved in writing, after the number of the tribes of Israel;
Ekegusii: Akamobeekera amarionya amabariri, ayio aroisetigwe nomoroisia okumete, na amagena yerigori bibachire buna ebonyi na gotobekwa etaabu, bionsi ebio biaroisetigwe nomoroisia bw’ebinto biebinto bigosamberwa ase omorero; biaroisetigwe ase okweinyoria omobaro bw’ebisaku bi’abaanto ba Israeli.

English: with a crown of gold upon the mitre, having engraved on it, as on a signet, “HOLINESS”, an ornament of honor, the work of an expert, the desires of the eyes, goodly and beautiful.
Ekegusii: Korwa ase oroiboro rwa Yakobo akamoorokia omonto obwate ogwancherwa ase abanto bonsi, ere aganchwa n’Omonene boigo na abanto bonsi. Oyio nere Musa tokogoka komoinyora.

English: Before him there never have been anything like it. No stranger put them on, but only his sons and his offspring perpetually.
Ekegusii: Tibiarengeo ebinto ebiya buna ebio agwo omochakano, na omogeni taiyo bweboyetie ebinto binga buna ebio. Abanto b’oroiboro rwaye boka nabwo beboyetie ebinto ebio ase chingaki chitakoera.

English: His sacrifices shall be wholly burned, twice every day continually.
Ekegusii: Ebing’wanso akorwa nigo bigosambwa bire ebigima, na birobio nigo birabe bikoruugwa ara kabere ase kera rituko.

English: Moses consecrated him, and anointed him with holy oil. It was an everlasting covenant with him and to his offspring, all the days of heaven, to minister to the Lord, to serve as a priest, and to bless his people in his name.
Ekegusii: Ere Musa akamwatanana Aroni, na komoaka amaguta amachenu. Kogakorwa okobwatana gotakoera ase egati yaye ere amo noroiboro rwaye, erio barabwo bamokorere Omonene ase obokuani na gosesenia abanto ase erieta riaye.

English: He chose him out of all living to offer sacrifice to the Lord— incense, and a sweet fragrance, for a memorial, to make atonement for your people.
Ekegusii: Omonene akamomwatanana Aroni kowa ase egati ya abanto bonsi, amorwere Omonene ekeng’wanso, aute ekoroso yokoinyoria ebwate ogotioka okuya, na kobakorera abanto okobwatana.

English: He gave to him in his commandments, authority in the covenants of judgments, to teach Jacob the testimonies, and to enlighten Israel in his law.
Ekegusii: Akamoa aaroni amachiiko aye, akamoa okobua gwokorwa amachiiko na kogaamba, koborokereria abanto ba Yakobo amachiiko aye na kobamorekera igoro yamachiiko aye.

English: Strangers conspired against him and envied him in the wilderness: Dathan and Abiram with their company, and the congregation of Korah, with wrath and anger.
Ekegusii: Abanto ba isiko bagateebania bamoamererie Musa, bakamotwarera ribero aria ase erooro. Barabwo nabwo Dathani, Abiramu amo noyomwabo, Kora amo nekeombe kiabo bagooka nendamwamu.

English: The Lord saw it, and it displeased him. In the wrath of his anger, they were destroyed. He did wonders upon them, to consume them with flaming fire.
Ekegusii: Ekere Omonene ayaroche ayio, ere tagokigwa, ase obororo bwaye obonene akabasiria. Agakora ebikone ase bare akabasamba nebieri bi’omorero.

English: He added glory to Aaron, and gave him a heritage. He divided to him the first fruits of the increase, and prepared bread of first fruits in abundance.
Ekegusii: Erio akamomentera Aroni esiko yaye, na komoa omwano oye ere omonyene: oboronge igoro ase okorwegwa kwogotongora.

English: For they eat the sacrifices of the Lord, which he gave to him and to his offspring.
Ekegusii: Endagera yabo nigo ekorwa ase ebing’wanso bi’Omonene; Omonene akamoa Aroni ebinto ebio ere amo na oroiboro rwaye.

English: However, in the land of the people, he has no inheritance, and he has no portion among the people, for the Lord himself is your portion and inheritance.
Ekegusii: Korende ere Aroni tarenge nomwando oye ase ense, tarenge nensemo yaye ase egati ya abanto; ekiagera ebing’wanso bi’Omonene nabio omwando oye.

English: Phinehas the son of Eleazar is the third in glory, in that he was zealous in the fear of the Lord, and stood fast when the people turned away, and he made atonement for Israel.
Ekegusii: Finehasi mosinto bw’Eliazaro noyogatato ase abanto abwo b’esiko, ekiagera ere arenge nokogania okonene gwokomoiroka Omonene, agatenena bokong’u ekero abanto bonsi babeete mamincha, akaba ang’e ase obuya bwaye bw’enkoro, na kobasabera Abaisraeli okwaberwa kw’ebibe.

English: Therefore, a covenant of peace was established for him, that he should be leader of the sanctuary and of his people, that he and his offspring should have the dignity of the priesthood forever.
Ekegusii: Ase ayio Omonene agakora okobwatana kwomorembe amo nere, buna ere nabe omorai bwa aase yogosasiimerwa ase abanto baye, ere amo na ababiare baye babe negetari giesiko yobokuhani getakoera.

English: Also he made a covenant with David the son of Jesse, of the tribe of Judah. The inheritance of the king is his alone from son to son. So the inheritance of Aaron is also to his seed.
Ekegusii: Nkwarengeo okobwatana konde na Daudi, mosinto o Yese bw’egesaku kiaYuda, omwando bwo oborwoti bwaye ase omwana gochia ase oyonde, korende omwando ase Aroni obe ase ababiare baye bonsi.

English: May God give you wisdom in your heart to judge his people in righteousness, that their good things may not be abolished, and that their glory may endure for all their generations.
Ekegusii: Omonene agosesenie nobong’aini ase enkoro yao, obagambere abanto baye ase oboronge, erio okogenderera kwabo tigosira na esiko yaabo etigare ase ebiare bionsi.

English: Joshua the son of Nun was valiant in war, and was the successor of Moses in prophecies. He was made great according to his name for the saving of God’s elect, to take vengeance on the enemies that rose up against them, that he might give Israel their inheritance.
Ekegusii: Yoshua mosinto o Nuni nigo arenge egeata ase esegi, nere nigo arenge buna erieta riaye, omotooria bwa abachoore ba Omonene, akabaakanera egesiomba ase ababisa abwo barenge kobarwania erio akabairaneria Abaisraeli omwando obo.

English: How he was glorified in the lifting up his hands, and in stretching out his sword against the cities!
Ekegusii: Ere nigo abete nomogooko ekero aimogetie amaboko aye igoro, ekero arenge koimokia na koraga omoro oye gochia ase obomenyo bw’ebisaku.

English: Who before him stood so firm? For the Lord himself brought his enemies to him.
Ekegusii: Ning’o naende omogwekaine konya ere atarabao? Ekiagera ere arwanete esegi y’Omonene.

English: Didn’t the sun go back by his hand? Didn’t one day become as two?
Ekegusii: Inee, risase tiriatenenete ase okoimokererigwa kwa amaboko aye? Inee, rituko tirianyarete gotambeigwa rikarengana amatuko abere?

English: He called upon the Most High, the Mighty One, when his foes pressed in all around him, and the great Lord heard him.
Ekegusii: Yoshua nigo amosabete Omonene Omobui ore n’Okobua, ekero ababisa bamoetananete korwa ase kera ensinyo.

English: With hailstones of mighty power, he caused war to break violently upon the nation, and on the slope he destroyed those who resisted, so that the nations might know his armor, how he fought in the sight of the Lord; for he followed the Mighty One.
Ekegusii: Nere Omonene ore n’Okobua, akamoiraneria akabatomera embura ere nechinguru ya amagena. Omonene agasaagana egesaku ase egetirimboko gia Beth-horoni akabasiria bonsi baria barenge komoengereria. Ekagera ebisaku bikerorera obuya bwebirwanero biaye, buna ere nigo arenge korwana ase obosio Omonene, ekiagera ere amotunyanete Omonene nenkoro yaye yonsi.

English: Also in the time of Moses, he did a work of mercy— he and Caleb the son of Jephunneh— in that they withstood the adversary, hindered the people from sin, and stilled their wicked complaining.
Ekegusii: Ase amatuko a Musa, Yoshua nigo arenge omwegenwa ere amo na Kalebu mosinto o Yefune, bagatenena bokong’u koengererania nomosangererekano, bakabatanga abanto tibakora ebibe, na gokiria okwemurungania kwa abanto abwo.

English: And of six hundred thousand people on foot, they two alone were preserved to bring them into their inheritance, into a land flowing with milk and honey.
Ekegusii: Ase egati ya abanto chilifu amagana atano nomo (600,000) barenge ase orogendo, nabwo babere boka batigetwe bakabaraa abaaanto goika ase ense eria yaabo, ense yarenge goiteka obooke na amabeere.

English: The Lord gave strength to Caleb, and it remained with him to his old age, so that he entered the hill country, and his offspring obtained it for an inheritance,
Ekegusii: Omonene akamoa Kalebu okobua, nere akaba nakorokwo goika obogotu bwaye.

English: that all the children of Israel might see that it is good to follow the Lord.
Ekegusii: Erio abanto bonsi b’egesaku kia Abaisraeli bakarora obuya bwokomotunyan’Omonene.

English: Also the judges, every one by his name, all whose hearts didn’t engage in immorality, and who didn’t turn away from the Lord— may their memory be blessed!
Ekegusii: Erio bakabwatia abagaambi, kera oyomo nechinkuma chiaye, barabwo tibang’ainegete komotiga Omonene na gosasiima emegwekano. Barabwo bakainyorwa emiaka yonsi ase chinkuma chiabo.

English: May their bones flourish again out of their place. May the name of those who have been honored be renewed in their children.
Ekegusii: Tiga emebere yaabo etware chinguru aaria ase batindegetwe, na amarieta abo abwo bamoirogete Omonene amenye goetera ase oroiboro rwabo.

English: Samuel, the prophet of the Lord, loved by his Lord, established a kingdom and anointed princes over his people.
Ekegusii: Samweli nigo anchetwe n’Omonene. Ekero arenge omobani Omonene agachaakia oborwoti, akabaaka amaguta abarai ba abanto.

English: By the law of the Lord he judged the congregation, and the Lord watched over Jacob.
Ekegusii: Akabagaambera emeganda ya abanto kobwatekana nogochika kw’Omonene, nere Omonene akabarenda abanto ba Yakobo.

English: By his faithfulness he was proved to be a prophet. By his words he was known to be faithful in vision.
Ekegusii: Ase obwegenwa bwaye akaenekiwa buna ere ekeene nomobani, ase amang’ana aye akaba omoringoria ogosemerigwa.

English: When his enemies pressed on him on every side, he called upon the Lord, the Mighty One, with the offering of the suckling lamb.
Ekegusii: Akamosaba Omonene Omobui, ekero ere aetananetwe na ababisa ase kera ensinyo, akamorwera Omonene ekeng’wanso ki’emanwa yeng’ondi.

English: Then the Lord thundered from heaven. He made his voice heard with a mighty sound.
Ekegusii: Erio Omonene akaruma korwa igoro, agakora eriogi riaye rikaigweka ase ogotitira okonene.

English: He utterly destroyed the rulers of the Tyrians and all the princes of the Philistines.
Ekegusii: Akabasiarera are abarai b’egesaku gia Turo, amo na abarai bonsi ba Abafilisiti.

English: Before the time of his age-long sleep, he testified in the sight of the lord and his anointed, “I have not taken any man’s goods, so much as a sandal;” and no one accused him.
Ekegusii: Ekero ere atararaara ase chitoro chiaye chi’omoerio, Samweli akaba kirori ase obosio bw’Omonene na omochore oye buna ere tanyaarete kobogoria enibo ya monto onde bwensi, gose nonya nenuga yebikoroto. Tabeteo omonto orenge aba komosoera.

English: Even after he fell asleep, he prophesied, and showed the king his end, and lifted up his voice from the earth in prophecy, to blot out the wickedness of the people.
Ekegusii: Akagenderera korwa obobani nonya nekero ere akuure akamobisoreria omorwoti igoro yomoerio oye; akarusia eriogi korwa ime ye embeera, akarua obobani ase ogosiria obobe bwa abanto.

English: After him, Nathan rose up to prophesy in the days of David.
Ekegusii: Erio boigo akabwatia Nathani; oyio orenge omobani ase amatuko y’omorwoti Daudi.

English: As is the fat when it is separated from the peace offering, so was David separated from the children of Israel.
Ekegusii: Koreng’ana buna amaguta yogokora ebing’wanso bi’omorembe agochoorwa na kogachwa ase emeremo y’Omonene, nabo Daudi aatananetwe korwa ase egati ya Abaisraeli.

English: He played with lions as with kids, and with bears as with lambs of the flock.
Ekegusii: Ere agakora egosori ase chindo buna oyore ase chimbori na chitokoro buna oyore ase egati yechimbori.

English: In his youth didn’t he kill a giant, and take away reproach from the people when he lifted up his hand with a sling stone, and beat down the boasting Goliath?
Ekegusii: Ase obosae bwaye agaita rimonto akabaruseria abanto baye amachaaya yokorama kwaye. Akaruta rigena ase enduruche yaye akamoiyeria Goliato omwetogia.

English: For he called upon the Most High Lord, and he gave him strength in his right hand to kill a man mighty in war, to exalt the horn of his people.
Ekegusii: Ekiagera ere amosororete Omonene Nyasae nere agatenenia okoboko kwaye gwokorio, erio ere anyare komobua omobisa omonyanguru ase esegi na kobasegeta abanto baye.

English: So they glorified him for his tens of thousands, and praised him for the blessings of the Lord, in that a glorious diadem was given to him.
Ekegusii: Abanto bakamotogia ase ogoita ababisa ikomi na komochengera ase amasesenigwa y’Omonene ekero abekeretwe egobia y’oborwoti.

English: For he destroyed the enemies on every side, and defeated the Philistines his adversaries. He broke their horn in pieces to this day.
Ekegusii: Akabaabusera are ababisa baye korwa chinsinyo chionsi na kobakiria Abafilisiti; agachitagora chisiiro chiabo goika reero iga.

English: In every work of his he gave thanks to the Holy One Most High with words of glory. He sang praise with his whole heart, and loved him who made him.
Ekegusii: Ase kera ring’ana akorete, ere Daudi akaba okomotogia Omochenu Omonene. Akamwancha Omotongi oye na komoterera amatera yogotogia ase enkoro yaye yonsi.

English: He set singers before the altar, to make sweet melody by their music.
Ekegusii: Akababeka abateri ase obosio bw’egesasiimero, barabwo banyaare komoteerera amateera amaya goetera ase amariogi abo amaya.

English: He gave beauty to the feasts, and set in order the seasons to completion while they praised his holy name, and the sanctuary resounded from early morning.
Ekegusii: Akayakora amatuko amanene koba amaseera, na koyarobereria chingaki chiaye ase omwaka omogima, ekero abanto barenge gotogia erieta richenu ri’Omonene, erio Hekalu egaichorwa namatera amaya gochaakera emambia ekero bogokiamoka.

English: The Lord took away his sins, and exalted his horn forever. He gave him a covenant of kings, and a glorious throne in Israel.
Ekegusii: Omonene akamoruseria Daudi ebibe biaye, na gokinia okobua kwaye kare na kare; akamoa oboronge bw’okoba omorwoti, akabeka ekerogo kiaye kiobonene ime ya Israeli.

English: After him a wise son rose up, who because of him lived in security.
Ekegusii: Magega ya Daudi, omwana oye omong’aini akamenya nomorembe ase engencho yaye.

English: Solomon reigned in days of peace. God gave him rest all around, that he might set up a house for his name, and prepare a sanctuary forever.
Ekegusii: Solomoni akagaamba ase engaki yomorembe. Nyasae akamoa ebisio bi’omorembe korwa chinsinyo chionsi, erio ere aagache enyomba ase esiko yerieta riaye, na koarigania Hekalu ekomenya ase chingaki chitakoera.

English: How wise you were made in your youth, and filled as a river with understanding!
Ekegusii: Ekeene aye nigo kwarenge n’obong’aini aye Sulemani ekero kwarenge omosae! Nigo kwarenge goitororoka obong’aini buna orooche.

English: Your influence covered the earth, and you filled it with parables and riddles.
Ekegusii: Okamanyekana ase ense engima ase obomanyi bwao, ase emereng’anio nokogena.

English: Your name reached to the far away islands, and you were loved for your peace.
Ekegusii: Erieta riao rigakuma goika ase ebisinga bie chinse chi’aare, abanto bakagwancha ase okobarentera omorembe.

English: For your songs, proverbs, parables, and interpretations, the countries marveled at you.
Ekegusii: Ase amateera, emegwekano, emereng’anio na amorokererio aye, chinse chionsi chigatengechigwa na goichana.

English: By the name of the Lord God, who is called the God of Israel, you gathered gold like tin, and multiplied silver like lead.
Ekegusii: Ase esiko ye erieta ri’Omonene, oyio okorokwa Omonene Nyasae bw’Abaisraeli, ogasangereria chitaabu buna ebibanga n’echifeta buna ebioma bia Abaisraeli.

English: You bowed your loins to women, and in your body you were brought into subjection.
Ekegusii: Korende aye okoyorwa omobere oo ase abakungu, okaba omosomba bw’okogania kwao.

English: You blemished your honor, and defiled your offspring, to bring wrath upon your children. I was grieved for your folly,
Ekegusii: Okabeeka ekemoa ase esiko yao, na goturutumba eamate yao goika okabarentera egesusuro abaibore bao, bagaichanigwa ase engencho yoboriri bwao.

English: because the sovereignty was divided, and a disobedient kingdom ruled out of Ephraim.
Ekegusii: Goika oborwoti bogaatananekana ara kabere, oborwoti bw’okoamererania bogasoka korwa Efraimu.

English: But the Lord will never forsake his mercy. He won’t destroy any of his works, nor blot out the posterity of his elect. He won’t take away the offspring of him who loved him. He gave a remnant to Jacob, and to David a root from his own family.
Ekegusii: Korende Omonene tagotiga koba namaabera, gose gotiga emeremo yaye yonsi esareke; ere takobatugutera are abaibore ba Daudi, omochoore oye, gose gosiria egesaku kiaye ere oria anchete. Ase igo ere akamotigareria Yakobo ebitigari, naboigo Daudi omori bw’eamate yaye.

English: So Solomon rested with his fathers. Of his offspring, he left behind him Rehoboam, the foolishness of the people, and one who lacked understanding, who made the people revolt by his counsel. Also Jeroboam the son of Nebat, who made Israel to sin, and gave a way of sin to Ephraim.
Ekegusii: Solomoni agakwa buna omogaka oye, akamotiga oyomo ase abana baye koba omorai. Oyio nere Rehoboamu, oichire oboriri naende otarenge na bong’aini ere ase oborai bwaye akabakora abanto bagatananeka. Narengeo boigo Reoboamu mosinto o Nebati, oyio ogerete Abaisraeli bagakora ebibe, naboigo kobaraa Abaefraimu ase enchera y’ogokora ebibe.

English: Their sins were multiplied exceedingly, until they were removed from their land.
Ekegusii: Ebibe biabo bikamenta koba ebinge kegima goika bikagera barabwo bagaserigwa korwa ase ense yaabo.

English: For they sought out all manner of wickedness, until vengeance came upon them.
Ekegusii: Ekiagera barabwo bateemete gokora kera engencho yobobe goika Omonene akabaakania egesiomba.

English: Then Elijah arose, the prophet like fire. His word burned like a torch.
Ekegusii: Erio agacha omobani Elija ore gwoka buna omorero; oyio amang’ana aye arenge gwoka buna ebieri bi’omorero.

English: He brought a famine upon them, and by his zeal made them few in number.
Ekegusii: Akarentera abanto enchara, na ase engencho amwanchete Omonene, abange bagaakwa n’omobaro obo ogakea ekiagera ere nigo aamereranetie nabwo ng’a baonchorerie.

English: By the word of the Lord he shut up the heavens. He brought down fire three times.
Ekegusii: Ere agakwana ase erieta ria Nyasae erio amare agasiekwa embura tiyatwa, na nyuma yayio akareta omorero ara gatato.

English: How you were glorified, O Elijah, in your wondrous deeds! Whose glory is like yours?
Ekegusii: Aye Elija, nigo gwachiete nkuma ase amakora ao y’ogokumia! Monto tari naende ase ense eye oretogie buna aye?

English: You raised up a dead man from death, from Hades, by the word of the Most High.
Ekegusii: Aye kwabogetie egetondo; ase erieta ri’Omonene, okamobokia korwa ase abakuure.

English: You brought down kings to destruction, and honorable men from their sickbeds.
Ekegusii: Aye kwaiyeretie abagaambi korwa ase ebirogo biabo na kobasiria; abanto baria bachiete nkuma okobarutera endwari bakaruara.

English: You heard rebuke in Sinai, and judgments of vengeance in Horeb.
Ekegusii: Aye kwaigwerete ogotogonya kw’Omonene aaria ase egetunwa gia Sinai, n’okoraria gw’egesusuro ase ababisa baye aaria ase egetunwa kia Orebu.

English: You anointed kings for retribution, and prophets to succeed after you.
Ekegusii: Ogatunia omogambi amaguta ng’a ae abanto egesusuro, na ababani gokora emeremo ase riika riao.

English: You were taken up in a tempest of fire, in a chariot of fiery horses.
Ekegusii: Aye kwairetwe igoro ase ekembugu-mbugu ki’omorero, ime ase agari y’ebarasi y’omorero

English: You were recorded for reproofs in their seasons, to pacify anger, before it broke out into wrath, to turn the heart of the father to the son, and to restore the tribes of Jacob.
Ekegusii: Neriikire ase egatabu kia Omonene ng’a n’ooroke ase engaki egwenerete erio bwororobie endamwamu ya Nyasae etarateka n’obororo; egere orete ogonsonsorana gati y’abaibori amo n’abana babo, okabigorora ebisaku bionsi b’enyomba ya Yakobo.

English: Blessed are those who saw you, and those who have been beautified with love; for we also shall surely live.
Ekegusii: Mbasesenirie baria bare moyo goika barore kogocha batarakwa; ko bono aye nosesenirie kegima kobua ekiagera ’moyo ore.

English: Elijah was wrapped in a whirlwind. Elisha was filled with his spirit. In his days he was not moved by the fear of any ruler, and no one brought him into subjection.
Ekegusii: Ekero Elija asirete ime ase ekembugu-mbugu keria, Elisa agaichorwa n’echinguru chia Elija. Ase obogima bwaye bwonsi tachieti konyegerigwa bosio bw’abagaambi, gose monto onde naende tari ore n’echinguru gose ribaga gocha ase.

English: Nothing was too hard for him. When he was buried, his body prophesied.
Ekegusii: Tiriarengeo ing’ana rinde rionsi riamokong’erete ere, na ekero akwete, omobere oye okarua obobani.

English: As in his life he did wonders, so his works were also marvelous in death.
Ekegusii: Buna ere arenge gokora ebikone ekero ki’obomoyo bwaye, akagenderera kobikora boigo engaki ere akuure.
